path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”

exclusion: Activities that do not transfer a promised good or service to the customer
inclusion: Evaluations of various promised outputs including tasks, licenses, and future options
descriptor.definition: At contract inception, entities assess all promised goods or services to identify distinct performance obligations. Promises can encompass manufactured goods, retail merchandise, consulting tasks, standby availability, asset construction, intellectual property licenses, or future purchase options.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes distinct promises evaluated as separate performance obligations from integrated components of a single combined promise.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Netting off disposal group assets against liabilities
inclusion: Separate presentation of held for sale assets
Separate presentation of held for sale liabilities
descriptor.definition: Financial statements must display non-current assets and disposal groups held for sale in a manner that allows users to evaluate their financial effects. Assets and liabilities within a disposal group must be shown separately without netting them against each other.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on balance sheet arrangement and layout rules rather than measurement or note disclosure.

path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”

exclusion: Subsequent measurement rules governed by unrelated accounting standards
inclusion: Balance sheet classification of contract assets and liabilities
Separate presentation of excise duty in the statement of profit and loss
descriptor.definition: An entity presents contract balances in its balance sheet as a contract asset, contract liability, or receivable depending on whether goods or services have been transferred relative to customer payments. Unconditional rights to consideration are accounted for as receivables under Ind AS 109.
nearby_distinctions: Contract liabilities arise from advance payments or due dates prior to performance, whereas contract assets and receivables arise after performance occurs.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS

exclusion: Maintaining provisions after underlying settlement amounts are completely finalized
Omitting periodic updates to estimates
inclusion: Periodic reviews of provisions at reporting dates
Reversal of provisions when outflows cease to be probable
Accretion of discount recognized as borrowing or finance cost
descriptor.definition: Provisions must be reviewed at each reporting period and adjusted to reflect current best estimates, with balances reversed if an outflow is no longer probable. When obligation amounts crystallize without uncertainty or discounting passes time, balances are reclassified to liabilities or recognized as finance costs.
nearby_distinctions: Transitions provisions into standard liabilities once amounts and uncertainties are fully resolved and finalized.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: External reports like management commentary or value-added statements
inclusion: Opening balance sheet for retrospective accounting changes
Two-section statement of profit and loss and OCI
descriptor.definition: A comprehensive set requires a balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, changes in equity, cash flows, and explanatory notes with material policies. Equal prominence must be given to all statements, incorporating appropriate comparative periods.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates routine annual comparative data from retroactive opening balance sheet requirements.

path.name: Chapter 11: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
Unit 3: FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS: EQUITY AND FINANCIAL

exclusion: Equity conversion options meeting equity classification criteria
Stand-alone derivative contracts
inclusion: Issuer call options
Early redemption features in convertible instruments
descriptor.definition: Non-equity embedded derivative features, such as an issuer's call option contained within a compound financial instrument, are categorized and included as part of the liability component. The residual value after deducting the combined liability and derivative obligations is then allocated to the equity component.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity conversion options because non-equity derivatives like issuer call options are grouped with the liability component rather than assigned to equity.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
PRESENTATION AND DISCLOSURES OF A NON- CURRENT ASSET (OR DISPOSAL GROUP) CLASSIFIED AS HELD FOR SALE
Presentation and Disclosures of Non-Current Assets Held for Sale

exclusion: Offsetting assets against liabilities as a single net amount
Re-presentation of prior period comparative balance sheets
inclusion: Separate balance sheet presentation of assets and liabilities
Disclosure of major asset and liability classes
descriptor.definition: Non-current assets and disposal group assets and liabilities held for sale must be presented separately on the balance sheet without offsetting them against each other. Major classes of these assets and liabilities must be disclosed, and comparative balance sheet amounts for prior periods are not re-presented.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes current presentation requirements from prior period balance sheet comparative restatement rules.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)

exclusion: Presenting completely unstructured or unclassified raw data without regard to shared characteristics
Concealing critical information entirely through excessive data compression
inclusion: Combining items with shared characteristics within the same classification
Presenting summarized line items on primary financial statements such as the balance sheet and statement of profit and loss
descriptor.definition: Aggregation involves grouping assets, liabilities, equity, income, or expenses that share common characteristics within the same classification. This process enhances financial utility by condensing extensive details, while requiring a balance to prevent important facts from being obscured by excessive summarization or insignificant minutiae.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from detailed disclosure in notes, which provides granular information corresponding to the aggregated line items on primary statements.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
Shares and Weighted Average Calculation for Diluted EPS

exclusion: Antidilutive potential ordinary shares
Interim weighted averages aggregated for year-to-date periods
inclusion: Ordinary shares issuable upon conversion of dilutive potential instruments
Cancelled or lapsed potential shares weighted for their active period
descriptor.definition: The share base for diluted earnings per share combines the weighted average of actual ordinary shares with incremental shares issuable from potential ordinary shares using the if-converted method. Potential shares are weighted for the active period they exist and are evaluated independently for each period presented.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
nearby_distinctions: Unlike basic EPS which only tracks historical actual issuances, diluted EPS applies the if-converted assumption to prospective instruments.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Disclosures for joint venture and associate
Disclosures for joint venture and associate

exclusion: Subsidiary consolidation disclosures not governed by associate and joint venture rules
Unadjusted investee financial statement figures when equity adjustments are required
inclusion: Current and non-current assets and liabilities of material joint ventures and associates
Revenue, profit or loss, and comprehensive income components
Dividends received and equity method reconciliation items
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose material summarised financial information for each joint venture and associate, including assets, liabilities, revenue, and profit or loss elements. These figures must reconcile to the carrying amount of the investment after factoring in equity method adjustments or permitted alternative bases.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from general subsidiary disclosure requirements by focusing strictly on associates and joint ventures under the equity method or fair value exceptions.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 21 : THE EFFECTS OF CHANGES IN FOREIGN
Subsequent recognition at the end of each reporting period

exclusion: Initial transaction date recognition mechanics
Functional currency re-determinations
inclusion: Translation of carrying amounts determined by comparing two or more amounts
Comparison of historical cost at transaction date rate against net realizable value at closing rate
Impairment loss recognition arising from currency valuation differences
descriptor.definition: At each reporting date, foreign currency items are translated using closing rates for monetary elements, historical rates for cost-based non-monetary elements, and specific valuation dates for fair-value non-monetary elements. For items determined by comparing multiple values like lower of cost and net realizable value, each component is translated using the exchange rate appropriate to the date of its specific determination.
nearby_distinctions: Comparison-based items require dual-rate evaluations where historical elements use transaction date rates and net realizable values use closing rates.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Tax rates enacted after the reporting period end
inclusion: Tax rates expected to apply during realization or settlement
Rates reflecting expected manner of asset recovery or liability settlement
descriptor.definition: Deferred tax assets and liabilities must be measured using the tax rates and laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted by the end of the reporting period. These rates must reflect the expected manner of recovery or settlement of the asset or liability's carrying amount.
nearby_distinctions: Tax rates applied depend on whether an asset is recovered through use or sale if different statutory rates apply to each mode.

exclusion: Internal management forecasts not required by standards
inclusion: Outstanding option movements
Financial statement impacts on profit or loss and balance sheet
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose the general terms, scope, and types of share-based payment agreements existing during the reporting period. Required disclosures also cover share option movements, exercise price ranges, weighted average remaining lives, and valuation methodologies used.
nearby_distinctions: Pertains to explanatory reporting and note disclosures rather than primary recognition mechanics.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Leases containing a purchase option evaluated at commencement
inclusion: Leases with a term of 12 months or less without purchase options
Leases of low-value assets
descriptor.definition: Lessees can elect to exempt short-term leases and leases of low-value underlying assets from standard balance sheet recognition requirements. Such exempted lease payments are recognized as an expense on a straight-line or other systematic basis over the lease term.
nearby_distinctions: Short-term exemptions apply strictly based on terms determined at commencement rather than subsequent duration reductions

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Standard routine amortisation charges
inclusion: Annual reviews for indefinite-life assets
Event-driven impairment checks
descriptor.definition: Intangible asset impairment evaluation follows the framework outlined in Ind AS 36 to verify carrying amounts against recoverable amounts. Assets with indefinite useful lives must be evaluated for impairment at least on an annual basis.
nearby_distinctions: Impairment captures unexpected declines in service potential or value below carrying cost, distinct from scheduled periodic amortisation.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)

exclusion: Applying enhancing criteria to override fundamental defects
Rigid linear sequencing of qualitative applications
inclusion: Balancing comparability against enhanced relevance
Using disclosures to compensate for transitional non-comparability
descriptor.definition: Enhancing qualitative characteristics should be maximized iteratively, acknowledging that individual traits may occasionally be balanced against one another. For example, a temporary sacrifice in comparability may be accepted to secure long-term relevance via a new accounting standard.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the dynamic interplay and optimization of secondary traits rather than primary definitions.

path.name: Chapter 14: Ind AS 101 “First-time Adoption of Ind AS”

exclusion: Continuation of previous GAAP recognition rules without modification
Selective application of non-effective standards
inclusion: Preparation of opening balance sheet at transition date
Consistent application of accounting policies across presented periods
descriptor.definition: First-time adopters must prepare an opening balance sheet at the transition date using consistent accounting policies aligned with the latest effective standards. The core principle requires retrospective application as if Ind AS had always been utilized, subject strictly to mandatory exceptions and optional exemptions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes pure retrospective application from modified retrospective handling governed by specific exceptions and exemptions.

path.name: Chapter 11: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments

exclusion: Planned future transactions
Unperformed standard firm commitments unless designated as FVTPL
inclusion: Unconditional receivables and payables upon becoming a contract party
Forward contracts on commitment date
Option contracts when holder or writer becomes a party
descriptor.definition: An entity must recognize a financial asset or financial liability on its balance sheet exclusively when it becomes a party to the contractual provisions of the instrument. Specific rules dictate that unconditional receivables, forward contracts, and firm commitments are recognized depending on transaction dates, option premiums, and performance milestones.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from subsequent measurement and derecognition phases of financial instruments.

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 10: EVENTS AFTER THE REPORTING PERIOD
SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES BETWEEN IND AS 10 AND AS 4
Comparative Standards: Ind AS 10 Versus AS 4

exclusion: Identical framework provisions
Unrelated measurement standards
inclusion: Treatment differences for non-adjusting events
Divergent going concern impact rules
Loan breach waiver adjustments
Appendix coverage for non-cash distributions
descriptor.definition: Significant structural variations exist between reporting frameworks regarding material non-adjusting events, going concern implications, loan covenant breaches, and the distribution of non-cash assets. These divergences dictate differing disclosure locations and accounting treatment for events occurring after the balance sheet date.
nearby_distinctions: Ind AS 10 requires financial statement disclosure for material non-adjusting events whereas AS 4 mandates disclosure in the approving authority report.

path.name: Chapter 11: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments

exclusion: non-qualifying hedging relationships
unbalanced hedge weightings
inclusion: fair value hedge adjustments
cash flow hedge reserve accounting
unrecognised firm commitments
descriptor.definition: Qualifying fair value hedges adjust the carrying amount of the hedged item with corresponding profit or loss recognition, whereas cash flow hedges adjust a separate equity reserve. The specific accounting treatment depends on whether the exposure relates to fair value changes or cash flow variability.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by the nature of the risk being managed, dividing treatments between balance sheet fair value adjustments and equity-based cash flow reserves.

path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”
Customer options for additional goods or services
Customer Options for Additional Goods or Services

exclusion: Marketing offers priced at standard stand-alone selling prices without conferring a material right
inclusion: Customer award credits
Discounts exceeding normal market ranges creating a material right
descriptor.definition: Options granted to customers to acquire additional goods or services constitute a separate performance obligation only if they provide a material right that would not be received without entering into the contract. If the option merely offers a stand-alone market price, it is treated as a standard marketing offer rather than an advance payment for future goods.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard marketing offers by whether the discounted price provides a material right unavailable to non-contracted customers.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: carrying value adjustments via upward revaluations into profit or loss under the cost model
inclusion: cost-based carrying amounts adjusted for depreciation and impairment
descriptor.definition: Entities must adopt the cost model as their accounting policy for all investment properties subsequent to initial recognition. Fair value must still be measured and disclosed for informational purposes even when applying the cost model.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the mandatory cost model for balance sheet recognition with the mandatory fair value disclosure requirement.

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 10: EVENTS AFTER THE REPORTING PERIOD

exclusion: Subsequent shareholder adoption or regulatory filings
inclusion: Board of Directors approval for companies
Corresponding authorized management body approval for other entities
descriptor.definition: The process of financial statement authorization varies according to management structure, statutory rules, and finalization workflows. For companies, approval occurs when the Board of Directors signs off, whereas other entities rely on their corresponding governing management body.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes executive board authorization from downstream shareholder adoption.

path.name: Chapter 1: Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards
How Ind AS have been structured?

exclusion: Unstructured narrative accounting guidelines
Standards lacking comparative compliance appendices
inclusion: Standard objective and scope parameters
Recognition, measurement, and subsequent valuation principles
Qualitative and quantitative disclosure mandates
descriptor.definition: Indian Accounting Standards replicate the structure of international standards, preserving original paragraph numbering while noting any local carve-outs in comparative appendices. Each standard typically comprises explicit sections for objectives, scope, definitions, core recognition and measurement principles, and disclosure requirements.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by a standardized modular layout that preserves international paragraph alignments for cross-reference ease.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES
Disclosure 4: Explanation of the relationship between tax expense (income) and accounting profit
Disclosure 4: Explanation of the relationship between tax expense (income) and accounting profit

exclusion: Standard balance sheet tax asset and liability schedules
inclusion: Numerical reconciliation of tax expense against accounting profit product
Numerical reconciliation of average effective tax rate against applicable tax rate
descriptor.definition: Entities must provide a numerical reconciliation explaining the variance between accounting profit multiplied by applicable rates and actual tax expense. This explanation can use either monetary tax amounts or effective tax rate percentages.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from component breakdowns by offering a conceptual bridge between pre-tax accounting profits and final tax expense calculations.

path.name: Chapter 11: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
Unit 3: FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS: EQUITY AND FINANCIAL
Rights issues, options or warrants to acquire entity’s own equity instruments for any currency
Rights Issues, Options Or Warrants To Acquire Entity’S Own Equity Instruments For Any Currency

exclusion: Non-pro-rata third-party warrants
Variable-share foreign currency options
inclusion: Pro rata rights issues in foreign currency
Fixed-share foreign currency convertible bond options
descriptor.definition: Rights, options, or warrants offering a fixed number of own equity instruments for a fixed amount in any currency are classified as equity if offered pro rata to existing owners. Ind AS 32 provides a carve-out permitting equity classification for foreign currency convertible bond conversion options.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from IFRS rules which treat foreign currency equity conversion options as derivative liabilities causing profit and loss volatility.

exclusion: Application of the pooling-of-interests method for transactions within the scope of Ind AS 103
inclusion: Identification of the acquiring enterprise based on control principles
Measurement of identifiable net assets and non-controlling interests at fair value
descriptor.definition: Accounting for business combinations requires following a structured four-step acquisition method to identify the acquirer, establish the acquisition date, and measure identifiable assets, liabilities, and non-controlling interests. Any excess of consideration over net assets is recognized as goodwill or a bargain purchase gain.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard consolidation procedures by focusing specifically on the purchase price allocation and goodwill determination at the acquisition date

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: initial recognition of unrecognized intangible assets via revaluation
selective revaluation of isolated assets without revaluing their entire class
inclusion: carrying amount adjustments for amortization and impairment
fair value revaluations referenced to an active market
descriptor.definition: Entities must choose either the cost model or the revaluation model as an accounting policy for subsequent measurement of intangible assets. Under the cost model, assets are carried at cost less accumulated amortization and impairment, whereas the revaluation model uses fair value based on active markets.
nearby_distinctions: Cost model carrying value tracking versus active market revaluation model

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 10: EVENTS AFTER THE REPORTING PERIOD

exclusion: Common control transactions
Shareholder-side accounting procedures
inclusion: Equally treated non-cash asset distributions to equity owners
Distributions offering cash or non-cash options
descriptor.definition: The standard appendix governs non-reciprocal non-cash distributions and cash-alternative choices provided equally to all members of a specific equity class. It expressly excludes common-control transactions, retained-control subsidiary distributions, and recipient-side accounting treatments.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general standard scope by isolating entity-level non-cash distribution accounting and excluding recipient-level ledger entries.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

exclusion: Unreconciled segment figures or missing prior period restatements
inclusion: General organizational factors and aggregation judgments
Reconciliations of segment revenues, assets, and liabilities to entity totals
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose general information, performance measures, assets, liabilities, and measurement bases for each period presenting profit or loss statements. Comprehensive reconciliations linking segment totals back to corresponding entity-wide financial statement amounts must also be provided.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes core segment performance metrics from mandatory reconciliations required to tie internal reports to official financial statements.

exclusion: rights offered to all equity holders proportionally
fixed cash grants independent of share price fluctuations
inclusion: stock options granted to employees
bonuses linked strictly to entity share prices
descriptor.definition: Ind AS 102 applies to equity-settled, cash-settled, and alternative settlement share-based payments, including arrangements involving unidentified goods or services. Transactions with shareholders acting solely in their ownership capacity are strictly excluded from its scope.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes employee services compensated via share value from general equity distributions to shareholders.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Preparation of consolidated financial statements after applying above principles
Preparation of consolidated financial statements after applying above principles

exclusion: Unadjusted separate financial statements without elimination
inclusion: Combination of parent and subsidiary balance sheet, profit and loss, and cash flow items
Elimination of intra-group balances and transactions
descriptor.definition: The preparation of consolidated financial statements involves combining line-by-line assets, liabilities, income, expenses, and cash flows of parents and subsidiaries while eliminating intra-group transactions. It also recognizes non-controlling interests, goodwill or capital reserves, and the parent's share of post-acquisition profits.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from individual financial statements by incorporating group-wide entity aggregations and eliminations rather than single-entity reporting.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

exclusion: Simple unweighted closing share balances
inclusion: Opening ordinary shares
Time-weighted adjustments for share issuances
Time-weighted deductions for share buybacks
descriptor.definition: The weighted average number of ordinary shares reflects the shares outstanding at the beginning of a period adjusted by shares issued or bought back, multiplied by a time-weighting factor. This factor proportions the duration days the shares remain outstanding against total days in the period.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
nearby_distinctions: Replaces simple period-end share counts with a time-apportioned average reflecting capital changes during the period.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Recognized dividend liability tax provisions
inclusion: Income tax consequences of dividends proposed after reporting date but before approval
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose the income tax consequences of dividends proposed or declared after the reporting date but prior to financial statement approval. Such dividend tax impacts are omitted from balance sheet liabilities but require explicit disclosure.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from recognized liabilities by targeting post-reporting date unrecognised corporate distributions.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Exempted short-term leases
Low-value asset leases
inclusion: Initial lease liability present value calculation
Right-of-use asset recognition
descriptor.definition: Lessee accounting mandates that entities acquiring a right to use an asset recognize a right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability at the commencement date. All qualifying leases are brought onto the balance sheet unless specific short-term or low-value exemptions apply.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with historical off-balance-sheet operating lease treatment by mandating universal asset and liability capitalization

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Unresolved negotiating period estimates prior to finalization
inclusion: Lease term reassessments
Index-linked payment updates
descriptor.definition: Lessees update lease liabilities and corresponding right-of-use assets following changes in lease terms, expected residual guarantees, or index-linked payments. Revised discount rates are applied for term or purchase option reassessments, while original rates are retained for index or residual updates.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from lease modifications by adjusting existing parameters due to reassessments or triggers rather than executing contractual structural changes

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
Diluted Earnings Per Share Scope and Objective

exclusion: Antidilutive potential ordinary shares
Basic earnings per share computations without potential share adjustments
inclusion: Profit or loss from continuing operations attributable to ordinary equity holders
After-tax amount of dividends and interest on dilutive potential ordinary shares
Weighted average of additional ordinary shares from assumed conversions
descriptor.definition: Diluted earnings per share measures an entity's performance interest per ordinary share by adjusting profit or loss and the weighted average shares for the effects of all dilutive potential ordinary shares. Numerators are adjusted for after-tax dividends and interest on potential shares, while denominators include incremental shares assumed converted.
terminology: Weighted average number of ordinary shares
Profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders
nearby_distinctions: Basic earnings per share reflects only currently issued ordinary shares without factoring in potential future conversions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Accounting for sales or contributions of assets to a joint operation in separate and consolidated financial statement of joint operator
Accounting for sales or contributions of assets to a joint operation in separate and consolidated financial statement of joint operator

exclusion: Full immediate recognition of internal transaction profits or losses
inclusion: Partial gain or loss recognition based on external ownership percentages
Full recognition of impairment or net realizable value reductions
descriptor.definition: When a joint operator sells or contributes assets to a joint operation, resulting gains and losses are recognized only to the extent of other parties' interests. Unrealized portions corresponding to the transferring operator's interest are deferred against the carrying amount of the asset.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from transactions with external third parties by restricting profit or loss recognition to the extent of external joint operators' stakes.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Values computed purely under income tax depreciation schedules
inclusion: Balance sheet values adjusted for accounting depreciation
Balance sheet values adjusted for asset impairment
descriptor.definition: The carrying amount represents the balance sheet value at which an asset or liability is recognized after accounting for subsequent adjustments such as depreciation and impairment. It reflects the ledger balance determined under applicable accounting standards rather than tax rules.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes book values from tax base values utilized in temporary difference calculations.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES IN IND AS 23 VIS-À-VIS AS 16
Significant Differences In Ind As 23 Vis-À-Vis As 16

exclusion: Legacy AS 16 treatment provisions that conflict with current Ind AS frameworks
inclusion: Scope exclusions for fair-value measured qualifying assets
Effective interest rate method calculations for borrowing costs
Inclusion of lease liabilities
descriptor.definition: Significant structural variations exist between modern accounting standards and older frameworks regarding scope exclusions, measurement methods, and lease treatment. These differences affect how borrowing costs are calculated, scoped, and adjusted for foreign exchange variations.
terminology: Qualifying asset measured at fair value
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by comparing contemporary Ind AS requirements directly against legacy AS guidelines to highlight operational framework divergences.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
Unit 5: THE ELEMENTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
LINK BETWEEN INFORMATION IN GENERAL PURPOSE FINANCIAL REPORTS AS PER CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK AND ELEMENTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
Link Between Information In General Purpose Financial Reports As Per Conceptual Framework And Elements Of Financial Statements

exclusion: Equity contributions and distributions categorized as financial performance elements
inclusion: Mapping of economic resources to assets and claims to liabilities
Mapping of financial changes to income and expense elements
descriptor.definition: General purpose financial reports reflect underlying economic resources and claims through specific balance sheet elements like assets, liabilities, and equity. Changes in these resources and claims over time are captured via financial performance elements such as income and expenses.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes static structural elements (assets, liabilities, equity) from dynamic performance elements (income, expenses).

path.name: Financial Statements of Corporate Entities under Schedule III

exclusion: Horizontal balance sheet formats
Prescription of specific accounting measurement treatments
inclusion: Vertical balance sheet formatting
Minimum face-value disclosures and note disclosures
descriptor.definition: Corporate financial statements must follow the vertical format and minimum disclosure requirements set out in Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013. Schedule III prescribes content and presentation rules but does not dictate underlying accounting treatments, which are governed by notified standards.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard-setting rules because Schedule III governs presentation formats rather than the accounting recognition and measurement principles.
instrument_references: Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
Presentation in the statement of profit and loss
Presentation in the Statement of Profit and Loss

exclusion: Detailed line-item breakdown for newly acquired subsidiaries meeting held-for-sale criteria on acquisition
inclusion: Single line item for discontinued operations results
Detailed revenue and expense breakdown
Attributable income disclosures for parent owners
descriptor.definition: The statement of profit and loss must feature a single composite amount representing post-tax results of discontinued operations combined with post-tax disposal or fair value remeasurement gains. An accompanying breakdown of revenues, expenses, pre-tax results, and related income taxes must be provided either on the face or in the notes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between the aggregate single-line disclosure on the income statement face and the detailed supporting analysis.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
INFORMATION PROVIDED BY PARTICULAR MEASUREMENT BASES
Information Provided By Particular Measurement Bases

exclusion: Non-financial operational performance metrics
inclusion: Balance sheet carrying amounts across bases
Statement of profit and loss event treatments
descriptor.definition: Selecting a measurement basis requires evaluating the specific nature of the financial information it produces for both the balance sheet and the statement of profit and loss. Different bases handle transaction costs, interest income, and value changes through distinct recognition and expense mechanisms.
nearby_distinctions: Compares balance sheet presentation and income statement volatility generated by historical cost versus current value alternatives.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Netting off disposal group assets against liabilities
inclusion: Separate presentation of held for sale assets
Separate presentation of held for sale liabilities
descriptor.definition: Financial statements must display non-current assets and disposal groups held for sale in a manner that allows users to evaluate their financial effects. Assets and liabilities within a disposal group must be shown separately without netting them against each other.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses specifically on balance sheet arrangement and layout rules rather than measurement or note disclosure.

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies

exclusion: Forced or distressed market actors
inclusion: Independent entities transacting without external pressure
Participants possessing sufficient market knowledge
descriptor.definition: Market participants are buyers and sellers in the principal or most advantageous market who are independent, unforced, and adequately informed. Pricing models must incorporate the economic assumptions these participants would use.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates general market entities from specific internal management perspectives that lack broad market consensus.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

exclusion: Separate dual lines when no potential ordinary shares exist and basic equals diluted EPS
inclusion: Basic and diluted amounts for profit or loss from continuing operations
Per share figures for discontinued operations in notes or financial statements
descriptor.definition: Entities must present basic and diluted earnings per share with equal prominence within the statement of profit and loss for every presented period. Negative earnings amounts representing losses per share must be explicitly disclosed alongside distinct figures for continuing and discontinued operations.
nearby_distinctions: Discontinued operations require separate per-share disclosure, distinguishing them from continuing operations performance metrics.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Disclosure requirements in other Ind AS
Disclosure Requirements In Other Ind As

exclusion: Direct standard-specific disclosures covered entirely within Ind AS 19
inclusion: Related party transactions with post-employment benefit plans
Contingent liabilities from post-employment benefit obligations
descriptor.definition: Entities must provide disclosures concerning post-employment benefit plans and key management personnel under separate accounting standards. Additionally, disclosures regarding contingent liabilities arising from employee benefit obligations are required.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard-internal disclosures by relying strictly on external standard mandates like Ind AS 24 and Ind AS 37.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Compares the efficiency of different entities
Compares the efficiency of different entities

exclusion: disparate entity-specific profit recognition rules
inclusion: cross-entity comparison
standardized cash metric computation
descriptor.definition: While accounting profits vary due to subjective policies, cash flows apply a standardized measurement technique. This common denominator allows stakeholders to objectively compare operating efficiency across entirely different companies.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from net income comparisons, which can be distorted by differing accounting policies and definitions.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)

exclusion: grouping dissimilar items together
offsetting assets and liabilities
inclusion: sorting assets and liabilities
sorting income and expenses by shared traits
descriptor.definition: Classification categorizes financial statement elements based on shared characteristics such as nature, business function, or measurement basis. Grouping dissimilar items obscures relevant information and reduces understandability.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from aggregation, which combines items already sharing the same classification.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS

exclusion: Financial instruments under Ind AS 109
Income taxes under Ind AS 12
inclusion: Provisions
Contingent liabilities
Contingent assets
descriptor.definition: The standard ensures appropriate recognition criteria and measurement bases are applied to provisions, contingent liabilities, and contingent assets. It also requires sufficient note disclosures regarding their nature, timing, and amount.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between recognized provisions and unrecognised contingent items based on probability and measurement reliability.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS

exclusion: Contractual fees for services rendered
Fines for legal violations
inclusion: Statutory charges imposed by national or local governments
descriptor.definition: A levy represents a governmental charge imposed on entities via laws or regulations that results in economic resource outflows. Government entities comprise local, national, or international agencies.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes compulsory legislative levies from bilateral contracts and regulatory penalties.

path.name: Chapter 11: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
Unit 3: FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS: EQUITY AND FINANCIAL

exclusion: Fair value changes of an entity's own equity instruments
Abandoned equity transaction costs recognized as expense
inclusion: Interest and dividends on financial liabilities
Distributions to equity holders
Incremental transaction costs of equity and compound transactions
descriptor.definition: The classification of a financial instrument dictates whether related returns and value changes flow through profit or loss or directly into equity. Specifically, liabilities generate expenses or income in profit or loss, whereas equity distributions are recognized directly in equity.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by instrument classification, routing liability-related returns through profit or loss while recording equity distributions directly through equity reserves.

path.name: Chapter 16: Professional and Ethical Duty of a Chartered Accountant

exclusion: Detailed assurance engagement independence rules
inclusion: Moral principles
Conduct standards
descriptor.definition: Ethics represents moral principles, conduct systems, and duties governing individual behavior or specific disciplines. The ICAI Code of Ethics establishes behavioral standards for chartered accountants to serve the public interest.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from specific statutory schedules by focusing on foundational behavioral principles rather than penal clauses.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
To assess the ability to generate cash and cash equivalents
To assess the ability to generate cash and cash equivalents

exclusion: non-cash profitability figures
inclusion: creditor payment analysis
profitability versus cash flow correlation
descriptor.definition: This objective evaluates a company's operational efficiency in producing liquid assets to cover debts and creditor payments. It examines the relationship between reported accounting profits and actual net cash inflows.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from profit and loss assessments by measuring actual liquidity rather than theoretical earnings.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Disconnecting tax accounting from the classification of the underlying economic event
inclusion: Tax effects recognized in profit or loss, OCI, or equity
Pro rata allocation for complex items recognized outside profit or loss
descriptor.definition: The accounting treatment for deferred tax effects must align with the underlying transaction or event, being recognized in profit or loss, other comprehensive income, or directly in equity. Subsequent changes in deferred tax balances driven by tax rate changes are also routed through profit or loss unless tied to prior non-P&L items.
nearby_distinctions: Items originating in equity or OCI mandate that their corresponding deferred tax adjustments bypass the statement of profit and loss.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS

exclusion: Utility accruals with known timing
Uninvoiced goods under agreed trade terms
Financial guarantees under Ind AS 109
inclusion: Warranty obligations
Liabilities with uncertain settlement timing or amount
descriptor.definition: Provisions differ from trade payables and accruals due to a significantly higher degree of uncertainty regarding timing or amount. Trade payables and accruals represent invoiced or agreed liabilities for received goods and services with minimal estimation variance.
nearby_distinctions: Accruals involve minor estimation variance for known invoiced or received services, whereas provisions involve substantial uncertainty over timing and amount.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS
Levies Under Appendix C of Ind AS 37

exclusion: Costs arising from recognizing a levy liability
Fines or penalties for legal breaches
Contractual payments for asset acquisition or services
Emissions trading scheme liabilities
inclusion: Accounting for levy liabilities within standard scope
Identified obligating events triggering levy payments
descriptor.definition: Appendix C establishes principles for recognizing liabilities to pay government-imposed levies whose timing and amount are certain under Ind AS 37 scope. It excludes other specific outflows like fines, penalties, and contractual payments.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes government levies from contractual payments, penalties for legal breaches, and emissions trading scheme liabilities.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
EXTRACTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS OF LISTED ENTITIES
Extracts Of Financial Statements Of Listed Entities

exclusion: Normative calculation rules or theoretical definitions
inclusion: Real-world corporate presentation examples from major listed companies
descriptor.definition: Published financial disclosures from listed commercial entities illustrate practical reporting conventions for earnings per share metrics. These extracts demonstrate the application of disclosure standards across corporate annual reporting frameworks.
source_ambiguities: The source text consists purely of corporate headings and source citations without substantive rules or definitions.
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an illustrative reporting exhibit rather than setting standard-derived computation mandates.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Equity instruments governed strictly under share-based payment standards
inclusion: Full-time and part-time employee provisions
Permanent, casual, and temporary worker benefits
Payments to third-party insurers
descriptor.definition: Employee benefits include all forms of consideration given by an entity in exchange for services rendered or for the termination of employment. These provisions extend to payments made directly to employees, their dependents, beneficiaries, or external third parties such as insurance companies.
nearby_distinctions: Encompasses direct remuneration as well as indirect provisions channeled to family members or insurance providers.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: Tailored custom reports for individual users
inclusion: Historical financial statement comparisons
Cross-entity financial comparisons
descriptor.definition: The objective establishes a standardized basis for presenting general-purpose financial statements to facilitate comparability with an entity's historical reports and those of external entities. It mandates comprehensive structural rules and baseline content specifications.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from recognition criteria by focusing exclusively on presentation formatting and comparability.

path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”

exclusion: Arrangements where the private entity acts merely as an agent without management responsibilities
inclusion: Private sector management of public infrastructure such as roads, hospitals, and utilities
Contracts containing specified pricing and arbitration terms
descriptor.definition: Service concession arrangements require an operator to construct, upgrade, operate, and maintain public infrastructure for a set duration while being paid for services through contractual mechanisms. The public sector grantor sets performance standards, pricing adjustment rules, and dispute resolution processes.
nearby_distinctions: The operator takes responsibility for management and operations rather than simply acting as an ordinary commercial agent.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Classification of Cash Flows as Investing Activity
Classification of Cash Flows as Investing Activity

exclusion: Financing transactions involving partial equity changes without loss of control
Standard operating cycle cash flows
inclusion: Total consideration paid or received for control changes
Cash and cash equivalents acquired or disposed of in business changes
descriptor.definition: Aggregate cash flows arising from acquiring or relinquishing control of subsidiaries or other businesses are classified strictly as investing activities and presented separately. The net cash consideration paid or received is reported net of cash and cash equivalents acquired or disposed of in the transaction.
nearby_distinctions: Separates major structural entity acquisition or disposal cash flows from routine operational or financing cash movements.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS

exclusion: Future commitments unconnected to past obligating events
inclusion: Obligations from explicit or implicit contract terms
Obligations from past practice and published policies
descriptor.definition: A provision is a liability of uncertain timing or amount arising from a present obligation due to past events. Legal obligations stem from contracts, legislation, or operation of law, whereas constructive obligations arise from an entity's established practices and created expectations.
nearby_distinctions: Legal obligations derive strictly from binding laws or terms, whereas constructive obligations derive from created valid expectations via past actions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities
Preparation of consolidated financial statements after applying above principles
Preparation of consolidated financial statements after applying above principles

exclusion: Unadjusted separate financial statements without elimination
inclusion: Combination of parent and subsidiary balance sheet, profit and loss, and cash flow items
Elimination of intra-group balances and transactions
descriptor.definition: The preparation of consolidated financial statements involves combining line-by-line assets, liabilities, income, expenses, and cash flows of parents and subsidiaries while eliminating intra-group transactions. It also recognizes non-controlling interests, goodwill or capital reserves, and the parent's share of post-acquisition profits.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from individual financial statements by incorporating group-wide entity aggregations and eliminations rather than single-entity reporting.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)

exclusion: treating a single set of rights and obligations as one unit of account
inclusion: combining separate asset and liability units into a single net figure
descriptor.definition: Offsetting combines separately recognized assets and liabilities into a single net balance sheet amount. Because this practice groups dissimilar items, it is generally inappropriate unless specifically permitted.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from treating a single contractual set of rights and obligations as a single unit of account.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Actual or imputed cost of equity
Preferred capital not classified as a liability
inclusion: Directly attributable borrowing costs for qualifying assets
descriptor.definition: Borrowing costs that are directly attributable to the acquisition, construction, or production of a qualifying asset must be capitalized as part of that asset's cost. All other borrowing costs are recognized as expenses in the period in which they are incurred.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between mandatory capitalization for qualifying asset acquisition and expensing of general operational borrowing costs.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)

exclusion: Presenting completely unstructured or unclassified raw data without regard to shared characteristics
Concealing critical information entirely through excessive data compression
inclusion: Combining items with shared characteristics within the same classification
Presenting summarized line items on primary financial statements such as the balance sheet and statement of profit and loss
descriptor.definition: Aggregation involves grouping assets, liabilities, equity, income, or expenses that share common characteristics within the same classification. This process enhances financial utility by condensing extensive details, while requiring a balance to prevent important facts from being obscured by excessive summarization or insignificant minutiae.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from detailed disclosure in notes, which provides granular information corresponding to the aggregated line items on primary statements.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Periods for which interim financial statements are required to be presented
Periods for which Interim Financial Statements are Required

exclusion: Full annual comparative financial statements for income statement items outside comparative interim periods
inclusion: Balance sheet as of current interim period-end and prior year-end
Profit and loss for current and cumulative year-to-date periods with comparatives
Changes in equity and cash flows on a cumulative year-to-date basis with comparatives
descriptor.definition: Interim reports require a balance sheet as of the current interim period-end with a comparative balance sheet from the prior financial year-end. Statements of profit and loss, changes in equity, and cash flows must cover the current interim period and cumulative year-to-date periods alongside comparable prior-year periods.
nearby_distinctions: Mandates specific comparative timeframes tailored to interim and year-to-date reporting horizons.

path.name: Chapter 1: Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards
PROCESS OF DEVELOPMENT AND FINALISATION OF INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARDS
Process of Development and Finalisation of Indian Accounting Standards

exclusion: Direct unilateral adoption without regulatory consultation
Non-statutory guideline formulation without governmental notification
inclusion: Preparation of preliminary drafts with carve-ins and carve-outs
Stakeholder consultations and public comment exposure drafts
NFRA review and MCA statutory notification
descriptor.definition: Indian Accounting Standards are formulated by the ICAI's Accounting Standards Board through public comment exposure drafts and extensive inter-regulatory consultations. Following council approval and National Financial Reporting Authority review, the Central Government officially notifies these standards under the Companies Act.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from informal rule-making by following a structured multi-party consultative and statutory notification workflow.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
To understand the timing and certainty of their generation
To understand the timing and certainty of their generation

exclusion: random, non-recurring accounting accruals
inclusion: trend identification in cash generation
probability assessment
descriptor.definition: Historical cash flow analysis establishes recurring trends regarding the periods in which a company successfully generates cash. This evaluation helps stakeholders gauge the statistical probability of future cash generation.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from static liquidity measures by emphasizing temporal patterns and predictability of cash inflows.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
Objective of Non-Current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations

exclusion: Continuing operations assets and liabilities
inclusion: Non-current assets held for sale
Disposal groups
Discontinued operations results
descriptor.definition: The standard specifies the accounting, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements for non-current assets held for sale and discontinued operations. This segregation helps users evaluate an entity's future cash flows, earnings capacity, and financial position by separating them from continuing operations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between ongoing operational activities and assets whose value is recovered principally through a sale transaction.

path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”

exclusion: Procedural guidance for step execution
inclusion: Standardized accounting definitions for revenue recognition mechanics
descriptor.definition: This section sets out foundational terminology used throughout the revenue standard, including contracts, contract assets, contract liabilities, and performance obligations. These terms provide the technical definitions required to execute the five-step revenue recognition model.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between contract assets conditioned on factors other than the passage of time versus unconditional rights to consideration.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS
RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PROVISIONS AND CONTINGENT LIABILITIES
Relationship Between Provisions and Contingent Liabilities

exclusion: Remote possibilities requiring no disclosure
inclusion: Recognized provisions where outflow is probable
Contingent liabilities for possible obligations
descriptor.definition: Provisions are recognized liabilities because an outflow is probable and measurable, whereas contingent liabilities remain unrecgonized due to being possible obligations or failing probability and measurement criteria.
nearby_distinctions: Provisions meet the probability and reliability criteria for immediate recognition, while contingent liabilities fail either probability or measurement thresholds.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Face of balance sheet line-item values
Cash flow statement line items
inclusion: Descriptions of non-current assets or disposal groups
Circumstances and timing of expected disposal
Segment reporting classifications
descriptor.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive notes detailing the description, facts, circumstances, and expected timing of disposal for assets or disposal groups classified as held for sale. Additional required disclosures include recognized gains or losses, operating segment information, and the operational impacts of any cancelled sale plans.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from balance sheet presentation by requiring qualitative descriptive narratives and supplementary details within the notes.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
Information about profit or loss, assets and liabilities
Information about profit or loss, assets and liabilities

exclusion: Items never reviewed by the CODM and excluded from internal reporting measures
inclusion: Revenues from external customers and intersegment transactions
Additions to non-current assets excluding financial instruments and tax assets
descriptor.definition: Entities must report measures of profit or loss, total assets, and total liabilities for each reportable segment if regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker. Specific supplementary financial items like interest, depreciation, and equity-accounted investments must also be disclosed when included in metrics reviewed by the CODM.
nearby_distinctions: Ties mandatory reporting items directly to the internal data package reviewed by the CODM rather than imposing universal line-item checklists.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Agreements lacking an identified asset or failing to grant asset use direction rights
inclusion: Contracts granting rights to use explicitly or implicitly specified assets with economic benefit control
descriptor.definition: A contract is or contains a lease if it conveys the right to control the use of an identified asset for a period of time in exchange for consideration. This assessment is performed at the inception date, defined as the earlier of the lease agreement date or the date of commitment to principal terms.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes pure service contracts from lease arrangements based on control over the underlying asset use

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
Unit 4: FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND THE REPORTING
OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
Objective And Scope Of Financial Statements

exclusion: Detailed explanatory material regarding management expectations and strategies not tied to reported measures
inclusion: Information about assets, liabilities, and equity in the balance sheet
Information about income and expenses in the statement of profit and loss
Disclosures on risks, cash flows, and estimation methods in notes
descriptor.definition: The primary objective of financial statements is to supply financial information regarding an entity's assets, liabilities, equity, income, and expenses that assists users in evaluating future net cash inflows and management's stewardship. This financial information is communicated through the balance sheet, the statement of profit and loss, and accompanying notes disclosing recognised and unrecognised items, cash flows, equity contributions, and estimation judgments.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general purpose financial reports which encompass broader commentaries beyond the financial statements themselves.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: External reports like management commentary or value-added statements
inclusion: Opening balance sheet for retrospective accounting changes
Two-section statement of profit and loss and OCI
descriptor.definition: A comprehensive set requires a balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, changes in equity, cash flows, and explanatory notes with material policies. Equal prominence must be given to all statements, incorporating appropriate comparative periods.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates routine annual comparative data from retroactive opening balance sheet requirements.

path.name: PRESENTATION OF GRANTS RELATED TO ASSETS
Presentation Of Grants Related To Assets

exclusion: Grants related strictly to income without asset acquisition
inclusion: Setting up grants as deferred income
Deducting grants from asset cost
descriptor.definition: Government grants related to assets are presented in the balance sheet either by setting up the grant as deferred income or by deducting the grant from the asset carrying amount. Deferred income is recognized in profit or loss systematically over the useful life of the asset.
nearby_distinctions: Grants related to assets focus on capital property acquisition, whereas grants related to income defray periodic operational expenses.
