path.name: Chapter 1: Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards

exclusion: Entities exempted under specific statutory sector rules
Non-corporate business entities
inclusion: Mandatory Ind AS compliant companies
Voluntary Ind AS compliant companies
descriptor.definition: Schedule III presentation rules apply to all companies preparing financial statements in compliance with corporate accounting rules, supported by specialized guidance notes and regulatory circulars. Preparers must incorporate amendments introduced to presentation requirements for financial years commencing on or after specified dates.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from initial standard-setting notifications by establishing the ongoing annual presentation framework for active financial reporting.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: Omission of material information due to rounding
inclusion: Prominent display of reporting entity identity
Uniform rounding units
descriptor.definition: Financial statements must clearly isolate mandatory disclosures across specific primary statements and notes while adhering to regulatory rounding and currency identification rules. Entities apply systematic ordering to ensure published documents are clearly distinguished and understandable.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from recognition criteria by governing the visual display, layout, and numerical scaling of data.
instrument_references: Schedule III of the Companies Act 2013

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 8 : ACCOUNTING POLICIES, CHANGES IN ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES AND ERRORS
Introduction to Accounting Policies, Estimates and Errors

exclusion: rectification of inappropriate policies solely via notes
unsupported tax effect calculations
inclusion: disclosure of significant accounting policies
presentation requirements for retrospective policy application
descriptor.definition: Ind AS 1 establishes the foundational rules for financial statement presentation and requires clear disclosures of significant accounting policies alongside primary statements. Changes in accounting policies must be handled systematically rather than through notes alone, and retrospective changes with material effects necessitate a third balance sheet.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from detailed measurement criteria found subsequently in Ind AS 8 by focusing broadly on financial presentation foundations.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
Acquisition as part of a business combination
Acquisition as Part of a Business Combination

exclusion: goodwill components not meeting identifiable asset criteria
inclusion: identifiable intangible assets arising from contractual or legal rights
in-process research and development projects meeting asset definitions
descriptor.definition: Intangible assets acquired in a business combination are measured at fair value at the acquisition date, which incorporates market expectations of future economic benefits. The acquirer recognizes these identifiable assets separately from goodwill even if the acquiree had not previously recognized them.
nearby_distinctions: Business combination fair value recognition versus separate acquisition historical cost

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Significant Events and Transactions in Interim Reporting

exclusion: Relatively insignificant updates already covered in recent annual notes
inclusion: Inventory write-downs and reversals
Impairment losses and reversals
Litigation settlements and prior period error corrections
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose significant events and transactions that alter understanding of financial position and performance since the last annual reporting period. Required disclosures update prior annual information regarding inventory write-downs, impairments, restructuring reversals, asset acquisitions, litigation settlements, and prior period error corrections.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on major impactful occurrences during the interim period rather than routine operational updates.

path.name: BEST PRACTICES - APPLICABLE TO ALL COMPANIES
Best Practices for Presentation and Disclosure

exclusion: Use of vague conditional remarks regarding account balance reconciliations
inclusion: Drafting notes in clear and plain language
Ensuring complete disclosures without vague or ambiguous statements
descriptor.definition: Preparers should ensure financial statements are complete, compliant, and drafted in simple, plain English to avoid ambiguity or cross-questioning. Clear and specific accounting policies enhance effective communication regarding the entity's financial position and performance.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from mandatory minimum legal formats by focusing on stylistic clarity and communicative effectiveness.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Standard financial statement line items duplicated without explanatory notes
inclusion: Explanation of leasing activity nature
Risk management practices on retained asset rights
Quantitative breakdowns of finance income and selling profits
descriptor.definition: Lessor disclosure requirements provide users with insights into the amount, timing, and uncertainty of cash flows from leasing activities. Entities must outline risk management strategies concerning residual values, buy-back agreements, and variable payments.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on lessor-specific risk exposures like buy-back guarantees rather than lessee liability repayment schedules.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: External reports like management commentary or value-added statements
inclusion: Opening balance sheet for retrospective accounting changes
Two-section statement of profit and loss and OCI
descriptor.definition: A comprehensive set requires a balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, changes in equity, cash flows, and explanatory notes with material policies. Equal prominence must be given to all statements, incorporating appropriate comparative periods.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates routine annual comparative data from retroactive opening balance sheet requirements.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Attributing benefit to periods of service
Attributing Benefit to Periods of Service

exclusion: Attribution models failing to adjust for disproportionate benefit surges in later working years
inclusion: Obligations arising from employee service even prior to formal vesting
Discounted present values reflecting expected employee departure dates
descriptor.definition: Entities attribute benefits to service periods based on the plan's formula, utilizing straight-line allocation if later service yields materially higher benefits. This attribution spans from the initial date service leads to benefits until further service yields no material benefit increases outside of salary adjustments.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard period-cost matching by linking the liability creation directly to historical and current employee service delivery.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES
PART B: CURRENT TAX, ITS RECOGNITION, MEASUREMENT AND PRESENTATION

exclusion: Deferred tax asset calculations
inclusion: Unpaid current tax recognized as a liability
Excess advance tax or TDS recognized as an asset
Use of statistical tools for uncertain tax interpretations
descriptor.definition: Current tax liabilities and assets for current and prior periods are measured at the amount expected to be paid to or recovered from taxation authorities. Computations rely on enacted or substantively enacted tax rates and laws, treating any revisions resulting from uncertain tax positions as changes in estimates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes current period tax obligations settled via cash from future timing-based tax allocations.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

exclusion: Information already reported directly as part of segment reporting requirements under the standard
inclusion: Revenues from external customers for products and services
Geographical revenue and non-current asset disclosures
Major customer reliance disclosures
descriptor.definition: Entities must provide entity-wide disclosures regarding products, services, geographical areas, and major customers regardless of how their operating segments are organized. These additional disclosures use financial information utilized to produce the entity's financial statements.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard segment disclosures because they apply universally across the entity regardless of the internal management approach used to identify operating segments.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Taxes recognized directly in equity or other comprehensive income
inclusion: Aggregation of current tax amounts
Aggregation of deferred tax amounts within profit or loss
descriptor.definition: Tax expense or tax income represents the aggregate amount included in determining the profit or loss for a period. It combines both current tax and deferred tax components and can result in either a positive expense or negative tax income.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from cash tax paid by incorporating non-cash deferred tax adjustments.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Scope of Statement of Cash Flows

exclusion: entities exempt from general purpose financial statement presentation
inclusion: manufacturing organizations
trading concerns
banks and financial institutions
descriptor.definition: Every entity, regardless of size, industry, or operational focus, must prepare and present a statement of cash flows as an integral part of its financial statements. This mandate applies equally to commercial businesses, service organizations, and financial institutions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from optional supplementary schedules by being a mandatory, integral component of required financial reporting.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: general administrative overhead
costs incurred after asset is ready for intended use
inclusion: purchase price including import duties and non-refundable taxes
employee benefits cost arising directly from bringing the asset to working condition
professional fees and testing costs
descriptor.definition: Intangible assets are initially measured at cost upon acquisition or self-generation. Separately acquired assets automatically satisfy probability criteria and include purchase price and directly attributable preparation costs.
nearby_distinctions: Initial cost measurement versus subsequent measurement models

path.name: Chapter 11: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
Unit 3: FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS: EQUITY AND FINANCIAL

exclusion: Equity conversion options meeting equity classification criteria
Stand-alone derivative contracts
inclusion: Issuer call options
Early redemption features in convertible instruments
descriptor.definition: Non-equity embedded derivative features, such as an issuer's call option contained within a compound financial instrument, are categorized and included as part of the liability component. The residual value after deducting the combined liability and derivative obligations is then allocated to the equity component.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity conversion options because non-equity derivatives like issuer call options are grouped with the liability component rather than assigned to equity.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

exclusion: Current period standalone figures without historical context
inclusion: Prior period numeric data
Relevant descriptive text from prior periods
descriptor.definition: Entities must present comparative information for the preceding period for all amounts reported in the current period, along with relevant narrative disclosures. The minimum requirement includes two balance sheets, two statements of profit and loss, two cash flow statements, two statements of changes in equity, and related notes.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from current period reporting by supplying baseline comparative metrics from immediately preceding cycles.

path.name: Recognition of Assets and Liabilities of the Acquired Entity
Recognition Of Assets And Liabilities Of The Acquired Entity

exclusion: Future restructuring costs or internal exit plans not obligating the acquiree at acquisition
inclusion: Acquired intangible assets unrecorded by the acquiree historically
Assumed liabilities meeting framework recognition criteria
descriptor.definition: On the acquisition date, the acquirer must recognize identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed separately from goodwill based on their compliance with framework definitions. Assets and liabilities brought onto the books are limited strictly to those acquired or assumed as part of the combination transaction.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general asset accumulation by focusing solely on items exchanged or assumed within the business combination perimeter

path.name: Chapter 1: Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards

exclusion: Schedules governed entirely by separate legislative acts for specialized financial sectors
Informal financial summaries
inclusion: Balance sheet and profit and loss statements
Cash flow statements and statements of changes in equity
descriptor.definition: Schedule III establishes the statutory presentation structure for financial statements prepared by companies registered under corporate legislation. Financial statements prepared under this framework encompass balance sheets, equity change statements, profit and loss statements, cash flow statements, and explanatory notes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from individual accounting standards by focusing strictly on presentation layout and disclosure structures rather than recognition and measurement rules.

exclusion: Replacement awards issued directly by the acquirer
inclusion: Vested share awards classified within non-controlling interest
Pre-combination portions of unvested acquiree awards
descriptor.definition: When an acquirer does not exchange outstanding share-based payment awards of the acquiree, they are measured at their market-based measure. Vested awards and the pre-combination portion of unvested awards form part of the non-controlling interest.
nearby_distinctions: Unvested non-replacement portions split across non-controlling interest for pre-combination service and employee cost for post-combination service.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 1 : PRESENTATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
True and Fair View and Compliance

exclusion: Unverified compliance claims lacking adherence to complete standard criteria
inclusion: Explicit compliance notes in financial statements
Additional disclosures when standard requirements prove insufficient
descriptor.definition: Financial statements must faithfully represent operational transactions and events in accordance with Conceptual Framework definitions. Compliance with applicable Indian Accounting Standards creates a legal presumption of achieving a true and fair view.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes baseline standard compliance from supplemental disclosures needed for genuine clarity.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Deferred tax liabilities on initial goodwill recognition exceptions
inclusion: Deferred tax impacts from asset and liability fair value uplifts in acquisitions
Adjustments to goodwill calculations
descriptor.definition: Practical application of income tax standards involves recognizing deferred tax assets and liabilities arising from fair value adjustments in business combinations. These recognized tax balances directly affect the determination of goodwill or bargain purchase gains on the acquisition date.
nearby_distinctions: Acquisition-date fair value adjustments create temporary differences that directly alter consolidated goodwill, distinguishing them from routine standalone asset shifts.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Leases failing to meet risk and reward transfer thresholds which default to operating leases
inclusion: Leases transferring ownership by the end of the term
Leases with bargain purchase options
Leases covering the major part of an asset economic life
descriptor.definition: Lessors evaluate lease agreements at inception to classify them as finance or operating leases according to the transfer of ownership risks and rewards. Indicators include transfer of title, purchase options, major economic life lease terms, and specialized asset nature.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts finance leases which shift ownership risks to the lessee with operating leases where the lessor retains those primary asset risks.

path.name: Chapter 4: Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies
EXTRACTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS OF LISTED ENTITIES
Financial Statement Extracts for Fair Value Measurement

exclusion: Hypothetical valuation models lacking corporate reporting backing
Unverified draft calculations
inclusion: Entity-specific accounting policy disclosures on fair value
Categorized financial statement presentation notes
descriptor.definition: Published corporate reports provide practical disclosures demonstrating how entities apply measurement techniques and accounting policies for fair value. These reporting extracts illustrate real-world execution of valuation governance within financial statements.
source_ambiguities: The source text provides only a heading and bibliographic reference without substantive accounting rules or data.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from theoretical standard text by presenting empirical corporate reporting compliance and application examples.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Actual or imputed cost of equity
Preferred capital not classified as a liability
inclusion: Directly attributable borrowing costs for qualifying assets
descriptor.definition: Borrowing costs that are directly attributable to the acquisition, construction, or production of a qualifying asset must be capitalized as part of that asset's cost. All other borrowing costs are recognized as expenses in the period in which they are incurred.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between mandatory capitalization for qualifying asset acquisition and expensing of general operational borrowing costs.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Face of balance sheet line-item values
Cash flow statement line items
inclusion: Descriptions of non-current assets or disposal groups
Circumstances and timing of expected disposal
Segment reporting classifications
descriptor.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive notes detailing the description, facts, circumstances, and expected timing of disposal for assets or disposal groups classified as held for sale. Additional required disclosures include recognized gains or losses, operating segment information, and the operational impacts of any cancelled sale plans.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from balance sheet presentation by requiring qualitative descriptive narratives and supplementary details within the notes.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
CHANGES IN EXISTING DECOMMISSIONING, RESTORATION AND SIMILAR LIABILITIES (APPENDIX A)
Changes in Existing Decommissioning, Restoration and Similar Liabilities (Appendix A)

exclusion: Initial recognition estimates of decommissioning obligations
Liabilities outside the scope of asset cost capitalization
inclusion: Obligations recognized as part of PPE or right-of-use asset costs
Liabilities recognized under Ind AS 37
descriptor.definition: This guidance applies to adjustments in existing dismantling, removal, and site restoration obligations initially incorporated into the cost of property, plant and equipment or right-of-use assets. It governs how entities account for subsequent shifts in estimated cash outflows, discount rates, and the unwinding of the discount over time.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial recognition by focusing exclusively on subsequent re-measurements and modifications of established liabilities.

path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”

exclusion: General financial statement notes unrelated to customer contracts
inclusion: Disclosures of opening and closing contract balances
Information about performance obligations and transaction prices
Judgements made in determining timing and measurement
descriptor.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive disclosures regarding contracts with customers, including disaggregated revenue, contract balances, performance obligations, and transaction prices. These disclosures enable users to understand the nature, amount, timing, and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows.
nearby_distinctions: General disclosures provide high-level totals of revenue and impairments, whereas specific disclosures break down performance obligations, transaction prices, and significant judgements.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)

exclusion: Presenting completely unstructured or unclassified raw data without regard to shared characteristics
Concealing critical information entirely through excessive data compression
inclusion: Combining items with shared characteristics within the same classification
Presenting summarized line items on primary financial statements such as the balance sheet and statement of profit and loss
descriptor.definition: Aggregation involves grouping assets, liabilities, equity, income, or expenses that share common characteristics within the same classification. This process enhances financial utility by condensing extensive details, while requiring a balance to prevent important facts from being obscured by excessive summarization or insignificant minutiae.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from detailed disclosure in notes, which provides granular information corresponding to the aggregated line items on primary statements.

path.name: Contingent Payments to Employees or Selling Shareholders
Contingent Payments to Employees or Selling Shareholders

exclusion: Unconditional purchase consideration distributed uniformly to all former owners
inclusion: Payments automatically forfeited upon termination of employment
Contingent arrangements tied to required employment periods
descriptor.definition: Contingent payments to selling shareholders who become employees are evaluated to determine whether they represent contingent consideration or remuneration for post-combination services. Factors such as employment forfeiture clauses and employment duration help clarify the substance of the payments.
nearby_distinctions: Classified as post-combination employee expense if dependent on continued employment, rather than part of the purchase price.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Retrospective adjustments for changes that were anticipated in the original contract terms
inclusion: Evaluation of scope and consideration changes
Separate lease accounting when criteria for added assets are fulfilled
Prospective reclassification assessment for non-separate modifications
descriptor.definition: A lease modification is a change in scope or consideration not part of the original terms. It is accounted for as a separate lease if scope increases due to additional underlying assets at standalone prices; otherwise, non-separate modifications are reassessed prospectively.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between modifications that expand distinct asset rights treated as separate contracts versus changes requiring a combined prospective reassessment.

path.name: Chapter 11: Accounting and Reporting of Financial Instruments
Balance Sheet Disclosures for Financial Instruments

exclusion: Non-financial asset and liability disclosures
inclusion: Carrying amounts of financial assets and liabilities at fair value through profit or loss
Carrying amounts at amortised cost
Financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose the carrying amounts of financial assets and liabilities categorized under various valuation paradigms either directly on the balance sheet or within the notes. These categories include items measured at fair value through profit or loss, amortized cost, and fair value through other comprehensive income.
terminology: Fair Value through Profit or Loss
Fair Value through Other Comprehensive Income
nearby_distinctions: Differs from statement of profit and loss disclosures by focusing on stock balances rather than flow items of income and expense

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
Disclosures in the statement of cash flows
Disclosures in the Statement of Cash Flows

exclusion: Cash flow disclosures for newly acquired subsidiaries meeting held-for-sale criteria at acquisition
inclusion: Net cash flows of discontinued operations
Basic and diluted earnings per share for discontinued operations
descriptor.definition: Entities must disclose net operating, investing, and financing cash flows attributable to discontinued operations either within the financial statements or notes. Earnings per share figures for discontinued operations must also be presented with equal prominence alongside continuing operations.
nearby_distinctions: Extends reporting requirements beyond the income statement to cash flow tracking and per-share performance metrics.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Omission of residual risk management descriptions in qualitative notes
inclusion: Balance sheet presentation of net investment for finance leases
Asset nature-based presentation for operating leases
Tabular quantitative maturity breakdowns
descriptor.definition: Lessors present finance lease assets as receivables representing the net investment, while operating lease assets are presented according to their specific asset nature. Extensive quantitative and qualitative disclosures are required to communicate cash flow timing and uncertainties.
nearby_distinctions: Compares lessor presentation rules under Ind AS 116 with older standards like AS 19 which lacked formal lease modification guidance.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements

exclusion: Movements between items constituting cash or cash equivalents
inclusion: Investments realizable easily in a short period
Items utilized for meeting short-term cash commitments
descriptor.definition: Cash equivalents represent short-term investments easily realizable into known cash amounts with negligible risk of value fluctuation. Internal movements and transfers between items constituting cash or cash equivalents are excluded from cash flows because they form part of entity cash management.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from operating, investing, and financing cash flows which involve external resource exchanges.

path.name: Determining what is part of the Business Combination Transaction
Determining what is part of the Business Combination Transaction

exclusion: Core consideration directly exchanged for the equity interests or assets of the acquiree
inclusion: Settlements of pre-existing relationships
Remuneration for post-combination employee services
descriptor.definition: Acquirers must isolate and exclude transactions that are separate from the exchange for the acquiree. Separate transactions are those arranged primarily for the benefit of the acquirer rather than the acquiree prior to combination.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from consideration transferred by serving acquirer-centric objectives rather than compensating former owners for the business.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: Combining discontinued EPS directly into a single blended EPS total without separate disclosure
inclusion: Basic EPS for discontinued operations
Diluted EPS for discontinued operations
descriptor.definition: Basic and diluted earnings per share metrics for discontinued operations must be disclosed separately in the statement of profit and loss or notes. These figures are presented alongside continuing operations metrics with equal prominence.
nearby_distinctions: Applies per-share calculation rules distinctively to discontinued segments rather than aggregate company performance alone.

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 1: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 12 : INCOME TAXES

exclusion: Initial recognition and measurement rules detailed in earlier sections
inclusion: Major components of tax expense
Taxes related to items charged directly to equity
descriptor.definition: Financial statement reporting mandates extend beyond recognition and measurement to encompass detailed disclosures regarding income taxes. These disclosures explain tax expenses, equity charges, and other tax-related line items.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from core recognition principles by focusing strictly on note disclosures and explanatory breakdowns.

exclusion: transactions governed solely by older guidance notes for entities complying with Ind AS
inclusion: grants of shares or options to employees
payments to suppliers of professional services using shares
descriptor.definition: A share-based payment is a transaction where an entity acquires goods or services by granting equity instruments or incurring liabilities based on equity values. Corporate entities following Ind AS apply Ind AS 102 for these transactions rather than general guidance notes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from cash-only compensation as the settlement amount is linked to equity prices.

path.name: Chapter 3: Ind AS on Presentation of General Purpose Financial Statements
CONTENTS OF AN INTERIM FINANCIAL REPORT
Contents of an Interim Financial Report

exclusion: Unnecessary repetition of previously reported annual information
inclusion: Condensed balance sheet
Condensed statement of profit and loss
Condensed statement of changes in equity
Condensed statement of cash flows
Material accounting policy information and explanatory notes
descriptor.definition: An interim financial report must minimally include a condensed balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows, and selected explanatory notes. It focuses on new activities and events to avoid duplicating information previously disclosed in the most recent annual report.
terminology: Condensed Statement of Profit and Loss
nearby_distinctions: Differs from annual reports by allowing condensed formats and focusing exclusively on updates rather than exhaustive disclosures.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

exclusion: Separate dual lines when no potential ordinary shares exist and basic equals diluted EPS
inclusion: Basic and diluted amounts for profit or loss from continuing operations
Per share figures for discontinued operations in notes or financial statements
descriptor.definition: Entities must present basic and diluted earnings per share with equal prominence within the statement of profit and loss for every presented period. Negative earnings amounts representing losses per share must be explicitly disclosed alongside distinct figures for continuing and discontinued operations.
nearby_distinctions: Discontinued operations require separate per-share disclosure, distinguishing them from continuing operations performance metrics.
