path.name: Globalization Impact and Base Erosion Drivers

exclusion: Domestic-only commercial transactions
Traditional double taxation elimination mechanisms
inclusion: Cross-border movement of capital and labor
Digital product delivery models
Aggressive corporate tax minimization practices
descriptor.definition: Global economic integration and digital advancements enable multinational enterprises to shift productive activities and exploit legal gaps across jurisdictions. These operational shifts facilitate aggressive tax planning structures that artificially erode domestic corporate tax bases.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from historical double taxation issues by focusing on profit disappearance through legal mismatch exploitation rather than mere overlapping tax jurisdictions.

path.name: NOTICE DEEMED TO BE VALID IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 292BB]
Notice Deemed To Be Valid In Certain Circumstances [Section 292Bb]

exclusion: Cases where the assessee formally objects to service defects before assessment completion
inclusion: Curing of defective, delayed, or unserved notices through assessee participation
Waiver of service objections upon cooperation in proceedings
descriptor.definition: An assessee who participates in assessment or reassessment proceedings is precluded from later challenging the validity, timeliness, or manner of notice service. This deeming provision does not apply if the assessee raises a specific objection regarding service defects prior to the completion of the assessment or reassessment.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from document-level errors under section 292B by specifically addressing personal notice service and recipient participation waivers.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
CERTAIN DEDUCTIONS ALLOWED ON ACTUAL PAYMENT BASIS ONLY [SECTION 37]
Certain Deductions Allowed On Actual Payment Basis Only [Section 37]

exclusion: Expenses claimable purely on accrual without regard to actual payment mandates
inclusion: Taxes, duties, cess, or fees levied under law
Employer contributions to provident, superannuation, or gratuity funds
Bonus, commission, or leave encashment payable to employees
descriptor.definition: Specific statutory liabilities such as taxes, duties, welfare fund contributions, leave encashment, and bonuses are deductible only upon actual payment regardless of accounting methods. However, timely payments made on or before the return filing due date fulfill this condition for the incurred tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard accrual-based commercial expenses from statutory liabilities requiring actual cash outflow or timely return-filing payment.

path.name: MONETARY LIMITS FOR REGULATING FILING OF APPEALS BY INCOME TAX AUTHORITIES [SECTION 268A]
Monetary Limits for Regulating Filing of Appeals by Income Tax Authorities

exclusion: Appeals exceeding the specified monetary cutoffs where merits justify litigation
inclusion: Departmental appeals restricted by prescribed monetary thresholds
Future filings on identical issues for other assessment years or assessees
descriptor.definition: The central board is empowered to set financial thresholds that regulate when tax authorities can file appeals or reference applications before tribunals and courts. Failure to appeal in a specific case due to these monetary limits does not prevent the authority from litigating the same issue in other assessment years or against different assessees.
nearby_distinctions: Regulates administrative discretion to litigate based on financial stakes rather than the legal merit of the underlying dispute.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Interest for defaults in furnishing return of income [Section 234A]
Interest for Defaults in Furnishing Return of Income

exclusion: Inclusion of additional income tax components specified under sections 140B or 143 within the interest calculation base
inclusion: Monthly interest computations for late or un-furnished tax returns
Reductions for advance interest payments made under section 140A
descriptor.definition: Simple interest is charged when an assessee fails to submit an income tax return by the statutory due date or omits filing entirely. The charge accrues monthly from the day following the due date until the actual filing date or best-judgment completion.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on return submission timelines rather than installment payment milestones or tax deferment discrepancies.

path.name: APPLICABLE RATE OF TAX IN RESPECT OF WINNINGS FROM ONLINE GAMES [SECTION 194(1) (TABLE: SI. NO. 5)]

exclusion: Traditional physical lotteries, crosswords, and offline gambling winnings
inclusion: Net winnings originating from internet-accessible games via computer resources
descriptor.definition: Net winnings from online games accessed through computer resources or telecommunication devices are subject to a flat tax rate. No related expenditure allowances, Chapter VIII deductions, or basic exemption limit adjustments are permitted against this income.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes digital and internet-based gaming platforms from traditional offline casual income sources.

exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
descriptor.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward
NO SET OFF OF LOSSES AGAINST UNDISCLOSED INCOME CONSEQUENT TO SEARCH, REQUISITION AND SURVEY [SECTION 120]
NO SET OFF OF LOSSES AGAINST UNDISCLOSED INCOME CONSEQUENT TO SEARCH, REQUISITION AND SURVEY [SECTION 120]

exclusion: surveys conducted under section 253(4)
inclusion: prohibition of loss set-off against undisclosed assets or transactions
restriction on offsetting unabsorbed depreciation against discovered income
descriptor.definition: Brought forward losses, current losses, and unabsorbed depreciation cannot be set off against undisclosed income uncovered during statutory searches, requisitions, or qualifying surveys. Undisclosed income encompasses unrecorded assets, transactions, or incorrect expense and deduction claims for the block period.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard business income and regular loss adjustments from punitive non-set-off rules applied exclusively to discovered undisclosed income.

path.name: REFERENCE TO PRINCIPAL COMMISSIONER OR COMMISSIONER IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 144BA]
Reference To Principal Commissioner Or Commissioner In Certain Cases

exclusion: Arrangements finalized without giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard
inclusion: References for declaring arrangements as impermissible avoidance arrangements
Approving Panel binding directions
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer can refer an arrangement to the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner to declare it an impermissible avoidance arrangement. The authority issues notices, evaluates objections, and may refer the matter to an Approving Panel which issues binding directions for completion.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard tax evasion inquiries by targeting complex tax avoidance arrangements through a specialized multi-tier review involving the Principal Commissioner and Approving Panel.

path.name: WITHHOLDING TAX PROVISIONS FOR NON- RESIDENTS
Withholding Tax on Non-Resident Salaries and Perquisites

exclusion: Salaries for services rendered entirely outside India
inclusion: Salary income deemed to accrue in India due to services rendered locally
Employer payment of tax on non-monetary perquisites without employee deduction
Deferred TDS on specified securities or sweat equity from eligible startups
descriptor.definition: Employers must deduct withholding tax at applicable rates on salary payments to non-residents when services are rendered within India. Special provisions govern tax calculation on non-monetary perquisites and allow deferred tax payment timelines for specified startup securities.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes monetary salary withholding from non-monetary perquisite tax handling

exclusion: Unapproved non-statutory communication channels lacking CBDT backing
inclusion: Service by post or approved courier services
Service via electronic records under IT Act chapter IV
Designated addressees for firms, companies, HUFs, and local authorities
descriptor.definition: Tax communications, notices, and summons may be served by post, approved courier services, Code of Civil Procedure methods, electronic records, or other CBDT-prescribed transmission means. Specific statutory addressees are designated for serving notices corresponding to distinct entity types such as firms, Hindu Undivided Families, companies, and associations.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the procedural modes and mandatory recipient addressees for serving notices, whereas Section 282A governs the authentication and signing validity of those notices

path.name: PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]
PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]

exclusion: Unauthorized third parties lacking specific legal designation or valid power of attorney
inclusion: Assessee himself for individuals under normal circumstances
Authorized power-of-attorney holders during absence or incapacity
Managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals for companies
descriptor.definition: Statutory provisions explicitly designate which individuals possess the legal authority to sign and verify income tax returns on behalf of different assessee types. Depending on circumstances such as absence, mental incapacity, winding up, or corporate insolvency, specific representatives like power-of-attorney holders, managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals are authorized.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on the legal competence to sign and authenticate return documents, separate from the actual preparation or computation of income.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Liability for payment of advance tax
Liability for Payment of Advance Tax

exclusion: Taxpayers whose total advance tax liability remains under ten thousand rupees
Non-residents meeting age criteria
inclusion: Mandatory advance tax obligations for liabilities exceeding the statutory threshold
Relief provisions for elderly resident individuals with rental or interest incomes
descriptor.definition: An obligation to pay advance tax is triggered whenever the computed tax liability reaches or exceeds ten thousand rupees for the financial year. Resident individuals aged sixty or older without business or professional income are exempted from this payment rule.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general tax remittance because liability is conditioned specifically on crossing a minimum financial threshold and the absence of speculative business revenue for senior exemptions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Faceless collection and recovery of tax [Section 231]
Faceless Collection And Recovery Of Tax [Section 231]

exclusion: Traditional physical field enforcement operations not covered under the notified scheme
inclusion: Faceless processing of lower deduction or collection certificates
Digital handling of installment extensions and penalty levies
Automated resource optimization and team-based assessments
descriptor.definition: The Central Government is empowered to notify schemes for faceless collection and recovery of tax to eliminate physical interfaces between authorities and assessees. This framework covers lower deduction certificates, default orders, interest waivers, and recovery certificate operations using dynamic jurisdiction.
nearby_distinctions: Replaces traditional localized administrative touchpoints with an automated, virtual, team-based jurisdiction model across recovery and deduction functions.

exclusion: Capital expenditures not specifically authorized by the provisions
inclusion: Commissions for realizing interest on securities
Repairs, insurance, and depreciation for let-out plant, machinery, or furniture
Family pension statutory limits and 50% deduction on enhanced compensation interest
descriptor.definition: Computations under this head permit specific deductions including banking realization commissions for securities, employee contribution recoveries remitted before return filing deadlines, and asset letting expenses. Other allowed items comprise family pension standard deductions, compensation interest reliefs, and specific pension commutations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between standard operational expense deductions and flat statutory percentage deductions allowed for specific income types like family pensions.

path.name: Civil Court Powers and Inquiry Authority of Tax Officials (Continuation)

exclusion: Arbitrary extra-judicial actions unaligned with formal civil procedure principles
inclusion: Issuing commissions
Compelling production of books of account
Investigating suspected concealed income prior to formal proceedings
descriptor.definition: Specific income-tax authorities possess the same powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure when handling matters such as discovery, enforcing attendance, and compelling document production. These powers can be invoked for inquiry or investigation purposes even when no active proceeding is pending if tax concealment is suspected.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general survey or search actions by strictly adopting judicial trial powers like examination on oath and discovery under civil procedural rules.

path.name: COMPUTATION OF CAPITAL GAINS IN CASE OF DEPRECIABLE ASSETS [SECTIONS 74 & 75]
Computation of Capital Gains in Case of Depreciable Assets

exclusion: Non-depreciable capital assets governed by standard holding period criteria for long-term or short-term classification
inclusion: Assets forming part of a depreciable block of assets
Power sector depreciable assets under specific provisions
descriptor.definition: Capital gains on the transfer of depreciable assets forming part of a block of assets are deemed short-term capital gains when the full value of consideration exceeds the aggregate of transfer expenses, opening written down value, and actual cost of new acquisitions. If an entire block of assets ceases to exist due to full transfer, the resulting excess or deficit is treated accordingly under overriding rules.
nearby_distinctions: Overrides standard short-term asset definitions based on holding periods by automatically classifying gains from depreciable asset blocks as short-term.

path.name: POWER OF ASSESSING OFFICER TO MAKE A REFERENCE TO THE VALUATION OFFICER [SECTION 142A]
Power Of Assessing Officer To Make A Reference To The Valuation Officer [Section 142A]

exclusion: References made without affording an opportunity of being heard before final assessment integration
inclusion: Reference for estimating fair market value of assets, properties, or investments
Best judgment estimation upon non-cooperation
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer can reference a Valuation Officer to estimate the fair market value or value of any asset, property, or investment for assessment purposes. The Valuation Officer must submit the report within six months, and the Assessing Officer utilizes it after granting the assessee a hearing opportunity.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from special audits under section 142(2A) as it focuses strictly on estimating asset, property, or investment values through a specialized Valuation Officer rather than financial account auditing.

exclusion: Data outside official authority possession or information not authorized for upload under relevant tax exchange agreements
inclusion: Information relating to tax deducted or collected at source
Information relating to specified financial transactions and tax payments
Information relating to demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings
descriptor.definition: Tax authorities must upload an annual information statement in Form No. 26AS into an assessee's registered electronic filing portal account within three months of receiving the underlying data. This statement aggregates information on tax deducted or collected at source, specified financial transactions, tax payments, demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings.
nearby_distinctions: Constitutes the consolidated statement uploaded to the taxpayer's portal under Section 285BB, whereas Section 285BA governs the underlying reporting obligations submitted by reporting entities

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Consequences of failure to deduct or pay
Consequences Of Failure To Deduct Or Pay

exclusion: Standard tax remittance within statutory due dates
Penalties charged without proper opportunity of being heard
inclusion: Interest at 1 percent per month for failure to deduct
Interest at 1.5 percent per month from deduction to payment date
descriptor.definition: Failing to deduct or pay tax makes a person a deemed assessee-in-default, attracting mandatory simple interest liabilities. However, an exception applies if the payee has already reported the income, paid the tax, and an accountant's certificate is furnished.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from routine tax compliance by imposing punitive default status and compounding interest rates for non-compliance.

path.name: BOARDS FOR ADVANCE RULINGS – AN INTRODUCTION

exclusion: Old Settlement Commission rulings
inclusion: Boards constituted under Chapter XIX-B
descriptor.definition: Bodies established by the Central Government to pronounce binding determinations on tax questions for applicants under Chapter XIX-B. These boards consist of two officers not below the rank of Chief Commissioner.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Income-tax Authorities and Appellate Tribunals by specific statutory jurisdiction.

path.name: OBLIGATION TO FURNISH STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL TRANSACTION OR REPORTABLE ACCOUNT [SECTION 285BA]
Obligation To Furnish Statement Of Financial Transaction Or Reportable Account [Section 285Ba]

exclusion: Entities outside the designated categories of reporting persons and financial institutions defined under the section
inclusion: Transactions of purchase, sale, or exchange of goods, property, or rights
Transactions for rendering services or under works contracts
Transactions involving investments made, expenditures incurred, or loans taken
descriptor.definition: Specified entities, including reporting financial institutions, registrars, and government offices maintaining books or records, must furnish statements regarding specified financial transactions or reportable accounts to income-tax authorities. These prescribed transactions encompass property purchases, service rendering, works contracts, investments, expenditures, and loan takings.
nearby_distinctions: Imposes broad financial transaction reporting obligations across designated institutional entities, whereas Section 285B is strictly confined to film producers and specified media/event activities

path.name: COMPUTATION OF CAPITAL GAINS IN CASE OF MARKET LINKED DEBENTURES, SPECIFIED MUTUAL FUND ETC. [SECTION 76]
Computation of Capital Gains for Market Linked Debentures and Specified Mutual Funds

exclusion: Assets whose classification depends upon the traditional holding period rather than statutory overriding rules
inclusion: Units of specified mutual funds acquired on or after 1.4.2023
Market linked debentures
Unlisted bonds and debentures transferred or redeemed on or after 23.7.2024
descriptor.definition: Capital gains arising from the transfer, redemption, or maturity of specified mutual fund units, market linked debentures, or unlisted bonds and debentures are mandatorily treated as short-term capital gains. The gain is computed by deducting the cost of acquisition and transfer expenditures from the full value of consideration without allowing deductions for securities transaction tax.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general capital gains provisions by overriding normal holding period requirements and denying securities transaction tax deductions.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
EXEMPTION IN RESPECT OF INCOME OF CERTAIN UNIVERSITIES, EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, HOSPITALS, MEDICAL INSTITUTIONS ETC.
Exemption for Certain Educational and Medical Institutions

exclusion: Institutions operating for profit
Hospitals or educational institutions exceeding the financial receipt threshold without government financing
inclusion: Universities wholly or substantially financed by the government
Hospitals existing solely for philanthropic purposes and substantially financed by the government
Educational and medical institutions with aggregate annual receipts not exceeding five crore rupees
descriptor.definition: Specific universities, educational institutions, hospitals, and medical institutions are exempt from income tax on their total income if they are wholly or substantially financed by the government, or if their aggregate annual receipts do not exceed five crore rupees. An institution is considered substantially financed when government grants exceed 50 percent of its total receipts including donations during the tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes government-backed or smaller scale medical and educational bodies from standard commercial enterprises and general trusts.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Accrual-based recognition for items specifically mandated by statute to follow receipt or realization rules
inclusion: Interest on enhanced compensation taxed upon receipt
Price escalation claims and export incentives taxed upon realization certainty
Government subsidies and cash incentives taxed on receipt basis
descriptor.definition: Income under the business or profession head must be computed using either the cash or mercantile system regularly employed by the assessee. Specific items like certain government subsidies, price escalation claims, and export incentives are statutorily recognized for tax purposes based on receipt or realization certainty.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts regular accounting methods with specific statutory timing rules overriding standard cash or mercantile principles.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward
CARRY FORWARD AND SET OFF OF LOSSES NOT PERMISSIBLE IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 119]
CARRY FORWARD AND SET OFF OF LOSSES NOT PERMISSIBLE IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 119]

exclusion: carry forward of partner's proportionate loss upon retirement or death
carry forward of predecessor business losses by non-inheriting successors
inclusion: unabsorbed depreciation carry forward despite partnership constitution changes
business loss carry forward by legal heirs in succession by inheritance
descriptor.definition: Unabsorbed business losses proportionate to a retired or deceased partner cannot be carried forward upon a firm constitution change, though unabsorbed depreciation remains eligible. Similarly, business succession otherwise than by inheritance bars the successor from carrying forward the predecessor's losses, whereas succession by inheritance permits such carry forward.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between restrictions on unabsorbed business losses versus unabsorbed depreciation during constitution changes or non-inheritance successions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Fee/ penalty for default in furnishing TDS/ TCS Statements
Fee and Penalty for Default in Furnishing TDS and TCS Statements

exclusion: Penalty impositions under section 271H when delayed statements are filed within the permitted one-year timeframe alongside due payments
inclusion: Daily statutory fees for delayed TDS and TCS statement filings
Monetized penalty ranges for un-furnished or incorrect statements
Conditional penalty waivers for compliance within specified grace periods
descriptor.definition: Late submission of tax deduction or collection statements incurs a mandatory daily fee capped at the total tax amount. Additional monetary penalties apply for missing statutory deadlines or providing incorrect statement information, with thresholds adjusted for extended delays.
nearby_distinctions: Separates administrative daily late-filing fees from substantive legal penalties, imposing both concurrently only when delays exceed extended statutory limits.

exclusion: Rules that conflict with, restrict, or adversely affect the operative effect of parent act sections
inclusion: Rule-making authority of the Board
Statutory force and parliamentary oversight of formulated rules
descriptor.definition: The Central Board of Direct Taxes is empowered to formulate subordinate rules under central government control to implement the Act, which must be placed before Parliament. These rules carry statutory force equivalent to enactment sections provided they remain consistent with, supplementary to, and non-derogatory of the primary statute.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from primary legislative acts by being subordinate executive regulations that must strictly conform to the parent statute's mandate.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Initial demand notices or direct Assessing Officer garnishments without certificates
inclusion: Movable and immovable property attachments
Arrest and detention
Inclusion of assets transferred to close relatives without adequate consideration
descriptor.definition: When an assessee is in default, the Tax Recovery Officer draws up a signed statement of arrears and initiates recovery through specific statutory modes such as property attachment and sale, arrest, or appointment of a receiver. Transferred properties to spouses or minor children for inadequate consideration are legally included in the assessee's recoverable pool.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Section 220/221 because it represents an escalated administrative recovery stage executed specifically via a formal certificate drawn up by a designated recovery officer.

path.name: LIMITATION OF INTEREST DEDUCTION IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 94B]
Limitation of Interest Deduction in Certain Cases

exclusion: Dividend payments on equity financing
inclusion: Interest expenses on debt borrowed from associated enterprises
Ceiling limits on interest deductions under business income
descriptor.definition: This provision restricts the deductibility of interest expenses claimed on borrowings from associated enterprises to curb profit shifting through excessive debt financing. It sets a ceiling limit on interest deductions in alignment with international base erosion countermeasures.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general transfer pricing pricing rules as it applies specifically to debt-to-equity capitalization structures and interest caps.

exclusion: Incomes explicitly exempt from charge under statutory provisions
inclusion: Total income of persons specified under the Act
Tax rates specified by the Finance Act or Income-tax Act, 2025
descriptor.definition: Income-tax is charged on the total income of every person for the tax year at the rates prescribed by the annual Finance Act or the Income-tax Act, 2025. This charging provision forms the foundational basis from which any tax liability legally originates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from computational provisions by serving strictly as the legal origin of tax liability.

path.name: FACILITY FOR ACCEPTING PAYMENT THROUGH PRESCRIBED ELECTRONIC MODES [SECTION 269SU]
Facility For Accepting Payment Through Prescribed Electronic Modes [Section 269Su]

exclusion: Assessees whose gross receipts do not exceed the 50 crore rupee threshold
Specified persons having exclusively B2B transactions with at least 95 percent non-cash receipts
inclusion: Businesses with gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees
RuPay debit card payment facilities
BHIM-UPI and BHIM-UPI QR code payment facilities
descriptor.definition: Businesses with total sales, turnover, or gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees in the preceding financial year must provide facilities for accepting payments through prescribed electronic modes. Non-compliance attracts a daily penalty under section 271DB, while system providers are prohibited from imposing charges for using these mandated modes.
nearby_distinctions: Mandates the provision of electronic payment acceptance facilities rather than restricting transaction modes like sections 269SS, 269ST, and 269T

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
EXPENSES OR PAYMENTS NOT DEDUCTIBLE IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 36]
Expenses Or Payments Not Deductible In Certain Circumstances [Section 36]

exclusion: Reasonable payments conforming to fair market value and legitimate business requirements
inclusion: Payments made to relatives, directors, partners, or persons with substantial interest
Portion of expenditure deemed excessive relative to fair market value or business needs
descriptor.definition: Expenditures resulting from transactions with specified related persons can be restricted if the Assessing Officer determines they are excessive or unreasonable. This assessment considers fair market values, legitimate business needs, and benefits derived by the assessee.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes arm's length commercial transactions from related-party dealings subject to reasonableness scrutiny.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment on transfer of certain immovable property other than agricultural land [Section 194-IA]
Payment on transfer of certain immovable property other than agricultural land [Section 194-IA]

exclusion: rural agricultural land
compulsory acquisitions
inclusion: consideration for transfer of land other than rural agricultural land
buildings or parts of buildings
incidental charges like club membership and parking fees
descriptor.definition: Transferees acquiring immovable property other than rural agricultural land from a resident must deduct tax from the consideration or stamp duty value. Compulsory acquisitions are excluded as they fall under alternative provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike compulsory property acquisitions covered under Section 194LA, standard voluntary property transfers fall under Section 194-IA.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]

exclusion: individuals and HUFs required to deduct tax under Sections 194C, 194H, or 194J
inclusion: contract work payments
commission or brokerage
fees for professional services made by non-audit individuals and HUFs
descriptor.definition: Individuals and HUFs not subject to regular business audit requirements who pay substantial sums for contract work, commission, brokerage, or professional services must deduct tax at source. Taxpayers already obligated to deduct tax under specific contractor, commission, or professional sections are excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Serves as a catch-all provision for individual and HUF payees who exceed high financial thresholds but lack business audit obligations.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Eligible hedging contracts regarding raw materials, merchandise, or stocks and shares
Forward contracts executed by exchange members
inclusion: Transactions settled without actual delivery of commodities or scrips
Company share trading deemed as speculation subject to specific exceptions
descriptor.definition: A speculative business involves contracts for purchasing or selling commodities or stocks settled without actual delivery, and must be treated as distinct from any other business. Consequently, speculation losses can only be set off and carried forward against profits derived from speculation businesses.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard commercial trading from speculative transactions lacking actual delivery, enforcing strict segregation of losses.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: rent paid to a business trust being a REIT in respect of directly owned real estate assets
inclusion: payments for land or buildings
rent for plant, machinery, equipment, furniture, or fittings
descriptor.definition: Entities responsible for paying rental income for the use of land, buildings, machinery, plant, equipment, furniture, or fittings to a resident must deduct tax at source. Real estate assets owned directly by a REIT are exempt from this deduction.
nearby_distinctions: Applies distinct tax rates for plant, machinery, and equipment rental compared to land, building, and furniture rental.

path.name: Recovery and Miscellaneous Compliance for Non-Residents

exclusion: Domestic tax recovery procedures devoid of cross-border or representative elements
inclusion: Recovery of tax arrears from any assets of the non-resident in India
Cross-border tax recovery enforcement via CBDT and treaty partner nations
Statement submission requirements for non-residents with liaison offices
descriptor.definition: Tax authorities can recover unpaid taxes owed by non-residents directly from any of their assets located within India or through international treaty mechanisms involving foreign tax recovery certificates. Additionally, non-residents maintaining liaison offices must submit prescribed periodic statements to tax authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes domestic asset attachment from reciprocal international tax recovery mechanisms

path.name: Chapter 11: Tax Planning, Tax Avoidance and Tax Evasion
TAX PLANNING, TAX AVOIDANCE AND TAX EVASION – AN OVERVIEW
Tax Planning, Tax Avoidance and Tax Evasion Overview

exclusion: Illegal suppression of income
Fraudulent manipulation of accounts
inclusion: Application of tax law provisions to practical situations
Utilization of statutory exemptions and deductions
Analysis of CBDT circulars and court case laws
descriptor.definition: Tax planning involves arranging financial affairs to minimize tax liability by fully utilizing available exemptions, deductions, and reliefs without violating any legal provisions. It requires a thorough understanding of direct tax laws, judicial pronouncements, and CBDT circulars to optimize investible surplus.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from tax evasion by operating strictly within legal boundaries rather than through illegal concealment or fraud.

path.name: ASCERTAINMENT OF COST IN SPECIFIED CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 73]
Ascertainment of Cost in Specified Circumstances

exclusion: Direct market purchases where the acquirer establishes an independent original purchase cost
inclusion: Asset costs derived from the last previous owner under gifts, wills, and successions
Inclusion of previous owner holding periods for short-term and long-term asset determination
descriptor.definition: When an assessee acquires a capital asset through non-purchase methods such as gifts, succession, company liquidation, or structural amalgamations, the cost of acquisition is deemed as the cost incurred by the previous owner. Transferees in these specified circumstances are also permitted to include the previous owner's holding period for classification purposes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct purchase cost accounting from derivative cost tracking where asset ownership changes via inheritance, restructuring, or statutory distribution without fresh market acquisition.

path.name: Globalization Impact and Base Erosion Drivers

exclusion: Domestic-only commercial transactions
Traditional double taxation elimination mechanisms
inclusion: Cross-border movement of capital and labor
Digital product delivery models
Aggressive corporate tax minimization practices
descriptor.definition: Global economic integration and digital advancements enable multinational enterprises to shift productive activities and exploit legal gaps across jurisdictions. These operational shifts facilitate aggressive tax planning structures that artificially erode domestic corporate tax bases.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from historical double taxation issues by focusing on profit disappearance through legal mismatch exploitation rather than mere overlapping tax jurisdictions.

path.name: NOTICE DEEMED TO BE VALID IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 292BB]
Notice Deemed To Be Valid In Certain Circumstances [Section 292Bb]

exclusion: Cases where the assessee formally objects to service defects before assessment completion
inclusion: Curing of defective, delayed, or unserved notices through assessee participation
Waiver of service objections upon cooperation in proceedings
descriptor.definition: An assessee who participates in assessment or reassessment proceedings is precluded from later challenging the validity, timeliness, or manner of notice service. This deeming provision does not apply if the assessee raises a specific objection regarding service defects prior to the completion of the assessment or reassessment.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from document-level errors under section 292B by specifically addressing personal notice service and recipient participation waivers.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
CERTAIN DEDUCTIONS ALLOWED ON ACTUAL PAYMENT BASIS ONLY [SECTION 37]
Certain Deductions Allowed On Actual Payment Basis Only [Section 37]

exclusion: Expenses claimable purely on accrual without regard to actual payment mandates
inclusion: Taxes, duties, cess, or fees levied under law
Employer contributions to provident, superannuation, or gratuity funds
Bonus, commission, or leave encashment payable to employees
descriptor.definition: Specific statutory liabilities such as taxes, duties, welfare fund contributions, leave encashment, and bonuses are deductible only upon actual payment regardless of accounting methods. However, timely payments made on or before the return filing due date fulfill this condition for the incurred tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard accrual-based commercial expenses from statutory liabilities requiring actual cash outflow or timely return-filing payment.

path.name: MONETARY LIMITS FOR REGULATING FILING OF APPEALS BY INCOME TAX AUTHORITIES [SECTION 268A]
Monetary Limits for Regulating Filing of Appeals by Income Tax Authorities

exclusion: Appeals exceeding the specified monetary cutoffs where merits justify litigation
inclusion: Departmental appeals restricted by prescribed monetary thresholds
Future filings on identical issues for other assessment years or assessees
descriptor.definition: The central board is empowered to set financial thresholds that regulate when tax authorities can file appeals or reference applications before tribunals and courts. Failure to appeal in a specific case due to these monetary limits does not prevent the authority from litigating the same issue in other assessment years or against different assessees.
nearby_distinctions: Regulates administrative discretion to litigate based on financial stakes rather than the legal merit of the underlying dispute.

parts.label: i
parts.question_text:
(i)  The total receipts of the trust for the F.Y. 2024-25 for educational institution 
is ` 3.50 crores and for the hospital is ` 3.90 crores.

parts.label: ii
parts.question_text:
(ii)  Voluntary contributions [included in (i) above) received during the F.Y. 
2024-25 from the public amounted to ` 115 lakhs. Voluntary contributions 
of ` 115 lakhs includes corpus donations of ` 65 lakhs (for purchase of 
building for the trust) and anonymous donations of ` 20 lakhs with specific 
direction that such donations is for the purpose of educational institution 
run by the trust.

parts.label: iii
parts.question_text:
(iii)  During the F.Y. 2024-25, computers for use in the educational institution of 
trust were purchased for ` 85 lakhs out of – 
• 
Corpus fund mentioned in (ii) above - ` 35 lakhs. 
• 
Loan - ` 25 lakhs 
• 
Voluntary contributions - ` 25 lakhs

parts.label: iv
parts.question_text:
(iv)  Corpus donation received during the FY 2024-25 are invested in the same 
FY in- 
• 
Post Office Saving Accounts- ` 15 lakhs 
• 
Canara Bank as Fixed deposits - ` 5 lakhs 
• 
Deposit with a Private Limited Company-` 10 lakhs

parts.label: v
parts.question_text:
(v)  Amount paid to another trust registered u/s 12AB by way of donation of  
` 12 lakhs. Out of said amount ` 3 lakhs are given as corpus donations.

parts.label: vi
parts.question_text:
(vi)  ` 6 lakhs, being the amount set apart in the F.Y. 2023-24 by the trust for 
charitable purpose u/s 11(2) utilized in the F.Y. 2024-25 for making 
donation to another charitable trust, whose object is also education. 
From the facts given in the case study, choose the correct answer to the 
following Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs No. 9 to 12): 
9. 
Out of the amount corpus donation invested in FY 2024-25 [as mentioned 
in (iv)] by Seva Niketan, which of the following amount would not form part 
of it's total income of the A.Y. 2025-26?

context.common_stem:
(D)  ` 3,49,960 
(2 Marks) 
Integrated Case Study - III 
Seva Niketan, a charitable trust registered under section 12AB runs an 
education institution and a hospital for treatment of persons suffering from 
mental disorder solely for philanthropic purposes. The trust has furnished the 
following information: 
5 
SUGGESTED ANSWERS 
FINAL EXAMINATION: JANUARY 2026

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
EXEMPTION IN RESPECT OF INCOME OF CERTAIN UNIVERSITIES, EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, HOSPITALS, MEDICAL INSTITUTIONS ETC.
Exemption for Certain Educational and Medical Institutions

exclusion: Institutions operating for profit
Hospitals or educational institutions exceeding the financial receipt threshold without government financing
inclusion: Universities wholly or substantially financed by the government
Hospitals existing solely for philanthropic purposes and substantially financed by the government
Educational and medical institutions with aggregate annual receipts not exceeding five crore rupees
descriptor.definition: Specific universities, educational institutions, hospitals, and medical institutions are exempt from income tax on their total income if they are wholly or substantially financed by the government, or if their aggregate annual receipts do not exceed five crore rupees. An institution is considered substantially financed when government grants exceed 50 percent of its total receipts including donations during the tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes government-backed or smaller scale medical and educational bodies from standard commercial enterprises and general trusts.

path.name: Return of Income of Charitable Trusts and Institutions [Section 139(4A)]
Return Of Income Of Charitable Trusts And Institutions [Section 139(4A)]

exclusion: Trusts whose gross income before exemptions stays at or below the basic exemption limit
inclusion: Trusts holding property for charitable or religious obligations
Institutions receiving voluntary contributions
descriptor.definition: Every person in receipt of income held under a trust for charitable or religious purposes must furnish a return of income if total income before exemptions exceeds the basic exemption limit. Representative assessees must file these returns voluntarily within prescribed timelines.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from individual returns by computing income thresholds prior to applying statutory charitable exemptions under sections 11 and 12.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO INCOME OF POLITICAL PARTIES AND ELECTORAL TRUSTS [SECTION 12]
Special Provisions Relating to Income of Political Parties and Electoral Trusts

exclusion: Income failing to meet record-keeping and audit criteria
Donations accepted outside prescribed banking or electronic channels beyond permitted limits
inclusion: Income from house property of political parties
Voluntary contributions received by political parties and electoral trusts
Capital gains and income from other sources for political bodies
descriptor.definition: Political parties and electoral trusts receive tax exemptions on specific categories of income such as house property, other sources, capital gains, and voluntary contributions. To claim this exemption, entities must maintain proper books of accounts, record large contributions, audit accounts via a chartered accountant, and file required statutory returns.
nearby_distinctions: Exempts political and electoral income only upon strict compliance with transparency and record-keeping mandates, unlike standard trust income.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: payments made to the Government
payments made to specified banking companies or co-operative societies
inclusion: cash payments exceeding 1 crore rupees generally
cash payments exceeding 20 lakhs rupees for non-filers of returns
descriptor.definition: Banking institutions, co-operative banks, and post offices must deduct tax at source on cash withdrawals exceeding specific statutory thresholds during a previous year. Higher tax rates and lower withdrawal limits apply to recipients who have failed to file income tax returns for the preceding three assessment years.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard payment-based TDS provisions by targeting physical cash withdrawals from bank accounts based on aggregate annual volume.

path.name: Chapter 2: Incomes which do not form part of Total Income

exclusion: Incomes subject to deductions under Chapter VIII prior to final total income computation
inclusion: Incomes specified under Schedules II to VI
Total income of specified persons under Schedule VII
descriptor.definition: Exempt incomes under section 11 and its schedules are completely excluded from the computation of total income. In contrast, deductions under Chapter VIII are first included in the gross total income and subsequently deducted.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes complete exclusion from total income via exemptions versus subsequent subtraction through Chapter VIII deductions

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR REGISTERED NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATION
Special Provisions for Registered Non-Profit Organization

exclusion: Commercial business entities operating for profit
Private trusts claiming public charitable exemptions solely by status
inclusion: Trusts, societies, and section 8 companies
Public trusts with general public beneficiaries
Private trusts formed for individual or family convenience
descriptor.definition: Non-profit organizations are typically established as trusts, societies, or section 8 companies to carry out charitable or religious activities. A trust involves an obligation where a trustee holds and manages property according to a trust deed for the benefit of ascertainable or unascertainable beneficiaries.
nearby_distinctions: Public trusts qualify for special charitable exemption regimes, whereas private trusts do not qualify merely by being constituted as a trust.

exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
descriptor.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

path.name: Fee for default in furnishing return of income [Section 234F]
Fee for default in furnishing return of income [Section 234F]

exclusion: Timely filed returns complying with prescribed deadlines
inclusion: Default in furnishing return of income within the time limit under section 139(1)
descriptor.definition: A monetary fee is levied when a person mandated to file an income return fails to complete the submission within the specified statutory time limit. A tiered fee structure applies based on whether total income crosses the statutory threshold amount.
nearby_distinctions: Represents a specific penal fee for filing delays, distinct from substantive tax liabilities or interest calculations.

path.name: Chapter 8: Deductions from Gross Total Income
General Provisions of Chapter VIII Deductions

exclusion: Incomes exempt under section 11
Carrying forward negative income or losses caused by deductions
inclusion: Deductions from gross total income
Restrictions on aggregate deductions exceeding gross total income
descriptor.definition: Chapter VIII permits deductions from gross total income to compute total income, subject to the overall limitation that aggregate deductions cannot exceed the gross total income itself. These provisions prevent double counting by prohibiting member-level deductions for AOP or BOI shares already benefiting from specific sections, and restrict duplicate claims of Part C deductions under alternative provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from section 11 exemptions which completely exclude specified incomes from entering the computation process.

textbook_references.download_url: https://resource.cdn.icai.org/94202CHP-8 Deduction from Gross Total Income.pdf

exclusion: Incomes explicitly exempt from charge under statutory provisions
inclusion: Total income of persons specified under the Act
Tax rates specified by the Finance Act or Income-tax Act, 2025
descriptor.definition: Income-tax is charged on the total income of every person for the tax year at the rates prescribed by the annual Finance Act or the Income-tax Act, 2025. This charging provision forms the foundational basis from which any tax liability legally originates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from computational provisions by serving strictly as the legal origin of tax liability.

path.name: Residuary Scope of Income from Other Sources

exclusion: Income specifically falling under salaries, house property, business or profession, or capital gains
inclusion: Receipts failing to fall under other specific heads of income
Profits and gains not covered elsewhere
descriptor.definition: Income from other sources functions as a residuary tax head capturing all taxable profits, gains, or receipts that fail to qualify under any preceding specific head. It applies to any item chargeable under the Act that does not find a precise classification within other established income categories.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike specific heads with strict categorization criteria, this acts as a catch-all for remaining taxable items.

path.name: Chapter 8: Deductions from Gross Total Income
DEDUCTIONS IN RESPECT OF OTHER INCOME
Deduction in respect of interest on deposits

exclusion: Interest derived from bank accounts held on behalf of a firm or AOP/BOI
Deductions under the default tax regime
inclusion: Interest on savings accounts with banks, co-operatives, or post offices
Interest on time deposits for senior citizens
descriptor.definition: Resident individuals and Hindu Undivided Families who opt out of the default tax regime can claim a deduction for interest earned on specific bank, co-operative society, or post office deposits. Senior citizens enjoy higher deduction limits covering all types of deposits, whereas non-senior individuals and Hindu Undivided Families are restricted to savings account interest.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from investment deductions by applying strictly to passive interest earnings rather than active financial contributions.

textbook_references.download_url: https://resource.cdn.icai.org/94202CHP-8 Deduction from Gross Total Income.pdf

path.name: Chapter 2: Incomes which do not form part of Total Income
RESTRICTIONS ON ALLOWABILITY OF EXPENDITURE [SECTION 14 READ WITH RULE 14]

exclusion: Expenditures incurred solely in relation to taxable income streams
inclusion: Direct expenditure relating to exempt income
Indirect expenditure computed as a percentage of investment balances under prescribed rules
descriptor.definition: Expenditures incurred in relation to income that does not form part of total income are disallowed as deductions. This disallowance applies regardless of whether the corresponding exempt income was actually accrued, arisen, or received during the tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between deductible business expenses tied to taxable revenues and statutory disallowances mandated for expenses linked to tax-free receipts

path.name: Particulars to be furnished with return of income in case of an assessee engaged in business or profession [Section 139(6A)]
Particulars to be furnished with return of income in case of an assessee engaged in business or profession [Section 139(6A)]

exclusion: Non-business individual disclosures such as general personal bank accounts or credit cards
inclusion: Tax audit report referred to in section 44AB
Location and style of principal place of business and branches
Names and addresses of partners
Names of members and profit shares in an association of persons or body of individuals
descriptor.definition: Taxpayers engaged in any business or profession must submit specific commercial particulars with their return, including statutory audit reports and principal operational locations. Additionally, they must disclose names, addresses, and profit-sharing ratios of all partners or association members.
nearby_distinctions: Specifically targets commercial entities and professionals requiring structural disclosures like partnership details and audit reports, unlike general asset disclosures under section 139(6).

path.name: Chapter 6: Income of Other Persons included in Assessee’s Total Income
LIABILITY OF PERSON IN RESPECT OF INCOME INCLUDED IN THE INCOME OF ANOTHER PERSON [SECTION 100]
Liability for Tax on Clubbed Income

exclusion: tax liabilities unrelated to the specific income clubbed under Sections 96 through 99
inclusion: tax recovery enforcement notices served directly on asset transferees
joint and several tax liabilities for co-transferees of gifted assets
descriptor.definition: While clubbed income is taxed in the hands of the transferor, a notice of demand can legally be served upon the transferee to recover the portion of tax attributable to that specific clubbed income. If the underlying asset is held jointly by multiple transferees, such persons assume joint and several liability for the corresponding tax payment.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary assessment liability (on the transferor) from secondary recovery enforcement power (against the transferee holding the asset).

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: employer-paid tax on non-monetary perquisites and section 194N deductions from being deemed income received
inclusion: treating deducted tax amounts as income received for computation purposes
allocating tax credit to deductees or alternate assessable persons based on reporting rules
descriptor.definition: Tax deducted at source and foreign tax credits are legally deemed to be income received for total income computation, subject to explicit statutory exceptions. Tax remitted to the Central Government is treated as tax paid on behalf of the primary income owner, with credit governed by prescribed administrative rules.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from primary deduction mechanics by establishing post-deduction tax accounting, income grossing rules, and credit attribution frameworks.

path.name: Chapter 2: Incomes which do not form part of Total Income
INCOMES NOT INCLUDED IN TOTAL INCOME [SECTION 11]

exclusion: Income from land not used for agricultural purposes
Income from buildings located in specified urban areas failing rural land revenue criteria
inclusion: Rent or revenue derived from land situated in India and used for agricultural purposes
Income derived from agricultural operations and standard market-preparation processes
Income from farm buildings occupied by cultivators or receivers of rent under specified conditions
descriptor.definition: Agricultural income is entirely excluded from central income-tax due to constitutional limitations on central taxing powers. The statutory definition encompasses rent or revenue from Indian agricultural land, income derived from agricultural operations and processing, and income from specific rural farm buildings.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates between direct cultivation returns, land rents, and associated farm building usage versus non-agricultural commercial land uses

path.name: Chapter 6: Income of Other Persons included in Assessee’s Total Income
Inclusion of Loss in Income Computation

exclusion: gains or losses explicitly insulated by specific statutory deductions outside clubbing frameworks
inclusion: computational inclusion of transferable business or property losses in assessee's aggregate income
descriptor.definition: For the purposes of clubbing provisions, the statutory definition of income incorporates negative financial results or losses. Consequently, any specified loss arising from transferred assets or arrangements must be factored directly into the total income computation of the individual.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes tax computation under clubbing from general understandings of income by ensuring deficit figures are treated symmetrically with positive earnings.

exclusion: Receipts by the Government, banking companies, post office savings banks, or co-operative banks
Transactions of the nature referred to in section 269SS
Cash withdrawals by any person from a bank, co-operative bank, or post office savings bank
inclusion: Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in aggregate from a person in a day
Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in respect of a single transaction
Receipts relating to one event or occasion from a person
descriptor.definition: Receiving an amount of 2,00,000 rupees or more is prohibited unless executed through account payee instruments, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. This restriction applies to daily aggregates from a single person, single transactions, or transactions relating to a single event or occasion.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269SS which specifically targets loans, deposits, and immovable property advances
Applies a higher monetary threshold of 2,00,000 rupees compared to the 20,000 rupees limit under Section 269SS and Section 269T

path.name: Chapter 6: Income of Other Persons included in Assessee’s Total Income
Clubbing of Income Introduction and Transfer of Income without Asset

exclusion: transfers where both asset and income are legally transferred permanently without retained rights
inclusion: income transferred without transferring the asset
revocable or irrevocable income transfers
descriptor.definition: Clubbing provisions include the income of another person in the assessee's total income to prevent tax avoidance via asset or income diversions. Specifically, if any person transfers income from an asset without transferring the underlying asset itself, such income is taxed in the transferor's hands regardless of whether the transfer is revocable or irrevocable.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard taxation of an assessee's own income by shifting tax liability to the original benefactor under specific anti-avoidance rules.

path.name: Specified class or classes of persons to be exempted from filing return of income [Section 139(1C)]
Specified Class Or Classes Of Persons To Be Exempted From Filing Return Of Income [Section 139(1C)]

exclusion: Taxpayers earning other Indian-sourced incomes outside the specified exemptions
inclusion: Non-corporate non-residents with fund income in IFSC
Foreign companies with fund income in IFSC
descriptor.definition: The Central Government may exempt specific classes of taxpayers from filing a return of income to minimize compliance burdens. This includes non-corporate non-residents and foreign companies whose sole Indian income derives from specified International Financial Services Centre investment funds subject to tax deduction at source.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard filing requirements by granting total exemption from submitting returns under section 139(1) via executive notification.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
Taxation Regime of Special Entities and Non-Profit Organisations

exclusion: Standard corporate entities not falling under special exemptions
General individual taxpayers
inclusion: Charitable and religious institutions
Educational and medical organizations
Political parties and electoral trusts
Securitization and business trusts
Investment funds
descriptor.definition: This chapter covers the income tax treatment and exemptions applicable to educational and medical organizations, charitable or religious trusts, political parties, electoral trusts, and special entities like securitization trusts, business trusts, and investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Specific provisions govern registered non-profit organizations and special investment vehicles through dedicated sections and schedules.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general commercial entities and special tax-exempt non-profit or pass-through vehicles.

path.name: DETERMINATION OF TAX IN CERTAIN SPECIAL CASES [CHAPTER XII]
Special Tax Rates for Non-Residents and Foreign Companies

exclusion: General business profits subject to slab or standard corporate tax rates
inclusion: Dividends from units in an IFSC or other entities
Interest received from government or Indian concerns in foreign currency
Distributed income of business trusts from special purpose vehicles
descriptor.definition: Specific types of income earned by non-corporate non-residents and foreign companies, such as dividends, interest, and royalties, are taxed at specialized flat statutory rates. These rates vary based on the nature of the borrowing, listing status, and the type of financial instrument utilized.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes concessional withholding tax rates on foreign borrowings from general domestic interest taxation

path.name: MODE OF TAKING OR ACCEPTING CERTAIN LOANS, DEPOSITS AND SPECIFIED SUM [SECTION 269SS]
Mode Of Taking Or Accepting Certain Loans, Deposits And Specified Sum [Section 269Ss]

exclusion: Transactions involving the Government or banking companies
Transactions where parties derive income solely from agriculture
Transactions where neither party has taxable income
inclusion: Loans or deposits of 20,000 rupees or more
Unpaid earlier loans or deposits aggregating 20,000 rupees or more
Specified sums receivable for immovable property transfers
descriptor.definition: Accepting loans, deposits, or specified sums equal to or exceeding 20,000 rupees must be executed through account payee cheques, bank drafts, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. Specified sums include advance monies receivable regarding immovable property transfers, subject to specific institutional exemptions and agricultural conditions.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269T which governs loan repayments rather than acceptance
Differs from Section 269ST which governs general daily or transactional cash receipt limits

path.name: Chapter 6: Income of Other Persons included in Assessee’s Total Income
INCOME OF OTHER PERSONS INCLUDIBLE IN TOTAL INCOME OF AN INDIVIDUAL
Remuneration from Concern with Substantial Interest

exclusion: remuneration solely attributable to the technical or professional knowledge and qualifications of the spouse
inclusion: salary, commission, or fees paid to spouse from a concern with individual's substantial interest
descriptor.definition: Spousal remuneration received in cash or kind from a concern in which the individual holds a substantial interest is clubbed with the individual's total income. A substantial interest exists if equity voting power or profit entitlement is at least twenty percent, though an exemption applies if the remuneration is solely due to the spouse's professional or technical qualifications.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general asset transfers by focusing specifically on employment or service-based compensation derived from entities influenced by the taxpayer.

path.name: OTHER PROVISIONS RELATED TO VARIOUS ENTITIES
Taxation of Income from Global Depository Receipts for Resident Employees

exclusion: Deductions under general provisions when gross total income consists solely of GDR dividend income
inclusion: Resident employee dividend income from specified GDRs
Long-term capital gains from GDR transfers
descriptor.definition: Resident employees of specified knowledge-based Indian companies or their subsidiaries are taxed at concessional rates on dividends and long-term capital gains derived from foreign currency Global Depository Receipts. Gross total income calculations exclude standard deductions against such specific foreign currency depository receipt incomes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes specialized concessional taxation of employee stock-option-linked GDRs from standard capital gains and dividend tax regimes

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: employer-paid tax on non-monetary perquisites
tax deducted under section 194N on cash withdrawals
inclusion: all sums deducted under Chapter XVII TDS provisions
eligible foreign income tax deductions allowed as credit
descriptor.definition: All taxes deducted under statutory provisions and eligible foreign tax deductions are treated as income received when computing an assessee's total income. Specific statutory outflows, such as non-monetary perquisite taxes paid by employers and certain cash withdrawal deductions, are excluded from this income-inclusion rule.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from gross cash receipts by legally mandating the addition of withheld tax amounts back into the taxpayer's computed income base.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Credit for tax deducted at source [Section 199]
Credit For Tax Deducted At Source [Section 199]

exclusion: Direct payment of tax without statutory deduction mechanism
Credit given without matching deductor information
inclusion: Credit given to the deductee based on deductor reporting
Proportional credit across multiple years if income is assessable across years
descriptor.definition: Tax deducted at source and paid to the Central Government is treated as tax payment on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made or the owner of the relevant asset. Rule 37BA dictates that credit is given to the actual deductee or an alternate assessable person based on deductor information, aligned with the assessment year of the income.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 200 duty to deposit, focusing instead on granting tax credit to the income earner.

path.name: PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]
PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]

exclusion: Unauthorized third parties lacking specific legal designation or valid power of attorney
inclusion: Assessee himself for individuals under normal circumstances
Authorized power-of-attorney holders during absence or incapacity
Managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals for companies
descriptor.definition: Statutory provisions explicitly designate which individuals possess the legal authority to sign and verify income tax returns on behalf of different assessee types. Depending on circumstances such as absence, mental incapacity, winding up, or corporate insolvency, specific representatives like power-of-attorney holders, managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals are authorized.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on the legal competence to sign and authenticate return documents, separate from the actual preparation or computation of income.

path.name: Civil Court Powers and Inquiry Authority of Tax Officials (Continuation)

exclusion: Arbitrary extra-judicial actions unaligned with formal civil procedure principles
inclusion: Issuing commissions
Compelling production of books of account
Investigating suspected concealed income prior to formal proceedings
descriptor.definition: Specific income-tax authorities possess the same powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure when handling matters such as discovery, enforcing attendance, and compelling document production. These powers can be invoked for inquiry or investigation purposes even when no active proceeding is pending if tax concealment is suspected.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general survey or search actions by strictly adopting judicial trial powers like examination on oath and discovery under civil procedural rules.

path.name: OBLIGATION TO FURNISH STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL TRANSACTION OR REPORTABLE ACCOUNT [SECTION 285BA]
Obligation To Furnish Statement Of Financial Transaction Or Reportable Account [Section 285Ba]

exclusion: Entities outside the designated categories of reporting persons and financial institutions defined under the section
inclusion: Transactions of purchase, sale, or exchange of goods, property, or rights
Transactions for rendering services or under works contracts
Transactions involving investments made, expenditures incurred, or loans taken
descriptor.definition: Specified entities, including reporting financial institutions, registrars, and government offices maintaining books or records, must furnish statements regarding specified financial transactions or reportable accounts to income-tax authorities. These prescribed transactions encompass property purchases, service rendering, works contracts, investments, expenditures, and loan takings.
nearby_distinctions: Imposes broad financial transaction reporting obligations across designated institutional entities, whereas Section 285B is strictly confined to film producers and specified media/event activities

path.name: Civil Court Powers and Inquiry Authority of Tax Officials

exclusion: Arbitrary extra-judicial actions unaligned with formal civil procedure principles
inclusion: Issuing commissions
Compelling production of books of account
Investigating suspected concealed income prior to formal proceedings
descriptor.definition: Specific income-tax authorities possess the same powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure when handling matters such as discovery, enforcing attendance, and compelling document production. These powers can be invoked for inquiry or investigation purposes even when no active proceeding is pending if tax concealment is suspected.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general survey or search actions by strictly adopting judicial trial powers like examination on oath and discovery under civil procedural rules.

path.name: Chapter 19: Provisions to Counteract Unethical Tax Practices
Penalties for Foreign Income and Asset Non-Compliance

exclusion: Low-value bank accounts and minor aggregate asset holdings within statutory monetary limits
inclusion: Penalties equal to three times the tax computed
Fixed sum penalties for omission of foreign asset information
descriptor.definition: Assessees face financial penalties amounting to multiples of computed tax or fixed monetary fines for failing to disclose foreign assets or file required returns. Specific monetary thresholds and asset types provide exemptions from these penalties under defined conditions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from prosecution as these represent administrative financial sanctions rather than criminal imprisonment offenses.

path.name: Chapter 20: Tax Audit and Ethical Compliances
PENALTY FOR FAILURE TO FURNISH TAX AUDIT REPORT [SECTION 271B]
Penalty for Failure to Furnish Tax Audit Report under Section 271B

exclusion: Instances where a valid reasonable cause for default is successfully proved under section 273B
inclusion: Penalties for non-compliance with tax audit submission mandates
Aggregation rules for multiple business turnovers when evaluating thresholds
descriptor.definition: Failure to complete accounts audits or submit required tax audit reports under section 44AB attracts a monetary penalty levied by the Assessing Officer. The penalty amount is calculated as a specified percentage of total turnover or gross receipts, subject to a statutory ceiling, unless a reasonable cause is proven.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general income tax default penalties by specifically targeting the omission of mandatory tax audit reports.

path.name: PROVISIONAL ATTACHMENT TO PROTECT THE INTEREST OF THE REVENUE [SECTION 281B]
Provisional Attachment To Protect The Interest Of The Revenue [Section 281B]

exclusion: Extensions exceeding a total period of two years or sixty days after assessment/reassessment, whichever is later
inclusion: Provisional attachment of property during pending assessment or reassessment
Attachments for anticipated penalty under section 271AAD exceeding two crore rupees
Revocation of attachment upon furnishing a scheduled bank guarantee
descriptor.definition: Assessing officers are empowered to provisionally attach an assessee's property during pending assessment, reassessment, or penalty proceedings with high-ranking administrative approval to protect revenue interests. Such attachments remain valid for six months, extendable up to two years or sixty days post-assessment, but can be revoked if the assessee furnishes a scheduled bank guarantee.
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a precautionary attachment mechanism during active proceedings, distinct from Section 281 which retroactively voids fraudulent transfers

path.name: Chapter 20: Tax Audit and Ethical Compliances
Distinction and Application of Form 3CA and Form 3CB

exclusion: General financial statements audit reports independent of tax return annexures
inclusion: Tax audit reporting for entities audited under separate laws using Form 3CA
Tax audit reporting for unaudited entities using Form 3CB
descriptor.definition: Form 3CA is utilized for tax audits when an entity's accounts are already audited under another statute, requiring the tax auditor to annex those existing reports and opine solely on Form 3CD particulars. Conversely, Form 3CB applies when no other statutory audit is required, obligating the tax auditor to express an independent opinion on the financial statements' true and fair view alongside the particulars.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between entities with pre-existing statutory audits relying on Form 3CA and entities requiring complete financial statement opinions via Form 3CB.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward

exclusion: Inter-source set-off against casual income like lotteries and betting
Set-off of long-term capital loss against short-term capital gain
inclusion: Set-off of loss from one house property against another house property
Set-off of loss from one non-speculation business against another non-speculation business
descriptor.definition: Losses incurred from any source under a specific head of income can generally be offset against income from another source under the same head during the same tax year. However, certain restrictions apply to specific categories such as capital losses, speculation business, specified activities, and casual winnings.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes source-level adjustments within a single income head from inter-head adjustments across different income heads.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward

exclusion: Setting off capital gains losses against any other head
Setting off business losses against salary income
inclusion: Adjusting business losses against other heads except salaries
Setting off house property loss up to specified monetary limits against other heads under the default regime
descriptor.definition: Losses computed under one head of income may be adjusted against income under another head within the same tax year, excluding capital gains. Specific restrictions apply, such as business losses not being adjustable against salary income and house property losses being capped or restricted depending on the tax regime.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes inter-head adjustments from inter-source adjustments restricted strictly within the same head.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]

exclusion: transactions subject to tax deduction under other provisions where section 194Q priority rules apply
transactions liable to TCS under specific sub-sections of section 206C
inclusion: sum paid or credited for purchasing goods exceeding 50 lakhs rupees in a previous year

explanations inserted within one year to clarify scope
