descriptor.definition: The time of supply indicates the exact point when the liability to pay goods and services tax arises for intra-State or inter-State transactions. While the tax liability crystallizes at this specific time, the actual payment can be made by the prescribed due dates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the payment of tax due date which occurs later in the filing cycle

path.name: PLACE OF SUPPLY OF GOODS OTHER THAN SUPPLY OF GOODS IMPORTED INTO, OR EXPORTED FROM INDIA [SECTION 10]
Place of Supply of Domestic Goods

exclusion: imported goods cross-border transactions
exported goods leaving India
inclusion: terminating points of goods movement
third-party principal business locations
unregistered consumer invoice addresses
descriptor.definition: Statutory rules determine the location where domestic goods are supplied based on physical movement, third-party delivery directions, or stationary delivery. For unregistered recipients, specific invoicing address criteria apply when movement is absent.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard movement-based delivery rules from bill-to-ship-to triangular arrangements where a third party's principal place of business dictates the outcome.

path.name: CHANGE IN RATE OF TAX IN RESPECT OF SUPPLY OF GOODS OR SERVICES [SECTION 14]
Time of Supply under Change in Rate of Tax

exclusion: Standard forward charge time of supply without rate changes
Reverse charge mechanics
inclusion: Supplies made before tax rate change
Supplies made after tax rate change
descriptor.definition: When tax rates change, the time of supply overrides standard provisions to depend strictly on the chronological relationship between the date of supply, invoice issuance, and payment receipt. Specific permutations dictate whether the supply occurs before or after the rate revision.
nearby_distinctions: Applies specialized ordering rules based on rate change timing rather than standard invoice or payment precedence

exclusion: Central and State Government subsidies
Discounts recorded on invoices or linked via pre-supply agreements with reversed ITC
inclusion: Separate third-party levies other than specified GST laws
Recipient liabilities paid by supplier
Delayed payment interest, late fees, and penalties
descriptor.definition: The taxable value of a supply equals its transaction value when parties are unrelated and price is the sole consideration. Additions such as incidental expenses, recipient liabilities, non-government subsidies, and taxes are included, while qualifying pre- and post-supply discounts are excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts mandatory additions to the price with permitted exclusions like conditional discounts and government subsidies.

path.name: PLACE OF SUPPLY OF SERVICES WHERE LOCATION OF SUPPLIER OF SERVICE AND THE LOCATION OF THE RECIPIENT OF SERVICE IS IN INDIA [SECTION 12]
Place of Supply of Services Within India

exclusion: cross-border import of services
cross-border export of services
inclusion: architect and interior decorator services
hotel and boat lodging accommodations
event organization at immovable properties
descriptor.definition: Domestic service rules establish the place of supply based on recipient registration status or specific performance ties to immovable properties and venues. Properties spanning multiple territories require proportional value allocation.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes general B2B and B2C recipient-location rules from location-specific performance rules governing immovable property and related events.

path.name: INTRA-STATE SUPPLY [SECTION 8 OF THE IGST ACT]

exclusion: Special Economic Zone developer or unit supplies
imported goods before customs clearance
inclusion: supplies within the same state
branch establishments treated as distinct persons
descriptor.definition: Intra-state supply occurs when both the supplier and the place of supply are located within the same state or union territory, attracting CGST and SGST. Specific transactions involving Special Economic Zone units, uncrossed imports, or international tourists are legally excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard local state-contained transactions from excluded categories like SEZ supplies that default to inter-state treatment despite occurring locally.

path.name: COMPOSITION LEVY [SECTION 10 OF THE CGST ACT]

exclusion: Taxpayers engaged in inter-State outward supplies of goods or services
Suppliers of non-taxable goods or services
inclusion: Registered persons with preceding financial year aggregate turnover meeting statutory limits
Manufacturers, restaurant service providers, and other eligible suppliers
descriptor.definition: Eligible registered taxpayers with an aggregate turnover below a specified statutory threshold in the preceding financial year may opt to pay tax at a concessional rate calculated on their state or union territory turnover. This scheme restricts outward inter-State supplies and limits the supply of services alongside specific manufacturing or catering conditions.
terminology: Turnover in State or Union territory
nearby_distinctions: Composition levy offers a simplified tax calculation at lower rates based on state turnover instead of standard rates, subject to strict eligibility constraints.

exclusion: taxable supplies subject to standard or reduced positive rates
supplies outside statutory definitions
inclusion: supplies attracting nil rate of tax
wholly exempt goods or services
non-taxable supplies including specified petroleum products and alcoholic liquor
descriptor.definition: An exempt supply comprises any goods, services, or both attracting a nil tax rate, full exemption, or non-taxable status under governing statutes. This classification includes items and services not leviable to tax under the primary legislative acts.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes between wholly exempt items and non-taxable supplies which are both subsumed under exempt supply definitions

path.name: POWER TO GRANT EXEMPTION FROM TAX [SECTION 11 OF THE CGST ACT/SECTION 6 OF THE IGST ACT]
Power to Grant Exemption from Tax

exclusion: collection of tax in excess of effective rates on absolute exemptions
exemptions granted without council recommendation
inclusion: general exemptions via notification
special orders for exceptional circumstances
explanations inserted within one year to clarify scope
descriptor.definition: The Government may issue notifications or special orders on council recommendations to exempt specific goods or services from whole or part of taxes in the public interest. Registered suppliers must not collect tax exceeding the effective rate on absolutely exempted supplies.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes general notifications applied broadly from special orders issued for exceptional individual cases

path.name: GST Foundation and Territorial Charging Mechanism

exclusion: Supplies outside the charging provisions of the respective tax statutes
inclusion: Intra-State supplies of goods or services
Inter-State supplies of goods or services
descriptor.definition: The charge of goods and services tax is triggered by the taxable event of supply, drawing its legislative power from the Constitution of India. Intra-State supplies attract central tax and state or union territory tax, whereas inter-State supplies attract integrated tax.
nearby_distinctions: Intra-State supply is governed by CGST and SGST/UTGST based on supplier location and place of supply, whereas inter-State supply attracts IGST.

exclusion: processed or branded items outside the exemption notification
taxable manufactured goods
inclusion: unbranded or unpackaged staple food items
fresh milk, eggs, and curd
fresh vegetables and specified raw agricultural produce
descriptor.definition: Specified everyday consumption items are exempted from the whole of tax under statutory exemption powers. These include essential public consumption products notified under governing tax legislation.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes raw or unpackaged essential food items from processed commercial goods subject to standard taxation

path.name: LIST OF SERVICES EXEMPT FROM TAX
List of Services Exempt From Tax

exclusion: renting of rooms with daily charges meeting or exceeding specified monetary thresholds
renting of commercial shops exceeding monthly rental limits
inclusion: charitable activities by registered entities
religious ceremonies and eligible renting of religious precincts
training or coaching in arts, culture, or sports by specified entities
descriptor.definition: Specific categories of services rendered by qualified entities, such as charitable activities and religious ceremonies, are exempted wholly from central tax under designated notifications. Certain monetary thresholds apply to determine the applicability of exemptions on renting properties and premises.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes general commercial service providers from charitable trusts and religious institutions qualifying for specific service exemptions

path.name: RULES FOR VALUATION OF SUPPLY OF GOODS AND/OR SERVICES

exclusion: Standard arm-length transactions where price is the sole monetary consideration under section 15(1)
inclusion: Barter transactions
Part-exchange arrangements
Supplies between distinct establishments or related entities
descriptor.definition: Valuation rules determine taxable values when consideration is not wholly in money or when transactions occur between distinct or related persons. The process follows a hierarchical methodology starting with open market value and falling back to like-kind quality or computed cost rules.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates default transaction pricing from sequential fallback valuation rules applied during non-monetary or related-party transactions.

path.name: POWER NOT TO RECOVER GOODS AND SERVICES TAX NOT LEVIED OR SHORT- LEVIED AS A RESULT OF GENERAL PRACTICE
Power Not to Recover Tax Not Levied or Short-Levied Due to General Practice

exclusion: tax non-payment resulting from isolated taxpayer errors unsupported by general trade practice
adjustments executed without council recommendation
inclusion: supplies where central tax was not levied due to prevalent general practice
supplies charged at a lower rate in accordance with established industry customs
descriptor.definition: The Government may direct that uncollected or short-levied tax need not be paid if a specific industry practice of non-levy or lower levy was generally prevalent. This relief mechanism protects taxpayers who followed widespread customary practices in good faith upon council recommendations.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes regular statutory exemptions from retroactive relief granted specifically for widespread industry misinterpretations or customary practices

exclusion: Non-ad-valorem levies
Transactions where price is not the sole consideration
inclusion: Goods and services supply valuations
CGST, SGST, UTGST, and IGST computation frameworks
descriptor.definition: Fiscal statutes compute tax liability on an ad-valorem basis using a prescribed valuation mechanism for goods and services. The transaction value between unrelated parties acts as the default taxable base under statutory valuation provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard transaction value pricing from specialized rule-based valuation methods used when standard criteria fail.
instrument_references: Chapter IV of the CGST Rules, 2017

path.name: Extent and Commencement of GST Law

exclusion: Territories outside the specified sovereign boundaries of India
inclusion: Territory of India under Article 1 of the Constitution
Maritime zones including territorial waters and exclusive economic zones
descriptor.definition: The tax statutes extend to the entire territory of India, encompassing its territorial waters, seabed, subsoil, continental shelf, exclusive economic zone, and designated airspace. Each respective state or union territory enactment applies within its defined geographical boundaries.
nearby_distinctions: CGST and IGST extend pan-India, whereas UTGST applies exclusively to specific union territories without legislatures.
instrument_references: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and other Maritime Zones Act, 1976

exclusion: tax computation rules
input tax credit claiming mechanics
inclusion: goods consumption locations
service delivery tracking
cross-state service flows
descriptor.definition: The place of supply identifies the consumption jurisdiction for destination-based taxation, establishing where tax revenue must accrue. It resolves complexities caused by the intangible nature of services, mobile recipients, and alterable delivery formats.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the physical location of the supplier or billing address by focusing strictly on the ultimate place of consumption.

path.name: Relevant Definitions for Place of Supply

exclusion: valuation mechanisms
time of supply triggers
inclusion: conveyance classifications
distinct person establishment rules
foreign exchange receipt conditions
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions establish legal boundaries for continuous passenger journeys, international trade movements, and organizational establishments. These terms govern the interpretation of cross-border and multi-location transactions under the GST framework.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between a regular place of business and a fixed establishment based on the sufficiency of human and technical resources.

exclusion: immovable property statutory rules for port operations
inclusion: e-commerce delivery address recording
port wagon haulage and unloading services
descriptor.definition: Administrative clarifications resolve specific compliance ambiguities regarding e-commerce deliveries to unregistered persons and port cargo handling services. Cargo operations ancillary to port handling are classified under general service rules rather than immovable property rules.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes port cargo handling ancillary operations from direct immovable property leases or construction services.

path.name: SUPPLIES IN TERRITORIAL WATERS [SECTION 9 OF THE IGST ACT]

exclusion: high seas supplies beyond territorial water limits not captured by baseline rules
inclusion: bunker fuel supplies to vessels
ship stores provided offshore
descriptor.definition: Legal fictions assign supplier locations or places of supply occurring within territorial waters to the nearest coastal baseline state or union territory. This ensures every maritime supply links correctly to a destination-based administrative jurisdiction.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes unassigned offshore maritime locations from land jurisdictions by legally anchoring them to the nearest coastal baseline point.
instrument_references: Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone and Other Maritime Zones Act 1976

exclusion: Time of supply rules for services
Tax rate change provisions
inclusion: Forward charge supply rules for goods
Reverse charge supply rules for goods
descriptor.definition: The time of supply for goods is determined as the earliest of the invoice issue date, the last date required for invoice issuance, or the date of payment receipt. For reverse charge supplies, specific alternative rules apply involving goods receipt, payment entry, or thirty days post-invoice.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from service rules by prioritizing delivery milestones and different reverse charge timelines

exclusion: Unbundled individual supplies evaluated separately
inclusion: Naturally bundled supplies dependent on a principal supply
Unrelated supplies bundled together for a single price
descriptor.definition: Composite supplies involving naturally bundled elements take the tax rate of their principal supply, whereas mixed supplies not naturally bundled attract the highest applicable tax rate among their components. This mechanism ensures taxation certainty for bundled transactions combining multiple goods or services.
nearby_distinctions: Composite supplies rely on natural bundling and a principal component, while mixed supplies lack natural bundling and attract the highest tax rate.

exclusion: Time of supply rules for goods
Tax rate change provisions
inclusion: Forward charge rules for services
Reverse charge rules for services
descriptor.definition: The time of supply for services is generally determined as the earliest of the invoice issue date or payment receipt, provided the invoice is issued within the prescribed period. Under reverse charge mechanisms, it relies on payment dates or sixty days from the supplier's invoice.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from goods by incorporating the exact date of service provision and recipient book entries when standard rules fail

context.question_text: (ii) Alter the Articles of Association and pass a Special Resolution.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: Appointment and Qualification of Directors
COMPANY TO HAVE BOARD OF DIRECTORS [SECTION 149]

exclusion: Non-individual entities such as bodies corporate, firms, or association of persons
Exceeding 15 directors without passing a special resolution
inclusion: Minimum director requirements for public companies, private companies, and OPCs
Appointment of at least one woman director for prescribed classes of companies
descriptor.definition: Every company must constitute a Board of Directors consisting solely of individuals, adhering to specified minimum and maximum numerical thresholds. Public companies require a minimum of three directors, private companies two, and One Person Companies one, with an overall maximum cap of fifteen unless expanded via special resolution.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general member composition by strictly mandating individual natural persons and setting specific structural minimums and maximums.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014, Rule 3

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities

exclusion: Unilateral company policies
Non-binding operational understandings
inclusion: Written agreements
Articles or charters of separate vehicles
Terms detailing capital and resource sharing
descriptor.definition: A contractual arrangement is a binding agreement between parties, usually in writing, that dictates the terms of a joint activity. It often defines operational purpose, board appointments, voting rights, and capital contributions.
nearby_distinctions: Serves as the foundational legal and operational basis that differentiates formal joint arrangements from informal collaborations.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 3: Meetings of Board and Its Powers

exclusion: Private companies
Transactions where selling or leasing forms part of the company's ordinary business
Unauthorized capital reductions under the guise of asset sales
inclusion: Selling, leasing, or disposing of whole or substantially whole undertakings
Stipulating shareholder conditions regarding sale proceeds utilization
Protecting clean title of buyers acting in good faith
descriptor.definition: Public company boards must obtain shareholder consent via a special resolution before selling, leasing, or disposing of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking. This restriction does not apply to private companies or to sales conducted as part of a company's ordinary course of business.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general board powers under Section 179 by imposing a mandatory special resolution requirement for fundamental corporate asset disposals.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: Appointment and Qualification of Directors
APPOINTMENT OF ADDITIONAL DIRECTOR, ALTERNATE DIRECTOR, A DIRECTOR TO FILL CASUAL VACANCY AND NOMINEE DIRECTOR [SECTION 161]
Board Appointment of Additional and Alternate Directors

exclusion: Appointing any person as an additional director who failed to secure appointment at a general meeting
Extending an additional director's term beyond the due date of the annual general meeting
inclusion: Board appointment of additional directors via article authorization
Tenure limitations restricting additional directors to the date of the next annual general meeting
Alternate director appointments covering extended absences
descriptor.definition: The Board of Directors may appoint additional directors if empowered by the articles, provided the appointee has not been rejected at a general meeting, with tenure expiring at the next annual general meeting. Alternate directors may also be appointed during a director's long absence, subject to statutory and governance limitations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular shareholder-elected directors by originating from Board-level discretion authorized strictly through company articles to manage urgent management requirements.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 9: Adjudication, Special Courts, National Company Law Tribunal & National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
Serious Fraud Investigation Office Establishment and Functions

exclusion: Routine civil disputes handled through standard tribunal or court mechanisms
inclusion: Investigations assigned via Central Government order
Expert staffing across banking, taxation, and capital markets
descriptor.definition: The Serious Fraud Investigation Office is an specialized investigative body established to probe complex corporate frauds. The Central Government assigns investigations to this office based on specific statutory triggers such as registrar reports, public interest, or government requests.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard regulatory inquiries by focusing specifically on multi-disciplinary investigations of severe corporate fraud.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
INVESTIGATION INTO AFFAIRS OF COMPANY (SECTION 210 OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013)

exclusion: Preliminary inquiries handled exclusively by the local Registrar
Routine statutory audits
inclusion: Mandatory investigation orders by courts or tribunals
Suo moto investigations in public interest
Security deposit determination based on annual turnover
descriptor.definition: The Central Government may order an investigation into a company's affairs based on an inspection report, a special resolution passed by the company, public interest, or court and tribunal orders, appointing one or more inspectors for this purpose. Applicants requesting investigations may be required to deposit sliding-scale security based on company turnover, which is refundable if the process results in prosecution.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a Registrar-led inspection under Section 206 by representing a comprehensive deep-dive investigation executed by designated specialized inspectors appointed directly by the Central Government.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: Appointment and Qualification of Directors
OPTION TO ADOPT PRINCIPLE OF PROPORTIONAL REPRESENTATION FOR APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS [SECTION 163]

exclusion: Default appointment of all directors via standard simple majority voting
Failing to provide minority interest representation mechanisms in articles when opting for the system
inclusion: Adopting proportional representation via company articles for at least two-thirds of total directors
Methods including single transferable votes and cumulative voting systems
Triennial appointment cycles
descriptor.definition: Companies may adopt systems of proportional representation in their articles to ensure minority shareholders secure fair representation on the board. This mechanism overrides standard majority voting rules by utilizing single transferable votes, cumulative voting, or other transparent methods for at least two-thirds of total directors.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard simple majority voting by allowing minority voting blocks to secure proportional board representation rather than being entirely overridden.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
SECURITY FOR PAYMENT OF COSTS AND EXPENSES OF INVESTIGATION (SECTION 214 OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013)
Security For Payment Of Costs And Expenses Of Investigation

exclusion: Suo moto investigations initiated directly by the Central Government in public interest
Registrar-led routine inspections
inclusion: Deposits required for investigations ordered via special resolution or Tribunal application
Refund conditions linked to prosecution outcomes
descriptor.definition: When an investigation is ordered by the Central Government following a company special resolution or by the Tribunal upon member application, applicants may be required to deposit financial security up to twenty-five thousand rupees to cover investigation costs. This security is refunded to the applicant if the investigation ultimately results in prosecution.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from routine administrative funding because it imposes a conditional financial security requirement specifically on private applicants petitioning for investigations.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 2: Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel
APPOINTMENT OF MANAGING DIRECTOR, WHOLE TIME DIRECTOR OR MANAGER [SECTION 196]
Appointment of Managing Director, Whole Time Director or Manager [Section 196]

exclusion: Simultaneous appointment of both a managing director and a manager
inclusion: Appointments of managing directors, whole-time directors, and managers
Special resolution requirements for appointees over seventy years old
descriptor.definition: Companies can appoint a managing director, whole-time director, or manager for a maximum term of five years at a time. Re-appointments cannot occur earlier than one year before the current term expires, and appointees must meet specific age and directorial qualification criteria.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts general board appointments with statutory tenure limits and age restrictions

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
REMOVAL OF NAMES OF COMPANIES FROM THE REGISTER OF COMPANIES
Registrar Power to Remove Company Names

exclusion: Companies holding valid active operations or holding active dormant status applications
inclusion: Involuntary strike-off due to non-commencement or operational inactivity
Voluntary removal applications post-liability clearance
Regulatory body approvals for specialized corporate entities
descriptor.definition: The Registrar may initiate company strike-off procedures when an entity fails to commence business within one year, remains inactive for two consecutive financial years without dormant status, or omits mandatory incorporation filings. Alternatively, a company can voluntarily apply for name removal after extinguishing all liabilities through special resolution or high-threshold member consent.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from formal winding up or liquidation because strike-off is an administrative registry clearance rather than an insolvency resolution process.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
CIRCUMSTANCES IN WHICH COMPANY MAY BE WOUND UP BY TRIBUNAL [SECTION 271]
Circumstances In Which Company May Be Wound Up By Tribunal [Section 271]

exclusion: Petitions based solely on commercial debt defaults omitted under current framework provisions
inclusion: Winding up via special resolution
Actions harming state security or public order
Fraudulent formation or management
Consecutive five-year financial statement filing defaults
Just and equitable grounds
descriptor.definition: A company may face tribunal-ordered winding up under specific statutory grounds including special resolutions, actions against state integrity, fraudulent affairs, default in filing financial statements for five consecutive years, or when deemed just and equitable. These diverse statutory triggers ensure judicial intervention for severe corporate malfeasance or deadlock.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes objective statutory defaults like non-filing from subjective judicial assessments like the just and equitable standard.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 2: Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel
FORMS OF, AND PROCEDURE IN RELATION TO, CERTAIN APPLICATIONS [SECTION 201]
Forms Of, And Procedure In Relation To, Certain Applications [Section 201]

exclusion: Applications for managerial remuneration which no longer require prior approval
inclusion: Submitting Form MR-2 within ninety days of appointment
Mandatory English and regional newspaper publication of notices
descriptor.definition: When an appointment of an older managing director fails to secure a special resolution despite majority support, the company must apply to the Central Government. The process requires filing specific forms within ninety days along with proof of publishing general notices in local newspapers.
nearby_distinctions: Separates standard shareholder-approved appointments from government regularization procedures
instrument_references: Rule 7 of Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: Appointment and Qualification of Directors

exclusion: Directors appointed by the Tribunal or via proportional representation systems
inclusion: Removal by ordinary resolution before term expiry
Special resolution requirement for re-appointed independent directors
Special notice backed by specified voting power or paid-up share capital thresholds
descriptor.definition: Shareholders may remove a director before completing their term by passing an ordinary or special resolution after providing a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Special notices signed by qualifying members are required to propose such removal resolutions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from vacation of office occurring automatically by operation of law.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
FIRM, BODY CORPORATE OR ASSOCIATION NOT TO BE APPOINTED AS INSPECTOR (SECTION 215 OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013)
Firm, Body Corporate Or Association Not To Be Appointed As Inspector

exclusion: Individual natural persons appointed as competent inspecting authorities
inclusion: Prohibition against corporate entities or partnerships serving as inspectors
descriptor.definition: Statutory provisions expressly prohibit the appointment of any firm, body corporate, or other association of persons to act as an inspector for conducting company investigations.
nearby_distinctions: Serves as an eligibility restriction specific to the appointment of investigators, differentiating statutory inspector appointments from corporate audit firm engagements.

path.name: Chapter 14: Special Features of Audit of Banks & Non-Banking Financial Companies
Unit 2: – SPECIAL FEATURES OF AUDIT OF NON-BANKING FINANCIAL COMPANIES (NBFCs)

exclusion: Assuming business scope solely from wide formal memorandum clauses without operational verification
Omitting evaluations of recovery system efficacy
inclusion: Reviewing corporate objects and board meeting minutes
Evaluating internal control adequacy and recovery workflows
descriptor.definition: The audit engagement begins by scanning governing corporate documents, board minutes, and management strategies to accurately determine the entity's principal business activities. Auditors must independently evaluate internal control systems and recovery mechanisms to calibrate the nature, timing, and extent of subsequent substantive tests.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates foundational strategic business verification from transactional ledger testing performed later in the audit cycle.

exclusion: Direct corporate equity or unsecured bond issuance workflows
inclusion: Servicing agreements
Credit rating assignment processes
descriptor.definition: The securitization mechanism involves creating an asset pool, transferring it to a special purpose vehicle, selling structured papers, and sub-contracting asset administration back to the originator. Subsequent steps govern funds repayment, recourse conditions, and instrument credit rating.
nearby_distinctions: Represents the operational workflow pipeline from asset origination and pooling to final investor payout, distinct from static structural definitions.

exclusion: Retaining asset ownership within the originator's main financial ledgers
inclusion: Legal title transfer
Upfront payment execution
descriptor.definition: Once grouped, the asset pool is legally transferred to a specially created special purpose vehicle to ring-fence the assets from the originator's balance sheet. The SPV subsequently designs and sells structured instruments like pass-through securities or pay-through certificates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from simple custodial arrangements by executing a complete legal sale that removes assets from the originator's financial statements.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A

exclusion: Registrar petitions grounded in special resolution winding up
inclusion: Petitions by the company accompanied by a statement of affairs
Contributory petitions meeting six-month holding thresholds
Registrar petitions with prior government sanction
descriptor.definition: Authorized stakeholders including the company, contributories meeting holding duration criteria, the Registrar, or Central/State Governments may formally present a winding up petition to the Tribunal. Registrars require central government sanction after offering the company a representation opportunity.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates standing requirements across stakeholders, imposing strict holding duration rules for contributories and sanction rules for the Registrar.

exclusion: Income tax liabilities on Special Purpose Vehicles
Capital gains implications
inclusion: High stamp duty on mortgage debt in certain states
Exemption of pass through certificates from stamp duty
State-level reductions for securitized instruments
descriptor.definition: Stamp duty is a significant impediment to securitization growth in India, with mortgage debt duties reaching up to twelve percent in certain states. However, pass-through certificates are exempted because they represent receivables rather than debt, and specific states have reduced rates for securitized instruments.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Taxation issues, focusing specifically on statutory transfer levies rather than income or capital gains assessments.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 3: Meetings of Board and Its Powers

exclusion: Vacant director places when computing total board strength
Articles of association specifying a quorum lower than the statutory minimum
inclusion: Calculating quorum as one-third of total strength or two directors whichever is higher
Counting electronic participation via video conferencing towards quorum
Modifying quorum rules for compliant Section 8 companies as eight members or 25 percent whichever is less
descriptor.definition: A valid board meeting requires a quorum consisting of one-third of the total board strength or two directors, whichever is higher, with fractions rounded off as one. Directors participating through video conferencing or audio-visual means count towards the quorum unless excluded for specific items under the law.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general meeting quorums which apply to shareholder assemblies rather than board deliberations.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set B

exclusion: Treating production costs as strictly linear when capacity thresholds generate step-fixed expenses
Ignoring cost variances between bulk internal transfers and retail external sales
inclusion: Accounting for economies of scale and stepped fixed costs across output tiers
Adjusting transfer prices for cost savings such as avoided external selling or packaging expenses
Evaluating trade-offs between internal transfers, external sales, and special orders
descriptor.definition: Transfer pricing must account for varying demand levels across internal, external, and special-order channels, where production costs are influenced by economies of scale and capacity thresholds. Fluctuations in demand alter fixed overheads, variable selling expenses, and potential cost savings, which directly impact the valid transfer pricing range.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike basic capacity models, demand-level analysis explicitly integrates multi-channel order dynamics, cost scale thresholds, and specific cost-saving adjustments.

exclusion: Desynchronized cash flow servicing
Restructured debt tranches with varying maturities
inclusion: Direct claim on all securitized assets
Proportional distribution of principal prepayments
Simultaneous termination upon final payment
descriptor.definition: Pass Through Certificates represent direct proportional claims by investors on all assets securitized through a Special Purpose Vehicle, transferring all interest and principal receipts. Consequently, any principal prepayments are distributed proportionately, leading to the simultaneous termination of all securities upon final asset payment.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike Pay Through Securities, PTCs pass through all cash flows immediately and lack multi-maturity tranche restructuring.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 3: Meetings of Board and Its Powers
Powers of the Board of Directors

exclusion: Matters directed by law or articles to be exercised by shareholders in general meetings
Retrospective invalidation of prior valid board acts by subsequent general meeting regulations
inclusion: Exercising all powers authorized for the company management
Complying with memorandum, articles, and general meeting directions
Executing mandatory corporate powers via resolutions passed at board meetings
descriptor.definition: The board of directors is entitled to exercise all powers and do all acts that the company is authorized to do, subject to statutory provisions, memorandum, articles, and general meeting regulations. Specific statutory powers must be exercised exclusively through resolutions passed at duly convened board meetings.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from shareholder general meeting powers by vesting operational management in directors while retaining ultimate ownership authority with shareholders.
instrument_references: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, Rule 8

exclusion: Traditional equity shares issued directly by operating companies
inclusion: Pass-through certificates
Asset-backed debt instruments
descriptor.definition: Special purpose vehicles design and issue financial instruments tailored to the risk, return, and tenure preferences of investors using the pooled asset cash flows. These instruments typically take the form of pass-through securities or pay-through certificates.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the creation and distribution of marketable liabilities backed by cash flows, contrasting with the initial asset pooling phase.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
Taxation Regime of Special Entities and Non-Profit Organisations

exclusion: Standard corporate entities not falling under special exemptions
General individual taxpayers
inclusion: Charitable and religious institutions
Educational and medical organizations
Political parties and electoral trusts
Securitization and business trusts
Investment funds
descriptor.definition: This chapter covers the income tax treatment and exemptions applicable to educational and medical organizations, charitable or religious trusts, political parties, electoral trusts, and special entities like securitization trusts, business trusts, and investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Specific provisions govern registered non-profit organizations and special investment vehicles through dedicated sections and schedules.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general commercial entities and special tax-exempt non-profit or pass-through vehicles.

exclusion: Originator asset administration procedures
Macroeconomic problems in securitization
inclusion: Pass Through Certificates
Pay Through Securities
Stripped Securities consisting of Interest Only and Principal Only components
descriptor.definition: Securitization instruments are categorized based on maturity characteristics into Pass Through Certificates, Pay Through Securities, and Stripped Securities. These structures dictate how cash flows, principal repayments, and interest are distributed to investors through the Special Purpose Vehicle.
nearby_distinctions: Represents the broader taxonomy of financial instruments issued in securitization, encompassing specific structures like PTCs and PTS rather than administrative hurdles.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 9: Adjudication, Special Courts, National Company Law Tribunal & National Company Law Appellate Tribunal

exclusion: Non-corporate civil litigation outside statutory company laws
inclusion: Establishment of adjudication forums
Transfer of judicial and quasi-judicial powers
descriptor.definition: A dispute resolution mechanism encompasses structured institutional forums established to resolve business and legal conflicts efficiently. Under statutory provisions, specialized bodies such as tribunals, special courts, mediation panels, and investigative agencies operate to provide a unified framework for corporate matters.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general civil court litigation by offering specialized regulatory and company-specific administrative forums.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 2: Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel
A. PART II OF SCHEDULE V [SECTIONS I TO V] - MANAGERIAL REMUNERATION
Managerial Remuneration Under Schedule V Special Circumstances

exclusion: Established profitable companies governed strictly by standard profit percentage caps
inclusion: Remuneration flexibility for new businesses during their initial seven years
Paucity limits overridden by approved revival or insolvency schemes
descriptor.definition: Companies with no or inadequate profits may pay managerial remuneration exceeding standard limits under specific special circumstances. These exceptions apply to newly incorporated entities for seven years, sick or revived companies, and entities executing resolution plans under the insolvency framework.
nearby_distinctions: Separates standard profit-based payout rules from rehabilitation-period remuneration exceptions
instrument_references: Schedule V of the Companies Act, 2013

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
SPECIAL TAXATION REGIME FOR INVESTMENT FUNDS AND INCOME RECEIVED FROM SUCH FUNDS [SECTION 224]
Special Taxation Regime for Investment Funds and Income Received from Such Funds

exclusion: Offshore investment income routed through specified alternative investment funds for non-residents under direct investment rules
inclusion: Income distributed by investment funds to resident and non-resident unit holders
Business income taxable directly at the investment fund level
descriptor.definition: Income received by a unit holder from an investment fund is taxed as if the underlying investments were made directly by the unit holder. Investment funds are generally exempt from tax on income other than profits and gains from business or profession, which remains taxable at the fund level.
terminology: Profits and gains from business or profession
nearby_distinctions: Pass-through taxation applies to non-business incomes of investment funds, whereas business profits are taxed directly at the fund level.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 9: Adjudication, Special Courts, National Company Law Tribunal & National Company Law Appellate Tribunal

exclusion: Mandatory criminal trials that fall strictly under adversarial court adjudication
inclusion: Referrals initiated during pending proceedings before the Central Government, Tribunal, or Appellate Tribunal
Expert panel appointments for structured alternative dispute resolution
descriptor.definition: The Central Government maintains a panel of qualified experts to facilitate mediation between disputing parties during active proceedings. Matters may be referred to these experts either through an application by any party or suo motu by the adjudicating authority.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike binding judicial judgments, mediation focuses on facilitated consensus-building through specialized experts during administrative or tribunal proceedings.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 3: Meetings of Board and Its Powers

exclusion: Exempted transactions specifically provided under statutory non-applicability provisions
inclusion: Direct and indirect loan advancements
Provision of guarantees or securities for loans taken by directors or connected entities
descriptor.definition: Companies are generally prohibited from directly or indirectly advancing loans, book debts, guarantees, or securities to their directors, relatives, partners, or associated firms. Specific relaxations permit such financial assistance only if approved via special resolution with detailed explanatory statements and utilized strictly for principal business activities.
terminology: Person in whom director is interested
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general inter-corporate loans under Section 186 due to targeted restrictions on key management personnel and related entities

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 3: Meetings of Board and Its Powers

exclusion: Matters mandatorily requiring consideration at a duly convened physical board meeting
Resolutions lacking the requisite director consent
inclusion: Circulating draft resolutions and papers via email or fax
Noting resolutions passed by circulation in the subsequent board meeting minutes
Reverting to a physical meeting when requested by one-third of total directors
descriptor.definition: Companies may pass board resolutions by circulating drafts and necessary papers via electronic means to directors when urgent decisions do not necessitate a formal meeting. If at least one-third of total directors demand that a circulated resolution be decided at a meeting, the chairperson must put it before a convened board meeting.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from physical board meeting resolutions because it operates through document circulation without assembling directors in person.
instrument_references: Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014, Rule 5

path.name: Modifications to the Opinion, Emphasis of Matter Paragraph or Other Matter Paragraph in the Auditor’s Report on the Audited Financial Statements
Modifications and Special Paragraphs from Audited Financial Statements

exclusion: issuing clean summary reports when underlying reports contain adverse opinions or disclaimers
inclusion: disclosure of underlying report modifications in the summary report
dating restrictions relative to the main audit report
descriptor.definition: When the underlying audit report contains modifications, emphasis of matter, or other special sections, the summary report must state this fact and describe the basis and effect on the summaries. The summary report date cannot precede the date of the underlying audit report or the collection of sufficient evidence.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard reporting updates by requiring explicit cascading descriptions of prior modifications and their specific impacts on summarized figures.

path.name: Chapter 14: Special Features of Audit of Banks & Non-Banking Financial Companies
Unit 1: – SPECIAL FEATURES OF AUDIT OF BANKS
Types of Activities to be Covered
Types of Activities to be Covered in Concurrent Audit

exclusion: General strategic management decisions
Tax filing execution
inclusion: Cash transaction and currency chest checks
Investment holding and compliance verifications
Advances sanctioning and post-disbursement monitoring
descriptor.definition: Concurrent audit procedures target specific operational domains including cash management, investments, deposits, and advances to verify transaction authenticity and regulatory compliance. Auditors examine delegation of powers, physical security holdings, post-disbursement supervision, and asset classification accuracy.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from generalized operational reviews through precise verification procedures applied to high-risk banking transaction cycles.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set B
Chapter 1: An Introduction to Strategic Cost Management

exclusion: Standardized routine operational processes
Generic industry-wide cost structures
inclusion: Evaluation of resource uniqueness
Testing for market relevance and imitation difficulty
Exploitation of competencies across value chains
descriptor.definition: Core competencies are unique organizational strengths derived from specialized resources and capabilities that enable a firm to deliver distinct customer value and achieve market leadership. An effective core competency must pass specific evaluative parameters regarding relevance, difficulty of imitation, and breadth of application.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from key success factors by representing deeply embedded organizational traits that competitors cannot easily copy, rather than broad industry-wide requirements.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: Appointment and Qualification of Directors
APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS TO BE VOTED INDIVIDUALLY [SECTION 162]
Individual Voting Requirement for Director Appointments

exclusion: Passing a single resolution to elect multiple directors when any member casts a dissenting vote
Exemptions applicable to specific government companies, wholly-owned subsidiaries, and private companies under rules
inclusion: Separate resolutions required for each individual director appointment
Unanimous agreement exception allowing single resolution voting if no votes are cast against the proposal
descriptor.definition: Companies are prohibited from appointing two or more directors through a single collective resolution unless a preliminary proposal to do so is agreed upon without any dissenting votes. This ensures shareholders retain individual choice and can reject specific candidates without voting against an entire slate.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from block-voting practices by forcing strict individual assessment of candidates unless absolute unanimous consent permits a grouped ballot.
instrument_references: Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014

path.name: Chapter 13: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements of Group Entities

exclusion: Purely operational trade transactions devoid of risk absorption characteristics
inclusion: Evaluation of risks that structured entities were designed to create or pass on
descriptor.definition: The standard mandates qualitative and quantitative disclosures so financial statement users can assess the nature and associated risks of interests in other entities. It also requires evaluation of how these involvements impact the entity's financial position, performance, and cash flows.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses purely on disclosure objectives rather than recognition or measurement criteria prescribed by other accounting standards.

path.name: WITHHOLDING TAX PROVISIONS FOR NON- RESIDENTS
Withholding Tax on Non-Resident Salaries and Perquisites

exclusion: Salaries for services rendered entirely outside India
inclusion: Salary income deemed to accrue in India due to services rendered locally
Employer payment of tax on non-monetary perquisites without employee deduction
Deferred TDS on specified securities or sweat equity from eligible startups
descriptor.definition: Employers must deduct withholding tax at applicable rates on salary payments to non-residents when services are rendered within India. Special provisions govern tax calculation on non-monetary perquisites and allow deferred tax payment timelines for specified startup securities.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes monetary salary withholding from non-monetary perquisite tax handling

path.name: Chapter 14: Special Features of Audit of Banks & Non-Banking Financial Companies
Unit 1: – SPECIAL FEATURES OF AUDIT OF BANKS

exclusion: Exhaustive 100% pre-transaction checking
Unapproved non-risk areas
inclusion: High-risk transaction prioritisation
Random sample testing
Branch coverage discretion of internal audit heads
descriptor.definition: The scope of a concurrent audit is determined centrally by the bank's internal department in consultation with the Audit Committee of the Board, prioritizing high-risk operational areas. It covers key functions such as cash, deposits, advances, investments, and foreign exchange based on the identified risk profiles of specific units.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from fixed statutory audit scopes by allowing dynamic tailoring based on internal risk identification and business model specificities.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 3: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

exclusion: Direct initiation of liquidation without a preceding resolution phase
inclusion: Liquidation upon receiving no resolution plan
Liquidation due to committee decision approval
Liquidation following plan contravention
descriptor.definition: Liquidation is triggered only after a corporate insolvency resolution process fails due to missing plans, committee rejections, or plan contraventions. The adjudicating authority issues an order directing the corporate debtor into liquidation as governed by statute.
nearby_distinctions: Liquidation mandates asset realization, differing from CIRP's primary emphasis on business revival and continuation.
