units from administrators of specified undertakings or specified companies
descriptor.definition: Payers distributing income in respect of mutual fund units or specified undertakings must deduct tax at source. Capital gains distributions and amounts below the financial year threshold are exempt from this deduction.
nearby_distinctions: Excludes capital gains components, focusing strictly on income distributions from specified mutual fund and corporate units.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Furnishing of statements in respect of payment of any income to residents without deduction of tax [Section 206A]
Furnishing Of Statements In Respect Of Payment Of Any Income To Residents Without Deduction Of Tax [Section 206A]

exclusion: Payments subject to full tax deduction at source requirements
Payments exceeding statutory monetary limits
inclusion: Reporting sub-threshold interest payments to residents
Filing correction statements for rectifying reporting mistakes
descriptor.definition: Banking companies, co-operative societies, and specific housing finance public companies must furnish prescribed statements for resident interest payments not exceeding designated thresholds without tax deduction. Non-compliance invites daily monetary penalties under the statute.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard TDS return filing because it specifically tracks exempt or sub-threshold payments made without withholding.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Interest other than interest on securities [Section 194A]
Interest other than interest on securities [Section 194A]

exclusion: Routine daily or monthly macro-monitoring provisioning entries lacking constructive credit in core banking systems
inclusion: Interest payments from non-exempt entities to resident payees
Periodic or maturity-based interest credits on bank time deposits
descriptor.definition: Non-individual assessees, along with large business individuals or HUFs exceeding specific turnover limits, must deduct tax at source on non-security interest paid to residents. Automated core banking software provisioning for macro-monitoring does not constitute constructive credit triggering immediate TDS obligations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from interest on securities by excluding formal debentures and government security yields in favor of general bank and commercial interest.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Payments made by individuals or HUFs strictly for non-business personal purposes
inclusion: Contract sums for labor and construction work
Payments made by qualified businesses, governments, and large enterprises
descriptor.definition: Specified entities and large business operators making payments to resident contractors for carrying out any work must deduct tax at source upon credit or payment. Payments made by individuals or HUFs exclusively for personal purposes are exempt from these withholding obligations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from professional fees by applying explicitly to contractual execution of work rather than specialized professional services.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward

exclusion: carrying forward specified losses without a timely filed return under section 263(1)
inclusion: mandating timely loss return submission for business and capital losses
exempting house property loss and unabsorbed depreciation from filing preconditions
descriptor.definition: Carrying forward specified capital, business, speculation, and specified activity losses requires filing a valid loss return within the statutory timeframe. House property losses and unabsorbed depreciation are exempt from this mandatory return-filing prerequisite for carry forward.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates losses requiring mandatory return filing for carry-forward eligibility from those like house property losses that retain carry-forward rights regardless.

path.name: Particulars to be furnished with the return [section 139(6)]
Particulars to be furnished with the return [section 139(6)]

exclusion: General business audit reports governed under separate sub-sections like section 139(6A)
inclusion: Income exempt from tax
Assets held as beneficial owner or otherwise
Bank account and credit card details
Expenditure exceeding prescribed limits
descriptor.definition: Prescribed return forms require specified categories of taxpayers to disclose comprehensive financial details alongside their income declarations. These mandatory disclosures encompass exempt income, beneficial or other asset holdings, bank accounts, credit cards, and specified high-value outgoings.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from basic income computation schedules by focusing on specific asset ownership, bank linkages, and external financial indicators.

exclusion: Taxable domestic business income not covered under specific exemptions
inclusion: Interest on NRE bank accounts maintained by non-residents
Interest on specified offshore rupee-denominated bonds
Income of specified funds from transfer of specific assets in IFSC
descriptor.definition: Specific categories of income earned by non-residents, such as interest on NRE accounts or specified offshore rupee-denominated bonds, are exempt from tax under statutory provisions. These exemptions encourage foreign currency inflows and investments in recognized financial instruments.
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates between fully taxable foreign income and specifically exempted passive inflows

path.name: Chapter 8: Deductions from Gross Total Income
General Provisions of Chapter VIII Deductions

exclusion: Incomes exempt under section 11
Carrying forward negative income or losses caused by deductions
inclusion: Deductions from gross total income
Restrictions on aggregate deductions exceeding gross total income
descriptor.definition: Chapter VIII permits deductions from gross total income to compute total income, subject to the overall limitation that aggregate deductions cannot exceed the gross total income itself. These provisions prevent double counting by prohibiting member-level deductions for AOP or BOI shares already benefiting from specific sections, and restrict duplicate claims of Part C deductions under alternative provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from section 11 exemptions which completely exclude specified incomes from entering the computation process.

textbook_references.download_url: https://resource.cdn.icai.org/94202CHP-8 Deduction from Gross Total Income.pdf

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
Taxation Regime of Special Entities and Non-Profit Organisations

exclusion: Standard corporate entities not falling under special exemptions
General individual taxpayers
inclusion: Charitable and religious institutions
Educational and medical organizations
Political parties and electoral trusts
Securitization and business trusts
Investment funds
descriptor.definition: This chapter covers the income tax treatment and exemptions applicable to educational and medical organizations, charitable or religious trusts, political parties, electoral trusts, and special entities like securitization trusts, business trusts, and investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Specific provisions govern registered non-profit organizations and special investment vehicles through dedicated sections and schedules.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general commercial entities and special tax-exempt non-profit or pass-through vehicles.

exclusion: Transfers involving stock-in-trade under holding-subsidiary arrangements
inclusion: Distributions upon total or partial partition of a Hindu Undivided Family
Transfers under a will, gift, or irrevocable trust
Qualifying transfers between Indian holding and wholly owned subsidiary companies
descriptor.definition: Specific statutory provisions ensure certain structural reorganizations and family partitions are not treated as transfers for capital gains purposes. These exemptions apply to conditions involving Hindu Undivided Family partitions, gifts, trusts, and qualifying holding-subsidiary or amalgamation transfers.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes regular taxable asset transfers from statutory non-transfer events like corporate amalgamations and family gifts that defer tax realization.

path.name: SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO CONVERSION OF INDIAN BRANCH OF A FOREIGN BANK INTO A SUBSIDIARY COMPANY [CHAPTER XII-BB]
Conversion of Foreign Bank Indian Branch into Subsidiary

exclusion: Conversions executed outside of Reserve Bank of India regulatory frameworks
inclusion: Exemption of capital gains on conversion of foreign bank branches
Transfer of all assets and liabilities to the subsidiary
descriptor.definition: Capital gains arising when a foreign banking company converts its Indian branch into an Indian subsidiary company under an approved Reserve Bank of India scheme are exempt from tax. This exemption requires the complete transfer of all branch assets and liabilities to the new subsidiary under sanctioned amalgamation terms.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes structural corporate branch reorganizations from standard taxable asset transfers

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Exempt insurance proceeds fully compliant with statutory conditions
inclusion: Insurance solicitation commissions
Taxable payouts from non-exempt life insurance policies
descriptor.definition: Entities paying remuneration or commission to resident agents for soliciting or procuring insurance business must deduct tax at source when payments exceed statutory financial year limits. Non-compliant sums received under life insurance policies lacking exemption are similarly subjected to specific withholding rates.
nearby_distinctions: Targets insurance remuneration specifically, separating it from standard commercial contract payments and brokerage fees.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment in respect of life insurance policy [Section 194DA]
Payment in respect of life insurance policy [Section 194DA]

exclusion: sums fully exempt under Section 10(10D)
payments below the prescribed financial year threshold limit
inclusion: maturity proceeds of policies not qualifying for exemption
bonus amounts allocated under such policies
descriptor.definition: Tax is deductible on maturity or other proceeds of life insurance policies that fail to satisfy statutory exemption conditions. The deduction applies to the income component after subtracting the premium paid.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike fully exempt policies under Section 10(10D), policies failing conditions attract tax deduction on the net income element.

path.name: Chapter 2: Incomes which do not form part of Total Income

exclusion: Incomes subject to deductions under Chapter VIII prior to final total income computation
inclusion: Incomes specified under Schedules II to VI
Total income of specified persons under Schedule VII
descriptor.definition: Exempt incomes under section 11 and its schedules are completely excluded from the computation of total income. In contrast, deductions under Chapter VIII are first included in the gross total income and subsequently deducted.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes complete exclusion from total income via exemptions versus subsequent subtraction through Chapter VIII deductions

exclusion: Indian currency and foreign currency
Gift cards or discount vouchers
Loyalty, rebate, or reward mileage points
Non-fungible tokens whose transfer legally enforces underlying tangible asset ownership
inclusion: Cryptographically generated value tokens
Notified non-fungible tokens
Electronically transferable store-of-value digital codes
descriptor.definition: Virtual digital assets encompass cryptographically generated codes, tokens, or numbers providing a digital representation of value that can be electronically transferred, stored, or traded. The statutory definition includes non-fungible tokens while expressly excluding Indian or foreign currency, digital gift cards, reward points, and specific subscription vouchers.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard fiat currencies and traditional commercial discount vouchers by its cryptographic generation and electronic store-of-value properties.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
SPECIAL TAXATION REGIME FOR INVESTMENT FUNDS AND INCOME RECEIVED FROM SUCH FUNDS [SECTION 224]
Special Taxation Regime for Investment Funds and Income Received from Such Funds

exclusion: Offshore investment income routed through specified alternative investment funds for non-residents under direct investment rules
inclusion: Income distributed by investment funds to resident and non-resident unit holders
Business income taxable directly at the investment fund level
descriptor.definition: Income received by a unit holder from an investment fund is taxed as if the underlying investments were made directly by the unit holder. Investment funds are generally exempt from tax on income other than profits and gains from business or profession, which remains taxable at the fund level.
terminology: Profits and gains from business or profession
nearby_distinctions: Pass-through taxation applies to non-business incomes of investment funds, whereas business profits are taxed directly at the fund level.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Non-applicability of TDS provisions on payments made to Corporations whose income is exempt under section 10(26BBB) [Circular No.7/2015, dated 23-04-2015]
Non-applicability of TDS provisions on payments made to Corporations whose income is exempt under section 10(26BBB) [Circular No.7/2015, dated 23-04-2015]

exclusion: entities whose income is taxable under the Act or which are statutorily required to file returns
inclusion: corporations established by central or state acts for the welfare and economic upliftment of ex-servicemen
descriptor.definition: Tax deduction at source is not required for payments made to specific welfare corporations established for ex-servicemen whose income enjoys unconditional statutory exemption and who are exempt from filing returns. This policy aligns with administrative exemptions granted to entities whose total income falls outside the tax net.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general operational exemptions by relying on dual criteria of unconditional income exemption and lack of statutory return filing obligations.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Interest for defaults in furnishing return of income [Section 234A]
Interest for Defaults in Furnishing Return of Income

exclusion: Inclusion of additional income tax components specified under sections 140B or 143 within the interest calculation base
inclusion: Monthly interest computations for late or un-furnished tax returns
Reductions for advance interest payments made under section 140A
descriptor.definition: Simple interest is charged when an assessee fails to submit an income tax return by the statutory due date or omits filing entirely. The charge accrues monthly from the day following the due date until the actual filing date or best-judgment completion.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses exclusively on return submission timelines rather than installment payment milestones or tax deferment discrepancies.

path.name: APPLICABLE RATE OF TAX IN RESPECT OF WINNINGS FROM ONLINE GAMES [SECTION 194(1) (TABLE: SI. NO. 5)]

exclusion: Traditional physical lotteries, crosswords, and offline gambling winnings
inclusion: Net winnings originating from internet-accessible games via computer resources
descriptor.definition: Net winnings from online games accessed through computer resources or telecommunication devices are subject to a flat tax rate. No related expenditure allowances, Chapter VIII deductions, or basic exemption limit adjustments are permitted against this income.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes digital and internet-based gaming platforms from traditional offline casual income sources.

exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
descriptor.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward
NO SET OFF OF LOSSES AGAINST UNDISCLOSED INCOME CONSEQUENT TO SEARCH, REQUISITION AND SURVEY [SECTION 120]
NO SET OFF OF LOSSES AGAINST UNDISCLOSED INCOME CONSEQUENT TO SEARCH, REQUISITION AND SURVEY [SECTION 120]

exclusion: surveys conducted under section 253(4)
inclusion: prohibition of loss set-off against undisclosed assets or transactions
restriction on offsetting unabsorbed depreciation against discovered income
descriptor.definition: Brought forward losses, current losses, and unabsorbed depreciation cannot be set off against undisclosed income uncovered during statutory searches, requisitions, or qualifying surveys. Undisclosed income encompasses unrecorded assets, transactions, or incorrect expense and deduction claims for the block period.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard business income and regular loss adjustments from punitive non-set-off rules applied exclusively to discovered undisclosed income.

path.name: REFERENCE TO PRINCIPAL COMMISSIONER OR COMMISSIONER IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 144BA]
Reference To Principal Commissioner Or Commissioner In Certain Cases

exclusion: Arrangements finalized without giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard
inclusion: References for declaring arrangements as impermissible avoidance arrangements
Approving Panel binding directions
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer can refer an arrangement to the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner to declare it an impermissible avoidance arrangement. The authority issues notices, evaluates objections, and may refer the matter to an Approving Panel which issues binding directions for completion.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard tax evasion inquiries by targeting complex tax avoidance arrangements through a specialized multi-tier review involving the Principal Commissioner and Approving Panel.

path.name: WITHHOLDING TAX PROVISIONS FOR NON- RESIDENTS
Withholding Tax on Non-Resident Salaries and Perquisites

exclusion: Salaries for services rendered entirely outside India
inclusion: Salary income deemed to accrue in India due to services rendered locally
Employer payment of tax on non-monetary perquisites without employee deduction
Deferred TDS on specified securities or sweat equity from eligible startups
descriptor.definition: Employers must deduct withholding tax at applicable rates on salary payments to non-residents when services are rendered within India. Special provisions govern tax calculation on non-monetary perquisites and allow deferred tax payment timelines for specified startup securities.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes monetary salary withholding from non-monetary perquisite tax handling

exclusion: Unapproved non-statutory communication channels lacking CBDT backing
inclusion: Service by post or approved courier services
Service via electronic records under IT Act chapter IV
Designated addressees for firms, companies, HUFs, and local authorities
descriptor.definition: Tax communications, notices, and summons may be served by post, approved courier services, Code of Civil Procedure methods, electronic records, or other CBDT-prescribed transmission means. Specific statutory addressees are designated for serving notices corresponding to distinct entity types such as firms, Hindu Undivided Families, companies, and associations.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the procedural modes and mandatory recipient addressees for serving notices, whereas Section 282A governs the authentication and signing validity of those notices

path.name: PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]
PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]

exclusion: Unauthorized third parties lacking specific legal designation or valid power of attorney
inclusion: Assessee himself for individuals under normal circumstances
Authorized power-of-attorney holders during absence or incapacity
Managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals for companies
descriptor.definition: Statutory provisions explicitly designate which individuals possess the legal authority to sign and verify income tax returns on behalf of different assessee types. Depending on circumstances such as absence, mental incapacity, winding up, or corporate insolvency, specific representatives like power-of-attorney holders, managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals are authorized.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on the legal competence to sign and authenticate return documents, separate from the actual preparation or computation of income.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Liability for payment of advance tax
Liability for Payment of Advance Tax

exclusion: Taxpayers whose total advance tax liability remains under ten thousand rupees
Non-residents meeting age criteria
inclusion: Mandatory advance tax obligations for liabilities exceeding the statutory threshold
Relief provisions for elderly resident individuals with rental or interest incomes
descriptor.definition: An obligation to pay advance tax is triggered whenever the computed tax liability reaches or exceeds ten thousand rupees for the financial year. Resident individuals aged sixty or older without business or professional income are exempted from this payment rule.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general tax remittance because liability is conditioned specifically on crossing a minimum financial threshold and the absence of speculative business revenue for senior exemptions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Faceless collection and recovery of tax [Section 231]
Faceless Collection And Recovery Of Tax [Section 231]

exclusion: Traditional physical field enforcement operations not covered under the notified scheme
inclusion: Faceless processing of lower deduction or collection certificates
Digital handling of installment extensions and penalty levies
Automated resource optimization and team-based assessments
descriptor.definition: The Central Government is empowered to notify schemes for faceless collection and recovery of tax to eliminate physical interfaces between authorities and assessees. This framework covers lower deduction certificates, default orders, interest waivers, and recovery certificate operations using dynamic jurisdiction.
nearby_distinctions: Replaces traditional localized administrative touchpoints with an automated, virtual, team-based jurisdiction model across recovery and deduction functions.

context.question_text:
(D)  ` 91,000 
(2 Marks) 
4. 
In the given facts, in the case of Mr. Shiv Aggarwal in respect of the 
Assessment Year 2023-24, which of the following statement is correct?

exclusion: Submissions attempted after the statutory time limit or after completion of assessment
inclusion: Returns originally filed under section 139(1) or 139(4)
Returns filed under sub-sections (1A), (3), (4A) to (4F) of section 139
descriptor.definition: A taxpayer who discovers any omission or wrong statement in an initially filed return may submit a revised return prior to three months before the end of the relevant assessment year or before assessment completion, whichever is earlier. The latest submitted revised return entirely supersedes all previous filings made for that assessment year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from an original return because it corrects prior errors rather than establishing initial filing, and distinct from an updated return.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Credit for tax deducted at source [Section 199]
Credit For Tax Deducted At Source [Section 199]

exclusion: Direct payment of tax without statutory deduction mechanism
Credit given without matching deductor information
inclusion: Credit given to the deductee based on deductor reporting
Proportional credit across multiple years if income is assessable across years
descriptor.definition: Tax deducted at source and paid to the Central Government is treated as tax payment on behalf of the person from whose income the deduction was made or the owner of the relevant asset. Rule 37BA dictates that credit is given to the actual deductee or an alternate assessable person based on deductor information, aligned with the assessment year of the income.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 200 duty to deposit, focusing instead on granting tax credit to the income earner.

path.name: ACT TO HAVE EFFECT PENDING LEGISLATIVE PROVISION FOR CHARGE OF TAX [SECTION 294]
Act To Have Effect Pending Legislative Provision For Charge Of Tax [Section 294]

exclusion: Scenarios where regular charging provisions are enacted on or before April 1st
inclusion: Continuation of tax collection mechanisms during legislative delays
Application of the more beneficial tax rate between prior laws and pending bills
descriptor.definition: If a Central Act fails to enact income tax charging provisions by April 1st of an assessment year, the existing tax act remains operational. It continues to function using either the preceding year provisions or the current parliamentary bill proposals, whichever proves more favourable to the assessee.
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a temporary transitional safeguard specifically for tax charging continuity rather than general administrative rule-making.

exclusion: Returns filed after the expiry of the belated filing deadline
inclusion: Returns submitted after the section 139(1) due date within permitted statutory windows
descriptor.definition: A belated return is filed by any person who missed the original due date, submitted prior to three months before the end of the assessment year or before assessment completion. Filing a belated return incurs interest, late fees, and restrictions on carrying forward certain losses or claiming specific deductions.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike original timely returns, belated returns restrict loss carry-forward privileges and strip eligibility for specific tax incentive deductions.

exclusion: Ordinary colloquial meanings where statutory definitions explicitly expand or restrict terms
inclusion: Persons liable to pay tax or refund
Persons subject to assessment proceedings or deemed default
Procedures determining income through various assessment types
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions provide precise legal meanings for key terms used throughout the tax legislation. When a term lacks explicit definition in the statute, external aids like the General Clauses Act or dictionaries are utilized.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between terms defined directly in Section 2 versus those defined in specific operational sections.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
EXEMPTION IN RESPECT OF INCOME OF CERTAIN UNIVERSITIES, EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, HOSPITALS, MEDICAL INSTITUTIONS ETC.
Exemption for Certain Educational and Medical Institutions

exclusion: Institutions operating for profit
Hospitals or educational institutions exceeding the financial receipt threshold without government financing
inclusion: Universities wholly or substantially financed by the government
Hospitals existing solely for philanthropic purposes and substantially financed by the government
Educational and medical institutions with aggregate annual receipts not exceeding five crore rupees
descriptor.definition: Specific universities, educational institutions, hospitals, and medical institutions are exempt from income tax on their total income if they are wholly or substantially financed by the government, or if their aggregate annual receipts do not exceed five crore rupees. An institution is considered substantially financed when government grants exceed 50 percent of its total receipts including donations during the tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes government-backed or smaller scale medical and educational bodies from standard commercial enterprises and general trusts.

path.name: LIABILITY OF SUCCESSOR TO BUSINESS IN RESPECT OF TAX CHARGEABLE FROM THE PREDECESSOR [SECTION 313]
Liability of Successor to Business in Respect of Tax Chargeable from Predecessor

exclusion: Liabilities unrelated to the transferred business operations prior to succession
Unrelated third-party debts
inclusion: Apportionment of income between predecessor and successor for the succession year
Transfer of assessment proceedings pending before courts or tribunals
descriptor.definition: When a business or profession is transferred, the predecessor and successor are independently assessed for the income earned during their respective operational periods within that tax year. If the predecessor cannot be located, the successor inherits the tax liability for the succession year and the preceding year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between ongoing separate assessments during normal succession versus unified successor liability when the predecessor is untraceable

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Fee/ penalty for default in furnishing TDS/ TCS Statements
Fee and Penalty for Default in Furnishing TDS and TCS Statements

exclusion: Penalty impositions under section 271H when delayed statements are filed within the permitted one-year timeframe alongside due payments
inclusion: Daily statutory fees for delayed TDS and TCS statement filings
Monetized penalty ranges for un-furnished or incorrect statements
Conditional penalty waivers for compliance within specified grace periods
descriptor.definition: Late submission of tax deduction or collection statements incurs a mandatory daily fee capped at the total tax amount. Additional monetary penalties apply for missing statutory deadlines or providing incorrect statement information, with thresholds adjusted for extended delays.
nearby_distinctions: Separates administrative daily late-filing fees from substantive legal penalties, imposing both concurrently only when delays exceed extended statutory limits.

path.name: MONETARY LIMITS FOR REGULATING FILING OF APPEALS BY INCOME TAX AUTHORITIES [SECTION 268A]
Monetary Limits for Regulating Filing of Appeals by Income Tax Authorities

exclusion: Appeals exceeding the specified monetary cutoffs where merits justify litigation
inclusion: Departmental appeals restricted by prescribed monetary thresholds
Future filings on identical issues for other assessment years or assessees
descriptor.definition: The central board is empowered to set financial thresholds that regulate when tax authorities can file appeals or reference applications before tribunals and courts. Failure to appeal in a specific case due to these monetary limits does not prevent the authority from litigating the same issue in other assessment years or against different assessees.
nearby_distinctions: Regulates administrative discretion to litigate based on financial stakes rather than the legal merit of the underlying dispute.

path.name: Chapter 8: Deductions from Gross Total Income
Deduction in respect of investment in specified assets

exclusion: Deferred annuity contracts
Deductions under the default tax regime
inclusion: Life insurance premium payments for self, spouse, and children
Investments enumerated in Schedule XV
descriptor.definition: Eligible individuals and Hindu Undivided Families shifting out of the default tax regime can claim a deduction up to 150000 for specified investments and contributions made during the tax year. Qualifying life insurance policy premiums are restricted based on the date of issuance relative to the actual capital sum assured.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general deductions by explicitly limiting eligibility to non-default tax regime users and capping contributions at statutory thresholds.

textbook_references.download_url: https://resource.cdn.icai.org/94202CHP-8 Deduction from Gross Total Income.pdf

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Assessees whose computed advance tax liability falls below the statutory threshold of 10000 rupees
inclusion: Tax payment obligations on current financial year income
Exemptions for resident individuals aged 60 or above without business income
descriptor.definition: Assessees must discharge their tax liability on current income progressively during the financial year if the total advance tax payable meets the statutory threshold. Resident senior citizens with passive income and no business profits are exempt from this requirement.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from self-assessment tax or tax deducted at source by enforcing mandatory installment payments ahead of the assessment year based on estimated current earnings.

path.name: TIME LIMIT FOR COMPLETION OF ASSESSMENTS AND REASSESSMENTS [SECTION 153]
Time Limits For Completion Of Assessments And Reassessments

exclusion: Unspecified assessment procedures outside the statutory provisions of this section
inclusion: Time limits for regular scrutiny or best judgment assessments
Time limits for reassessments following section 148 notices
Time limits for fresh orders after appellate set-aside actions
descriptor.definition: Statutory time limits regulate the completion of assessments, reassessments, or fresh assessments based on the specific assessment year or the date of service of notices. These prescribed periods restrict when tax authorities must finalize orders following returns, searches, or appellate remands.
nearby_distinctions: Varies strictly by assessment year and the specific procedural trigger such as regular filings versus appellate remands.

path.name: Particulars to be furnished with return of income in case of an assessee engaged in business or profession [Section 139(6A)]
Particulars to be furnished with return of income in case of an assessee engaged in business or profession [Section 139(6A)]

exclusion: Non-business individual disclosures such as general personal bank accounts or credit cards
inclusion: Tax audit report referred to in section 44AB
Location and style of principal place of business and branches
Names and addresses of partners
Names of members and profit shares in an association of persons or body of individuals
descriptor.definition: Taxpayers engaged in any business or profession must submit specific commercial particulars with their return, including statutory audit reports and principal operational locations. Additionally, they must disclose names, addresses, and profit-sharing ratios of all partners or association members.
nearby_distinctions: Specifically targets commercial entities and professionals requiring structural disclosures like partnership details and audit reports, unlike general asset disclosures under section 139(6).

exclusion: Loss returns
Returns decreasing total tax liability
Returns creating or increasing refunds
Cases involving search, requisition, or certain surveys
inclusion: Returns filed within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year
Returns furnishing additional income
descriptor.definition: Assessees can furnish an updated return for any previous year within 24 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, regardless of whether original, belated, or revised returns were previously filed. However, updated returns are prohibited if they report a loss, decrease tax liability, result in or increase refunds, or if search, survey, or related proceedings apply.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from belated returns under section 139(4) and revised returns under section 139(5) by its specific purpose of updating income with additional tax payments and strict non-applicability to loss or refund scenarios.

exclusion: Manual face-to-face assessment proceedings outside the designated electronic portal
inclusion: Automated allocation of cases via NFAC
Electronic responses and notices
Cross-functional coordination with verification and technical units
descriptor.definition: Faceless assessment conducts scrutiny, best judgment, or income escaping assessments electronically through a designated portal via automated case allocation. The National Faceless Assessment Centre coordinates responses, inquiries, and technical assistance between the assessee and specialized assessment, verification, or technical units.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from traditional physical assessments by operating entirely through electronic portals with segregated functional units rather than a single local Assessing Officer.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Tax liabilities matching or exceeding payments made
inclusion: Refund claims for excess tax payments
Claims filed by legal representatives for incapacitated or deceased assessees
Direct refund applications under Section 195 arrangements
descriptor.definition: Assessees are entitled to claim tax refunds when total taxes paid exceed their properly chargeable liability for an assessment year. Such claims typically arise from excess tax deducted at source, advance tax overpayments, or appellate reductions of original tax assessments.
nearby_distinctions: Inverts recovery provisions by addressing the return of excess funds collected by the Government rather than the extraction of tax arrears from the assessee.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Inclusion of interest payments or monetary penalties within the creditable tax pool
inclusion: Crediting recovered or voluntarily paid advance tax sums against final tax liabilities
Allocation of payments exclusively to income tax components
descriptor.definition: Payments made towards advance tax, excluding any associated interest or penalties, are officially recognized as tax payments for the relevant previous year. The corresponding tax credit is formally granted during the regular assessment procedure.
nearby_distinctions: Separates pure advance tax principal payments from penal or interest charges, ensuring only principal tax remittances qualify for assessment-stage tax credits.

path.name: Chapter 6: Income of Other Persons included in Assessee’s Total Income
LIABILITY OF PERSON IN RESPECT OF INCOME INCLUDED IN THE INCOME OF ANOTHER PERSON [SECTION 100]
Liability for Tax on Clubbed Income

exclusion: tax liabilities unrelated to the specific income clubbed under Sections 96 through 99
inclusion: tax recovery enforcement notices served directly on asset transferees
joint and several tax liabilities for co-transferees of gifted assets
descriptor.definition: While clubbed income is taxed in the hands of the transferor, a notice of demand can legally be served upon the transferee to recover the portion of tax attributable to that specific clubbed income. If the underlying asset is held jointly by multiple transferees, such persons assume joint and several liability for the corresponding tax payment.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary assessment liability (on the transferor) from secondary recovery enforcement power (against the transferee holding the asset).

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: income of the nature of capital gains
aggregate income not exceeding the threshold limit in a financial year
inclusion: income distributed on mutual fund units
units from administrators of specified undertakings or specified companies
descriptor.definition: Payers distributing income in respect of mutual fund units or specified undertakings must deduct tax at source. Capital gains distributions and amounts below the financial year threshold are exempt from this deduction.
nearby_distinctions: Excludes capital gains components, focusing strictly on income distributions from specified mutual fund and corporate units.

path.name: Modified return - Effect of order of Tribunal or Court in respect of business reorganisaton [Section 170A]
Modified return - Effect of order of Tribunal or Court in respect of business reorganisaton [Section 170A]

exclusion: Standard voluntary revisions of income returns unrelated to formal business reorganisation judicial orders
inclusion: Entities undergoing business reorganisation under court, tribunal, or IBC orders
Modified returns filed in Form ITR-A within the stipulated timeline
descriptor.definition: Following a business reorganisation order from a competent judicial or adjudicating authority, a successor entity must submit a modified electronic return in Form ITR-A within six months. The Assessing Officer is then required to modify completed assessments or complete pending proceedings to align with the reorganisation order.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by its mandatory link to external corporate restructuring judicial directives rather than routine self-correction of tax errors.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]

exclusion: benefits or perquisites to a resident where aggregate value does not exceed 20,000 rupees in a financial year
providers being individuals or HUFs whose business turnover or professional receipts do not exceed statutory thresholds
inclusion: benefits or perquisites arising from business or exercise of a profession
perquisites provided wholly in kind, partly in kind, or in cash
descriptor.definition: Any person providing business or professional benefits or perquisites to a resident must ensure tax is deducted at source before release, regardless of whether the benefit is in cash, kind, or partly both. If the benefit is wholly or partly in kind and available cash is insufficient to cover tax, the deductor must ensure tax is paid prior to release.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard monetary income TDS by capturing non-monetary or mixed business advantages provided to trade partners or professionals.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Furnishing of statements in respect of payment of any income to residents without deduction of tax [Section 206A]
Furnishing Of Statements In Respect Of Payment Of Any Income To Residents Without Deduction Of Tax [Section 206A]

exclusion: Payments subject to full tax deduction at source requirements
Payments exceeding statutory monetary limits
inclusion: Reporting sub-threshold interest payments to residents
Filing correction statements for rectifying reporting mistakes
descriptor.definition: Banking companies, co-operative societies, and specific housing finance public companies must furnish prescribed statements for resident interest payments not exceeding designated thresholds without tax deduction. Non-compliance invites daily monetary penalties under the statute.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard TDS return filing because it specifically tracks exempt or sub-threshold payments made without withholding.

path.name: Chapter 19: Provisions to Counteract Unethical Tax Practices
IMMUNITY FROM IMPOSITION OF PENALTY AND PROSECUTION [SECTION 270AA]
Immunity From Imposition Of Penalty And Prosecution [Section 270AA]

exclusion: cases where the assessee pursues appellate litigation against the assessment order
inclusion: applications for penalty and prosecution immunity upon paying due taxes
statutory bars against granting immunity for suppression or false entries
descriptor.definition: Assessees can apply for immunity from under-reporting penalties and related prosecutions if they pay assessed taxes and interest within the demand period and refrain from filing appeals. Immunity is restricted and cannot be granted if assessments involve severe infractions like misrepresentation or unrecorded entries.
nearby_distinctions: Immunity under Section 270AA requires immediate tax compliance and forfeiture of appeal rights, unlike regular appellate dispute resolution.

path.name: Chapter 19: Provisions to Counteract Unethical Tax Practices

exclusion: Defaults remedied by filing returns prior to the expiration of the relevant assessment year where specified
inclusion: Criminal prosecution for intentional concealment
Mandatory prison terms for tax evasion attempts
descriptor.definition: Willful failures to furnish returns, report foreign assets, or attempts to evade tax carry criminal liability including rigorous imprisonment and fines. These prosecution proceedings operate independently of regular administrative tax assessments or time limitations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from civil penalties by involving criminal court trials, harsher personal liberties restrictions, and mandatory minimum imprisonment terms.

exclusion: Requiring accounts relating to a period more than 3 years prior to the previous year
inclusion: Issuance of notice to furnish returns
Production of accounts and documents
Submission of written information on assets and liabilities
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer may serve a notice to require a return, production of accounts and documents, or written information regarding assets and liabilities. Account production is restricted to periods not exceeding three years prior to the previous year, and asset statements require joint commissioner approval.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from summary processing under section 143(1) by involving active inquiries, document production demands, and notices issued directly by tax authorities.

path.name: Filing of return of income by a business trust [Section 139(4E)]
Filing Of Return Of Income By A Business Trust [Section 139(4E)]

exclusion: Business trusts covered under separate compulsory clauses
inclusion: All business trusts not otherwise filing under alternative provisions
descriptor.definition: Every business trust must furnish a return of its income or loss for every previous year if it has no separate filing mandate under other subsections. Standard procedural rules and provisions applicable to regular income returns govern these business trusts.
nearby_distinctions: Imposes universal annual filing obligations specifically tailored to business trust structures regardless of income performance.

path.name: SUBMISSION OF STATEMENTS BY PRODUCERS OF CINEMATOGRAPH FILMS OR PERSONS ENGAGED IN SPECIFIED ACTIVITY [SECTION 285B]
Submission Of Statements By Producers Of Cinematograph Films Or Persons Engaged In Specified Activity [Section 285B]

exclusion: Aggregate payments to a person not exceeding the 50,000 rupee threshold
Activities outside the defined scope of film production or specified event and media management
inclusion: Producers of cinematograph films
Persons engaged in event management, documentary production, or television/OTT programming
Payments exceeding 50,000 rupees in aggregate to engaged persons
descriptor.definition: Producers of cinematograph films and persons engaged in specified activities must furnish an electronic statement in Form No. 52A within 60 days from the end of the financial year. This filing covers aggregate payments exceeding 50,000 rupees made to persons engaged in production, event management, documentary creation, or television and OTT programming.
nearby_distinctions: Targets industry-specific production and event management reporting under Section 285B, whereas Section 285BA imposes general financial transaction reporting obligations across financial institutions and reporting entities

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
METHOD OF COMPUTING DEDUCTION IN THE CASE OF BUSINESS REORGANISATION OF CO-OPERATIVE BANKS [SECTION 64]

exclusion: Entities without business reorganisation events during the tax year
inclusion: Co-operative banks undergoing business reorganisation
Converted banking companies
descriptor.definition: This provision determines how specific deductions for depreciation, preliminary expenses, amalgamation expenses, and voluntary retirement payments are apportioned between a predecessor co-operative bank and a successor entity when business reorganisation occurs during a tax year. The allocation is calculated proportionally based on the number of days before and after the reorganisation date.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard annual deduction claims by applying a temporal day-count apportionment formula across merging entities.

path.name: Filing of return of income by investment fund Section 139(4F)]
Filing Of Return Of Income By Investment Fund Section 139(4F)]

exclusion: Funds already filing under alternative statutory sub-sections
inclusion: Investment funds referred to in section 115UB
descriptor.definition: Investment funds defined under specific statutory pass-through provisions must furnish an annual return of income or loss for every previous year. General tax provisions regulate these submissions as if they were standard returns filed under primary provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Specifically targets specialized investment funds governed by pass-through taxation mechanics rather than standard corporate entities.

exclusion: Returns where tax deduction certificates were unissued under section 203 or 206C and produced within two years
inclusion: Incomplete computation columns or statements
Missing tax computation statements or tax audit reports
Absence of tax deduction, collection, or advance tax payment proofs
descriptor.definition: An Assessing Officer may flag a return as defective if mandatory computation schedules, tax payment proofs, or required audit reports are missing or incomplete. The taxpayer is given an opportunity to rectify these defects within fifteen days, extendable upon request, to prevent the return from becoming invalid.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from a revised return because it represents a procedural cure initiated by an Assessing Officer notice rather than a voluntary taxpayer correction.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
DEDUCTION AT SOURCE AND ADVANCE PAYMENT [SECTION 190]
Deduction At Source And Advance Payment [Section 190]

exclusion: Post-assessment recovery proceedings initiated without prior collection mechanisms
inclusion: TDS
TCS
Advance tax

(2 Marks)

(iii) No deduction of tax under section 194A is to be made on interest 
income credited or paid to co-operative society engaged in banking 
business.  
Accordingly, Union Bank of India (UBI) is not required to deduct tax at 
source under section 194A on interest on FDR to Urban Co-operative 
Bank. 
Liability to deduct tax at source under section 194N shall not be 
applicable on payment made to co-operative society engaged in 
banking business. Accordingly, Union Bank of India (UBI) is also not

(a) (i)  As per section 194-IA, consideration for transfer of any immovable 
property include all charges in the nature of, inter alia, parking 
charges, generator cost and swimming pool cost.  
In case of more than one transferee, consideration shall be aggregate 
of amount paid by all the transferees for transfer of such property. 
29 
SUGGESTED ANSWERS 
FINAL EXAMINATION: SEPTEMBER 2025 
In the present case, since aggregate value of consideration of both 
transferees i.e., of Mr. A and Mrs. A not less than ` 50 lakhs, tax is 
required to be deducted at source under section 194-IA @1% on ` 94 
lakhs or 1% on ` 47 lakhs by Mr. A and 1% on ` 47 lakhs by Mrs. A 
since consideration of ` 94 lakhs is higher than stamp duty value of  
` 75 lakhs on purchase of flat from M/s XYZ Builders Ltd.

(ii) If Beta Ltd. accepts the enhancement to total income made on 
account of determination of Arm’s length price by the TPO, it has to 
make a secondary adjustment under section 92CE if the primary 
adjustment exceeds ` 1 crore. 
In the present case, the primary adjustment would be USD 2,10,000 
(700 pieces of computers x USD 300 (USD 1400 – USD 1100) which 
exceeds ` 1 crore. 
Accordingly, the excess money i.e., USD 2,10,000 available with 
Robert Inc. has to be repatriated to India within 90 days of the date of 
the order of the Assessing Officer. 
In case of non-repatriation, USD 2,10,000 would be deemed as an 
advance made by the Beta Ltd. to its associated enterprise, Robert 
Inc. 
Interest would be calculated on such advance at the rate of six-month 
LIBOR as on 30th September of the relevant previous year + 3%, since 
the international transaction is denominated in foreign currency. 
Alternatively, Beta Ltd. can opt to pay additional income-tax  
@ 20.9664% (tax @18% plus surcharge @12% plus cess@4%). 
31 
SUGGESTED ANSWERS 
FINAL EXAMINATION: SEPTEMBER 2025 
In such case, Beta Ltd. will not be required to make the secondary 
adjustment and compute interest up to the payment of tax from such 
date.

(b) (i) Beta Ltd., an Indian company and Robert Inc., a company 
incorporated in Country E are deemed to be associated enterprise as 
per section 92A(2), since Robert Inc. holds more than 26% of voting 
power i.e., 30% in Beta Ltd.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
AMOUNTS NOT DEDUCTIBLE IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 35]
Amounts Not Deductible In Certain Circumstances [Section 35]

exclusion: Taxes where statutory relief or exemptions apply without business deduction eligibility
inclusion: Income tax and foreign tax payments eligible for relief
Employer-paid tax on non-monetary employee perquisites
Thirty percent disallowance for resident payments lacking required tax deduction or timely deposit
descriptor.definition: Certain expenditures such as income taxes, foreign taxes eligible for relief, and employer-paid taxes on non-monetary employee perquisites are disallowed as deductions. Furthermore, a specified percentage of sums payable to residents is disallowed if tax deduction at source requirements and subsequent payment timelines are defaulted.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard deductible operating business expenses from statutory disallowances imposed due to tax compliance failures.

path.name: Chapter 6: Income of Other Persons included in Assessee’s Total Income
Clubbing of Income Introduction and Transfer of Income without Asset

exclusion: transfers where both asset and income are legally transferred permanently without retained rights
inclusion: income transferred without transferring the asset
revocable or irrevocable income transfers
descriptor.definition: Clubbing provisions include the income of another person in the assessee's total income to prevent tax avoidance via asset or income diversions. Specifically, if any person transfers income from an asset without transferring the underlying asset itself, such income is taxed in the transferor's hands regardless of whether the transfer is revocable or irrevocable.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard taxation of an assessee's own income by shifting tax liability to the original benefactor under specific anti-avoidance rules.

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS ON BUYBACK OF SHARES OR OTHER SECURITIES [SECTION 69]
Capital Gains on Buyback of Shares or Other Securities

exclusion: Standard non-promoter share transfers governed strictly by general capital gain rates without additional promoter surcharges
inclusion: Consideration received by shareholders on share and security buybacks
Additional tax liabilities for promoters on specific short-term and long-term capital gains
descriptor.definition: Consideration received from a company for the buyback of its shares or specified securities is chargeable as capital gains calculated as the difference between consideration and acquisition cost. Promoters face additional income tax and flat surcharges on such capital gains alongside standard tax rates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard shareholder tax treatment on buybacks from promoter-specific tax obligations that impose additional tier-based levies and flat surcharges.

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS TAXATION FOR NON RESIDENTS

exclusion: Indexation benefits for transfers on or after specific statutory dates
inclusion: Capital gains from transfer of Indian company shares or debentures acquired in foreign exchange
Conversion using applicable telegraphic transfer rates
descriptor.definition: Non-residents transferring capital assets in India are subject to capital gains tax, with specific currency fluctuation benefits applied when foreign exchange is invested. Computations require converting consideration, acquisition cost, and transfer expenses into the initial foreign currency used before reconverting the resulting gain into Indian currency.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard domestic capital gains calculation from foreign currency fluctuation adjusted calculations

exclusion: Persons falling entirely below statutory income and transaction thresholds without mandatory application triggers
inclusion: Persons with income exceeding the maximum unchargeable limit
Businesses with turnover likely to exceed specified monetary limits
Entities entering into high-value financial transactions and their key management personnel
descriptor.definition: Specified categories of taxpayers and entities engaged in high-value financial transactions or meeting income thresholds must mandatorily apply for a Permanent Account Number within prescribed timelines. This requirement extends to key managerial personnel of reporting entities and individuals executing large cash deposits.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct as an identification number allocation framework, whereas section 139 governs return filing procedures.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
SPECIAL TAXATION REGIME FOR INVESTMENT FUNDS AND INCOME RECEIVED FROM SUCH FUNDS [SECTION 224]
Special Taxation Regime for Investment Funds and Income Received from Such Funds

exclusion: Offshore investment income routed through specified alternative investment funds for non-residents under direct investment rules
inclusion: Income distributed by investment funds to resident and non-resident unit holders
Business income taxable directly at the investment fund level
descriptor.definition: Income received by a unit holder from an investment fund is taxed as if the underlying investments were made directly by the unit holder. Investment funds are generally exempt from tax on income other than profits and gains from business or profession, which remains taxable at the fund level.
terminology: Profits and gains from business or profession
nearby_distinctions: Pass-through taxation applies to non-business incomes of investment funds, whereas business profits are taxed directly at the fund level.

exclusion: Data outside official authority possession or information not authorized for upload under relevant tax exchange agreements
inclusion: Information relating to tax deducted or collected at source
Information relating to specified financial transactions and tax payments
Information relating to demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings
descriptor.definition: Tax authorities must upload an annual information statement in Form No. 26AS into an assessee's registered electronic filing portal account within three months of receiving the underlying data. This statement aggregates information on tax deducted or collected at source, specified financial transactions, tax payments, demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings.
nearby_distinctions: Constitutes the consolidated statement uploaded to the taxpayer's portal under Section 285BB, whereas Section 285BA governs the underlying reporting obligations submitted by reporting entities

path.name: Chapter 8: Deductions from Gross Total Income
Deduction in respect of investment in specified assets

exclusion: Deferred annuity contracts
Deductions under the default tax regime
inclusion: Life insurance premium payments for self, spouse, and children
Investments enumerated in Schedule XV
descriptor.definition: Eligible individuals and Hindu Undivided Families shifting out of the default tax regime can claim a deduction up to 150000 for specified investments and contributions made during the tax year. Qualifying life insurance policy premiums are restricted based on the date of issuance relative to the actual capital sum assured.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general deductions by explicitly limiting eligibility to non-default tax regime users and capping contributions at statutory thresholds.

path.name: Charging Provision and Scope of Capital Gains

exclusion: Stock-in-trade held for business or profession
Consumable stores
Raw materials held for business
inclusion: Property of any kind held by an assessee
Securities held by specified Foreign Institutional Investors or investment funds
Unit linked insurance policies without specific exemptions
descriptor.definition: Profits and gains arising from the transfer of a capital asset effected in a tax year are chargeable to income-tax under the head Capital Gains and deemed as income of that specific year. The core elements driving this charge are the identification of a valid capital asset and a recognized transfer.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between items held as business stock-in-trade versus items held as personal investments based on the manner of holding rather than the inherent nature of the asset.

exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
descriptor.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

path.name: Cost of Acquisition for Specific Intangible and Other Rights

exclusion: Tangible assets such as land or buildings
Assets acquired under circumstances not specified in the section
inclusion: Goodwill of a business or profession
Trademark or brand name
Right to manufacture, produce or process any article or thing
Tenancy rights and stage carriage permits
descriptor.definition: The cost of acquisition for specified intangible assets and rights purchased from a previous owner is the actual purchase price. For self-generated assets within this category, the cost of acquisition is treated as nil.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the cost of improvement which is taken as nil for intangible assets under Section 90(1).

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]

exclusion: transactions subject to tax deduction under other provisions where section 194Q priority rules apply
transactions liable to TCS under specific sub-sections of section 206C
inclusion: sum paid or credited for purchasing goods exceeding 50 lakhs rupees in a previous year
buyers with business turnover exceeding 10 crores rupees in the preceding financial year
descriptor.definition: Large business buyers whose preceding financial year turnover exceeds specified monetary limits must deduct tax at source when purchasing goods from a resident seller exceeding aggregate thresholds. The deduction occurs at the time of credit to the seller's account or actual payment, whichever happens earlier.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from TCS provisions under section 206C(1H) by placing the compliance burden directly on the high-turnover buyer rather than the seller.

path.name: ACT TO HAVE EFFECT PENDING LEGISLATIVE PROVISION FOR CHARGE OF TAX [SECTION 294]
Act To Have Effect Pending Legislative Provision For Charge Of Tax [Section 294]

exclusion: Scenarios where regular charging provisions are enacted on or before April 1st
inclusion: Continuation of tax collection mechanisms during legislative delays
Application of the more beneficial tax rate between prior laws and pending bills
descriptor.definition: If a Central Act fails to enact income tax charging provisions by April 1st of an assessment year, the existing tax act remains operational. It continues to function using either the preceding year provisions or the current parliamentary bill proposals, whichever proves more favourable to the assessee.
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a temporary transitional safeguard specifically for tax charging continuity rather than general administrative rule-making.

path.name: Filing of return of income by a business trust [Section 139(4E)]
Filing Of Return Of Income By A Business Trust [Section 139(4E)]

exclusion: Business trusts covered under separate compulsory clauses
inclusion: All business trusts not otherwise filing under alternative provisions
descriptor.definition: Every business trust must furnish a return of its income or loss for every previous year if it has no separate filing mandate under other subsections. Standard procedural rules and provisions applicable to regular income returns govern these business trusts.
nearby_distinctions: Imposes universal annual filing obligations specifically tailored to business trust structures regardless of income performance.

path.name: SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO CONVERSION OF INDIAN BRANCH OF A FOREIGN BANK INTO A SUBSIDIARY COMPANY [CHAPTER XII-BB]
Conversion of Foreign Bank Indian Branch into Subsidiary

exclusion: Conversions executed outside of Reserve Bank of India regulatory frameworks
inclusion: Exemption of capital gains on conversion of foreign bank branches
Transfer of all assets and liabilities to the subsidiary
descriptor.definition: Capital gains arising when a foreign banking company converts its Indian branch into an Indian subsidiary company under an approved Reserve Bank of India scheme are exempt from tax. This exemption requires the complete transfer of all branch assets and liabilities to the new subsidiary under sanctioned amalgamation terms.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes structural corporate branch reorganizations from standard taxable asset transfers
