path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Consequences of failure to deduct or pay
Consequences Of Failure To Deduct Or Pay

exclusion: Standard tax remittance within statutory due dates
Penalties charged without proper opportunity of being heard
inclusion: Interest at 1 percent per month for failure to deduct
Interest at 1.5 percent per month from deduction to payment date
descriptor.definition: Failing to deduct or pay tax makes a person a deemed assessee-in-default, attracting mandatory simple interest liabilities. However, an exception applies if the payee has already reported the income, paid the tax, and an accountant's certificate is furnished.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from routine tax compliance by imposing punitive default status and compounding interest rates for non-compliance.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: rent paid to a business trust being a REIT in respect of directly owned real estate assets
inclusion: payments for land or buildings
rent for plant, machinery, equipment, furniture, or fittings
descriptor.definition: Entities responsible for paying rental income for the use of land, buildings, machinery, plant, equipment, furniture, or fittings to a resident must deduct tax at source. Real estate assets owned directly by a REIT are exempt from this deduction.
nearby_distinctions: Applies distinct tax rates for plant, machinery, and equipment rental compared to land, building, and furniture rental.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Notified National Defence bonds, loans, and specific capital gains bonds
inclusion: Interest on Central or State Government securities
Interest on debentures issued by companies or local authorities
descriptor.definition: Any person paying interest on securities to a resident must deduct income tax at the specified rates upon credit or payment, whichever occurs earlier. Specific government bonds, loans, and notified public sector debentures are exempted from these deduction requirements.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general bank or corporate interest by applying specifically to formal monetary securities and debentures.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payments in respect of deposits under National Savings Scheme, etc. [Section 194EE]
Payments in respect of deposits under National Savings Scheme, etc. [Section 194EE]

exclusion: payments disbursed to the legal heirs of the assessee
inclusion: withdrawals from National Savings Scheme accounts
descriptor.definition: A person responsible for paying amounts from a National Savings Scheme Account must deduct tax at the specified rate upon payment. Payments made to legal heirs are exempt from these tax deduction requirements.
nearby_distinctions: Section 194EE specifically governs NSS account withdrawals, differing from general bank deposit interest provisions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]

exclusion: benefits or perquisites to a resident where aggregate value does not exceed 20,000 rupees in a financial year
providers being individuals or HUFs whose business turnover or professional receipts do not exceed statutory thresholds
inclusion: benefits or perquisites arising from business or exercise of a profession
perquisites provided wholly in kind, partly in kind, or in cash
descriptor.definition: Any person providing business or professional benefits or perquisites to a resident must ensure tax is deducted at source before release, regardless of whether the benefit is in cash, kind, or partly both. If the benefit is wholly or partly in kind and available cash is insufficient to cover tax, the deductor must ensure tax is paid prior to release.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard monetary income TDS by capturing non-monetary or mixed business advantages provided to trade partners or professionals.

path.name: PRESUMPTION AS TO ASSETS, BOOKS OF ACCOUNT, ETC. [SECTION 292C]
Presumption As To Assets, Books Of Account, Etc. [Section 292C]

exclusion: Materials and assets not found in the possession or control of the person during search, survey, or requisition
inclusion: Evidentiary presumptions regarding ownership of seized assets and documents
Assumptions of truth and correct execution for books of account and records
descriptor.definition: Books of account, documents, money, and assets found during searches, surveys, or requisition proceedings are legally presumed to belong to the person in possession. Further presumptions apply that document contents are true, signatures and handwriting belong to the purported authors, and executed documents were duly stamped and executed.
nearby_distinctions: Extends the evidentiary presumptions originally created for search operations to regular assessments and survey proceedings.

path.name: SCHEME FOR SUBMISSION OF RETURNS THROUGH TAX RETURN PREPARERS [SECTION 139B]
SCHEME FOR SUBMISSION OF RETURNS THROUGH TAX RETURN PREPARERS [SECTION 139B]

exclusion: Companies and taxpayers whose accounts require mandatory tax audits under section 44AB or other laws
inclusion: Individuals and Hindu Undivided Families utilizing authorized Tax Return Preparers
Preparation and signature assistance by certified preparers
descriptor.definition: The CBDT is empowered to notify a scheme enabling specified classes of small taxpayers to prepare and file their income returns through authorized Tax Return Preparers. Qualified preparers assist eligible individuals and HUFs while being strictly restricted from acting as preparers if they are bank officers, legal practitioners, chartered accountants, or company employees.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from self-filing or direct professional representation because it provides a dedicated administrative facilitation scheme for smaller taxpayers.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Income categories falling outside employment remuneration
inclusion: Payments chargeable under the head Salaries
descriptor.definition: Every person responsible for disbursing salary income is legally obligated to deduct income tax at the time of payment using the applicable average tax rate. Deductors must collect tax regime intentions from employees to correctly apply default or opted tax configurations.
nearby_distinctions: Applies strictly to employer-employee remuneration payouts unlike contract or professional fee deductions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: payments made to the Government
payments made to specified banking companies or co-operative societies
inclusion: cash payments exceeding 1 crore rupees generally
cash payments exceeding 20 lakhs rupees for non-filers of returns
descriptor.definition: Banking institutions, co-operative banks, and post offices must deduct tax at source on cash withdrawals exceeding specific statutory thresholds during a previous year. Higher tax rates and lower withdrawal limits apply to recipients who have failed to file income tax returns for the preceding three assessment years.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard payment-based TDS provisions by targeting physical cash withdrawals from bank accounts based on aggregate annual volume.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
PENAL CONSEQUENCES FOR FAILURE TO DEDUCT OR COLLECT OR PAY TAX AT SOURCE
Penal Consequences For Failure To Deduct Or Collect Or Pay Tax At Source

exclusion: Prosecution under section 276B if payment is made to the credit of the Central Government on or before the prescribed statement filing time w.e.f. 1.10.2024
inclusion: Penalty equal to un-deducted tax under section 271C
Rigorous imprisonment from 3 months to 7 years with fine for failure to pay deducted tax under section 276B
Penalty equal to un-collected tax under section 271CA
Rigorous imprisonment from 3 months to 7 years with fine for failure to pay collected tax under section 276BB
Penalties for failure to pay or ensure payment when consideration is in kind under relevant provisos
descriptor.definition: Statutory penalties and rigorous imprisonment are attracted when a person fails to deduct tax at source, collect tax at source, or remit such withheld amounts to the credit of the Central Government. These provisions apply equivalently whether the underlying consideration is monetary or delivered in kind under specific statutory provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between civil monetary penalties levied by the Joint Commissioner and criminal prosecution involving rigorous imprisonment.
Distinguishes between defaults relating to tax deduction at source versus tax collection at source.

exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
descriptor.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward
NO SET OFF OF LOSSES AGAINST UNDISCLOSED INCOME CONSEQUENT TO SEARCH, REQUISITION AND SURVEY [SECTION 120]
NO SET OFF OF LOSSES AGAINST UNDISCLOSED INCOME CONSEQUENT TO SEARCH, REQUISITION AND SURVEY [SECTION 120]

exclusion: surveys conducted under section 253(4)
inclusion: prohibition of loss set-off against undisclosed assets or transactions
restriction on offsetting unabsorbed depreciation against discovered income
descriptor.definition: Brought forward losses, current losses, and unabsorbed depreciation cannot be set off against undisclosed income uncovered during statutory searches, requisitions, or qualifying surveys. Undisclosed income encompasses unrecorded assets, transactions, or incorrect expense and deduction claims for the block period.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard business income and regular loss adjustments from punitive non-set-off rules applied exclusively to discovered undisclosed income.

path.name: REFERENCE TO PRINCIPAL COMMISSIONER OR COMMISSIONER IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 144BA]
Reference To Principal Commissioner Or Commissioner In Certain Cases

exclusion: Arrangements finalized without giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard
inclusion: References for declaring arrangements as impermissible avoidance arrangements
Approving Panel binding directions
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer can refer an arrangement to the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner to declare it an impermissible avoidance arrangement. The authority issues notices, evaluates objections, and may refer the matter to an Approving Panel which issues binding directions for completion.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard tax evasion inquiries by targeting complex tax avoidance arrangements through a specialized multi-tier review involving the Principal Commissioner and Approving Panel.

path.name: WITHHOLDING TAX PROVISIONS FOR NON- RESIDENTS
Withholding Tax on Non-Resident Salaries and Perquisites

exclusion: Salaries for services rendered entirely outside India
inclusion: Salary income deemed to accrue in India due to services rendered locally
Employer payment of tax on non-monetary perquisites without employee deduction
Deferred TDS on specified securities or sweat equity from eligible startups
descriptor.definition: Employers must deduct withholding tax at applicable rates on salary payments to non-residents when services are rendered within India. Special provisions govern tax calculation on non-monetary perquisites and allow deferred tax payment timelines for specified startup securities.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes monetary salary withholding from non-monetary perquisite tax handling

path.name: PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]
PERSONS AUTHORISED TO VERIFY RETURN OF INCOME [SECTION 140]

exclusion: Unauthorized third parties lacking specific legal designation or valid power of attorney
inclusion: Assessee himself for individuals under normal circumstances
Authorized power-of-attorney holders during absence or incapacity
Managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals for companies
descriptor.definition: Statutory provisions explicitly designate which individuals possess the legal authority to sign and verify income tax returns on behalf of different assessee types. Depending on circumstances such as absence, mental incapacity, winding up, or corporate insolvency, specific representatives like power-of-attorney holders, managing directors, liquidators, or insolvency professionals are authorized.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses strictly on the legal competence to sign and authenticate return documents, separate from the actual preparation or computation of income.

path.name: POWER OF ASSESSING OFFICER TO MAKE A REFERENCE TO THE VALUATION OFFICER [SECTION 142A]
Power Of Assessing Officer To Make A Reference To The Valuation Officer [Section 142A]

exclusion: References made without affording an opportunity of being heard before final assessment integration
inclusion: Reference for estimating fair market value of assets, properties, or investments
Best judgment estimation upon non-cooperation
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer can reference a Valuation Officer to estimate the fair market value or value of any asset, property, or investment for assessment purposes. The Valuation Officer must submit the report within six months, and the Assessing Officer utilizes it after granting the assessee a hearing opportunity.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from special audits under section 142(2A) as it focuses strictly on estimating asset, property, or investment values through a specialized Valuation Officer rather than financial account auditing.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities
EXEMPTION IN RESPECT OF INCOME OF CERTAIN UNIVERSITIES, EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, HOSPITALS, MEDICAL INSTITUTIONS ETC.
Exemption for Certain Educational and Medical Institutions

exclusion: Institutions operating for profit
Hospitals or educational institutions exceeding the financial receipt threshold without government financing
inclusion: Universities wholly or substantially financed by the government
Hospitals existing solely for philanthropic purposes and substantially financed by the government
Educational and medical institutions with aggregate annual receipts not exceeding five crore rupees
descriptor.definition: Specific universities, educational institutions, hospitals, and medical institutions are exempt from income tax on their total income if they are wholly or substantially financed by the government, or if their aggregate annual receipts do not exceed five crore rupees. An institution is considered substantially financed when government grants exceed 50 percent of its total receipts including donations during the tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes government-backed or smaller scale medical and educational bodies from standard commercial enterprises and general trusts.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward
CARRY FORWARD AND SET OFF OF LOSSES NOT PERMISSIBLE IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 119]
CARRY FORWARD AND SET OFF OF LOSSES NOT PERMISSIBLE IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 119]

exclusion: carry forward of partner's proportionate loss upon retirement or death
carry forward of predecessor business losses by non-inheriting successors
inclusion: unabsorbed depreciation carry forward despite partnership constitution changes
business loss carry forward by legal heirs in succession by inheritance
descriptor.definition: Unabsorbed business losses proportionate to a retired or deceased partner cannot be carried forward upon a firm constitution change, though unabsorbed depreciation remains eligible. Similarly, business succession otherwise than by inheritance bars the successor from carrying forward the predecessor's losses, whereas succession by inheritance permits such carry forward.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between restrictions on unabsorbed business losses versus unabsorbed depreciation during constitution changes or non-inheritance successions.

exclusion: Rules that conflict with, restrict, or adversely affect the operative effect of parent act sections
inclusion: Rule-making authority of the Board
Statutory force and parliamentary oversight of formulated rules
descriptor.definition: The Central Board of Direct Taxes is empowered to formulate subordinate rules under central government control to implement the Act, which must be placed before Parliament. These rules carry statutory force equivalent to enactment sections provided they remain consistent with, supplementary to, and non-derogatory of the primary statute.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from primary legislative acts by being subordinate executive regulations that must strictly conform to the parent statute's mandate.

exclusion: Incomes explicitly exempt from charge under statutory provisions
inclusion: Total income of persons specified under the Act
Tax rates specified by the Finance Act or Income-tax Act, 2025
descriptor.definition: Income-tax is charged on the total income of every person for the tax year at the rates prescribed by the annual Finance Act or the Income-tax Act, 2025. This charging provision forms the foundational basis from which any tax liability legally originates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from computational provisions by serving strictly as the legal origin of tax liability.

path.name: FACILITY FOR ACCEPTING PAYMENT THROUGH PRESCRIBED ELECTRONIC MODES [SECTION 269SU]
Facility For Accepting Payment Through Prescribed Electronic Modes [Section 269Su]

exclusion: Assessees whose gross receipts do not exceed the 50 crore rupee threshold
Specified persons having exclusively B2B transactions with at least 95 percent non-cash receipts
inclusion: Businesses with gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees
RuPay debit card payment facilities
BHIM-UPI and BHIM-UPI QR code payment facilities
descriptor.definition: Businesses with total sales, turnover, or gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees in the preceding financial year must provide facilities for accepting payments through prescribed electronic modes. Non-compliance attracts a daily penalty under section 271DB, while system providers are prohibited from imposing charges for using these mandated modes.
nearby_distinctions: Mandates the provision of electronic payment acceptance facilities rather than restricting transaction modes like sections 269SS, 269ST, and 269T

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
EXPENSES OR PAYMENTS NOT DEDUCTIBLE IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 36]
Expenses Or Payments Not Deductible In Certain Circumstances [Section 36]

exclusion: Reasonable payments conforming to fair market value and legitimate business requirements
inclusion: Payments made to relatives, directors, partners, or persons with substantial interest
Portion of expenditure deemed excessive relative to fair market value or business needs
descriptor.definition: Expenditures resulting from transactions with specified related persons can be restricted if the Assessing Officer determines they are excessive or unreasonable. This assessment considers fair market values, legitimate business needs, and benefits derived by the assessee.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes arm's length commercial transactions from related-party dealings subject to reasonableness scrutiny.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment on transfer of certain immovable property other than agricultural land [Section 194-IA]
Payment on transfer of certain immovable property other than agricultural land [Section 194-IA]

exclusion: rural agricultural land
compulsory acquisitions
inclusion: consideration for transfer of land other than rural agricultural land
buildings or parts of buildings
incidental charges like club membership and parking fees
descriptor.definition: Transferees acquiring immovable property other than rural agricultural land from a resident must deduct tax from the consideration or stamp duty value. Compulsory acquisitions are excluded as they fall under alternative provisions.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike compulsory property acquisitions covered under Section 194LA, standard voluntary property transfers fall under Section 194-IA.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]

exclusion: individuals and HUFs required to deduct tax under Sections 194C, 194H, or 194J
inclusion: contract work payments
commission or brokerage
fees for professional services made by non-audit individuals and HUFs
descriptor.definition: Individuals and HUFs not subject to regular business audit requirements who pay substantial sums for contract work, commission, brokerage, or professional services must deduct tax at source. Taxpayers already obligated to deduct tax under specific contractor, commission, or professional sections are excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Serves as a catch-all provision for individual and HUF payees who exceed high financial thresholds but lack business audit obligations.

path.name: Chapter 8: Deductions from Gross Total Income
Deduction in respect of investment in specified assets

exclusion: Deferred annuity contracts
Deductions under the default tax regime
inclusion: Life insurance premium payments for self, spouse, and children
Investments enumerated in Schedule XV
descriptor.definition: Eligible individuals and Hindu Undivided Families shifting out of the default tax regime can claim a deduction up to 150000 for specified investments and contributions made during the tax year. Qualifying life insurance policy premiums are restricted based on the date of issuance relative to the actual capital sum assured.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general deductions by explicitly limiting eligibility to non-default tax regime users and capping contributions at statutory thresholds.

textbook_references.download_url: https://resource.cdn.icai.org/94202CHP-8 Deduction from Gross Total Income.pdf

exclusion: Receipts by the Government, banking companies, post office savings banks, or co-operative banks
Transactions of the nature referred to in section 269SS
Cash withdrawals by any person from a bank, co-operative bank, or post office savings bank
inclusion: Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in aggregate from a person in a day
Receipts of 2,00,000 rupees or more in respect of a single transaction
Receipts relating to one event or occasion from a person
descriptor.definition: Receiving an amount of 2,00,000 rupees or more is prohibited unless executed through account payee instruments, electronic clearing systems, or prescribed electronic modes. This restriction applies to daily aggregates from a single person, single transactions, or transactions relating to a single event or occasion.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 269SS which specifically targets loans, deposits, and immovable property advances
Applies a higher monetary threshold of 2,00,000 rupees compared to the 20,000 rupees limit under Section 269SS and Section 269T

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Assessees whose computed advance tax liability falls below the statutory threshold of 10000 rupees
inclusion: Tax payment obligations on current financial year income
Exemptions for resident individuals aged 60 or above without business income
descriptor.definition: Assessees must discharge their tax liability on current income progressively during the financial year if the total advance tax payable meets the statutory threshold. Resident senior citizens with passive income and no business profits are exempt from this requirement.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from self-assessment tax or tax deducted at source by enforcing mandatory installment payments ahead of the assessment year based on estimated current earnings.

path.name: RESIDENTIAL STATUS AND SCOPE OF TOTAL INCOME

exclusion: Citizenship as a determinant of tax residency
inclusion: Stay in territorial waters
Stay on ships or boats moored in Indian territorial waters
Both arrival and departure dates counted as days in India
descriptor.definition: An individual's residential status depends on physical stay duration in India during the relevant previous year and preceding years. Citizenship or place of birth does not determine residential status.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes individual residency criteria from corporate residency

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS ON DISTRIBUTION OF ASSETS BY COMPANIES IN LIQUIDATION [SECTION 68]
Capital Gains on Distribution of Assets by Companies in Liquidation

exclusion: Distribution events treated as company transfers when liquidators sell assets directly prior to distribution
inclusion: Shareholder capital gains on money or assets received during company liquidation
Fair market value adoption as cost of acquisition for subsequent asset sales by shareholders
descriptor.definition: Asset distributions by a liquidated company to its shareholders are not treated as transfers at the company level, while shareholders face capital gains tax based on the market value of received assets minus accumulated profit components. Portions of distributions attributable to accumulated profits are treated separately as dividend income under other income sources.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes company-level exemption from asset distribution against shareholder-level taxation which splits distributions into deemed dividends and capital gains.

path.name: PROVISIONAL ATTACHMENT TO PROTECT THE INTEREST OF THE REVENUE [SECTION 281B]
Provisional Attachment To Protect The Interest Of The Revenue [Section 281B]

exclusion: Extensions exceeding a total period of two years or sixty days after assessment/reassessment, whichever is later
inclusion: Provisional attachment of property during pending assessment or reassessment
Attachments for anticipated penalty under section 271AAD exceeding two crore rupees
Revocation of attachment upon furnishing a scheduled bank guarantee
descriptor.definition: Assessing officers are empowered to provisionally attach an assessee's property during pending assessment, reassessment, or penalty proceedings with high-ranking administrative approval to protect revenue interests. Such attachments remain valid for six months, extendable up to two years or sixty days post-assessment, but can be revoked if the assessee furnishes a scheduled bank guarantee.
nearby_distinctions: Acts as a precautionary attachment mechanism during active proceedings, distinct from Section 281 which retroactively voids fraudulent transfers

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
TDS on certain payment by e-commerce operator to e-commerce participant [Section 194-O]
TDS on certain payment by e-commerce operator to e-commerce participant [Section 194-O]

exclusion: sums paid to individual or HUF participants with gross sales up to 5 lakh rupees who have furnished PAN or Aadhaar
advertisement hosting services not connected with the sale of goods or services
inclusion: gross amount of sales of goods or provision of services facilitated through digital platforms
direct payments made by purchasers to participants
descriptor.definition: E-commerce operators facilitating the sale of goods or provision of services by participants through digital platforms are required to deduct tax at source on the gross transaction value. Direct payments made by purchasers to participants are deemed to be amounts credited or paid by the e-commerce operator for deduction purposes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard business payment deductions by applying specifically to digital platform facilitators governing multi-party e-commerce transactions.

path.name: Fee for default in furnishing return of income [Section 234F]
Fee for default in furnishing return of income [Section 234F]

exclusion: Timely filed returns complying with prescribed deadlines
inclusion: Default in furnishing return of income within the time limit under section 139(1)
descriptor.definition: A monetary fee is levied when a person mandated to file an income return fails to complete the submission within the specified statutory time limit. A tiered fee structure applies based on whether total income crosses the statutory threshold amount.
nearby_distinctions: Represents a specific penal fee for filing delays, distinct from substantive tax liabilities or interest calculations.

path.name: Chapter 2: Incomes which do not form part of Total Income
RESTRICTIONS ON ALLOWABILITY OF EXPENDITURE [SECTION 14 READ WITH RULE 14]

exclusion: Expenditures incurred solely in relation to taxable income streams
inclusion: Direct expenditure relating to exempt income
Indirect expenditure computed as a percentage of investment balances under prescribed rules
descriptor.definition: Expenditures incurred in relation to income that does not form part of total income are disallowed as deductions. This disallowance applies regardless of whether the corresponding exempt income was actually accrued, arisen, or received during the tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between deductible business expenses tied to taxable revenues and statutory disallowances mandated for expenses linked to tax-free receipts

path.name: LIABILITY OF SUCCESSOR TO BUSINESS IN RESPECT OF TAX CHARGEABLE FROM THE PREDECESSOR [SECTION 313]
Liability of Successor to Business in Respect of Tax Chargeable from Predecessor

exclusion: Liabilities unrelated to the transferred business operations prior to succession
Unrelated third-party debts
inclusion: Apportionment of income between predecessor and successor for the succession year
Transfer of assessment proceedings pending before courts or tribunals
descriptor.definition: When a business or profession is transferred, the predecessor and successor are independently assessed for the income earned during their respective operational periods within that tax year. If the predecessor cannot be located, the successor inherits the tax liability for the succession year and the preceding year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between ongoing separate assessments during normal succession versus unified successor liability when the predecessor is untraceable

path.name: ADVANCE RULING TO BE VOID IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 245T]
Void Advance Rulings and Board Powers

exclusion: Civil court status for criminal procedure provisions affecting the administration of justice
inclusion: Declarations of nullity due to factual misrepresentation
Civil court powers for evidence collection and inspection
descriptor.definition: An advance ruling obtained through fraud or misrepresentation may be declared void ab initio by the Board. The Board possesses civil court powers for discovery, enforcing attendance, and examining witnesses under oath during judicial proceedings.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes administrative voiding due to fraud from normal appellate reversals.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment of compensation on acquisition of certain immovable property [Section 194LA]
Payment of compensation on acquisition of certain immovable property [Section 194LA]

exclusion: agricultural land
awards exempted under Section 96 of the Land Acquisition Act 2013
inclusion: compensation and enhanced consideration for compulsory property acquisition
descriptor.definition: Payers disbursing compensation or consideration for the compulsory acquisition of immovable property other than agricultural land must deduct tax at source. Awards exempted under specific land acquisition transparency legislation are excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Restricted exclusively to compulsory acquisitions under statutory laws rather than voluntary real estate transfers.
instrument_references: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward

exclusion: Inter-source set-off against casual income like lotteries and betting
Set-off of long-term capital loss against short-term capital gain
inclusion: Set-off of loss from one house property against another house property
Set-off of loss from one non-speculation business against another non-speculation business
descriptor.definition: Losses incurred from any source under a specific head of income can generally be offset against income from another source under the same head during the same tax year. However, certain restrictions apply to specific categories such as capital losses, speculation business, specified activities, and casual winnings.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes source-level adjustments within a single income head from inter-head adjustments across different income heads.

path.name: Chapter 7: Set Off or Carry Forward

exclusion: Setting off capital gains losses against any other head
Setting off business losses against salary income
inclusion: Adjusting business losses against other heads except salaries
Setting off house property loss up to specified monetary limits against other heads under the default regime
descriptor.definition: Losses computed under one head of income may be adjusted against income under another head within the same tax year, excluding capital gains. Specific restrictions apply, such as business losses not being adjustable against salary income and house property losses being capped or restricted depending on the tax regime.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes inter-head adjustments from inter-source adjustments restricted strictly within the same head.

path.name: Chapter 10: Assessment of Trusts and Institutions, Political Parties and Other Special Entities

exclusion: Trusts with specific, determinate beneficiary shares
Exempt provident, superannuation, or gratuity funds meeting specific conditions
inclusion: Trusts with unknown or indeterminate beneficiary shares
Representative assessees managing property under court orders or trust deeds
descriptor.definition: Discretionary trusts, where income is not specifically receivable on behalf of a single person or individual shares are indeterminate, are generally taxed at the maximum marginal rate. Specific statutory exceptions apply under conditions such as will-created trusts, certain dependent relative trusts, and employee benefit funds.
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with determinate trusts where beneficiary shares are known and taxed accordingly rather than at the maximum marginal rate.

exclusion: Applications submitted without proof of required fee payment
inclusion: Applications via registered e-mail address
Tiered fee structures based on transaction scale
descriptor.definition: An eligible person may apply for an advance ruling in quadruplicate through electronic means accompanied by prescribed fees based on transaction value. Applicants retain the right to withdraw their application within a specific statutory window.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes filing procedures and sliding-scale fees from standard tax return filings.

parts.answer_text:
(ii) M/s Seal India Pvt. Ltd. is required to deduct tax at source on 
commission paid to Mr. Prakash under section 194H @5% till 
30.9.2024 and @2% from 1.10.2024, being sum exceeding ` 15,000.  
Reimbursement of expenses of ` 1 lakh for booking air tickets for  
Mr. Prakash and his family other incentive of ` 60,000 and laptop of  
` 60,000 for achieving sale target is benefit or perquisite arising to  
Mr. Prakash from his business or the exercise of his profession, being

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
TDS on certain payment by e-commerce operator to e-commerce participant [Section 194-O]
TDS on certain payment by e-commerce operator to e-commerce participant [Section 194-O]

exclusion: sums paid to individual or HUF participants with gross sales up to 5 lakh rupees who have furnished PAN or Aadhaar
advertisement hosting services not connected with the sale of goods or services
inclusion: gross amount of sales of goods or provision of services facilitated through digital platforms
direct payments made by purchasers to participants
descriptor.definition: E-commerce operators facilitating the sale of goods or provision of services by participants through digital platforms are required to deduct tax at source on the gross transaction value. Direct payments made by purchasers to participants are deemed to be amounts credited or paid by the e-commerce operator for deduction purposes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard business payment deductions by applying specifically to digital platform facilitators governing multi-party e-commerce transactions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]
Deduction of tax at source on purchase of goods [Section 194Q]

exclusion: transactions subject to tax deduction under other provisions where section 194Q priority rules apply
transactions liable to TCS under specific sub-sections of section 206C
inclusion: sum paid or credited for purchasing goods exceeding 50 lakhs rupees in a previous year
buyers with business turnover exceeding 10 crores rupees in the preceding financial year
descriptor.definition: Large business buyers whose preceding financial year turnover exceeds specified monetary limits must deduct tax at source when purchasing goods from a resident seller exceeding aggregate thresholds. The deduction occurs at the time of credit to the seller's account or actual payment, whichever happens earlier.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from TCS provisions under section 206C(1H) by placing the compliance burden directly on the high-turnover buyer rather than the seller.

path.name: Transfer Pricing in Relation to International Transactions

exclusion: Domestic transactions between fully resident independent parties
inclusion: Purchase, sale, or lease of tangible or intangible property
Provision of services and lending or borrowing money
Cost-sharing arrangements and expense allocations
descriptor.definition: Chapter X of the tax statute provides a statutory framework to compute reasonable profits and curb base erosion from international transactions between associated enterprises. It mandates that qualifying transactions involving non-residents must be executed at an arm's length price that increases income or reduces losses.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from domestic tax computations by explicitly requiring cross-border international transaction triggers.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]

exclusion: benefits or perquisites to a resident where aggregate value does not exceed 20,000 rupees in a financial year
providers being individuals or HUFs whose business turnover or professional receipts do not exceed statutory thresholds
inclusion: benefits or perquisites arising from business or exercise of a profession
perquisites provided wholly in kind, partly in kind, or in cash
descriptor.definition: Any person providing business or professional benefits or perquisites to a resident must ensure tax is deducted at source before release, regardless of whether the benefit is in cash, kind, or partly both. If the benefit is wholly or partly in kind and available cash is insufficient to cover tax, the deductor must ensure tax is paid prior to release.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard monetary income TDS by capturing non-monetary or mixed business advantages provided to trade partners or professionals.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Mining and quarrying of mineral oil
Transactions covered by manufacturing declarations submitted by resident buyers
inclusion: Tax collection on specified forest produce, scrap, and minerals
Tax collection on lease or license of parking lots and mines
descriptor.definition: Sellers of specified goods and grantors of specific business leases or licenses are legally mandated to collect tax at source from buyers or licensees at prescribed percentages. Exemptions apply when resident buyers provide formal declarations that goods are intended for manufacturing or power generation rather than trading.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from tax deduction at source (TDS) as it is collected directly by sellers or licensors from buyers or lessees during commercial sales or transfers.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: insurance commission
professional services
inclusion: payments for services rendered in the course of buying or selling goods
transactions relating to assets or valuable articles other than securities
descriptor.definition: Specified payers making payments by way of commission or brokerage to a resident must deduct tax at source. Professional services are explicitly excluded from the scope of this provision.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from insurance commission which is covered under a separate section, and excludes professional services governed under Section 194J.

exclusion: Non-corporate entities like sole proprietorships unless declared
Standard partnership firms
inclusion: Indian companies
Foreign entities incorporated outside India
Institutions declared as companies by CBDT order
descriptor.definition: A company is treated as a distinct person for assessment purposes under the tax statute, encompassing Indian companies, foreign bodies corporate, and specified notified institutions. The statutory tax framework differentiates between domestic and foreign entities, applying distinct tax rates and surcharges based on turnover thresholds and company status.
nearby_distinctions: Distinction between domestic companies taxed at tiered rates versus foreign companies subject to standard foreign tax rates

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Capital receipts generally excluded from business income computations
inclusion: Profits realized in cash or in kind
Single trade ventures if undertaken with profit intent
Vocations included under professional scope
descriptor.definition: Business encompasses trade, commerce, manufacture, or any trade adventure pursued with a profit motive, whereas profession denotes occupations requiring specialized learning and includes vocations. Profits from both categories are generally taxable under the same head, while differences persist primarily for tax audit and presumptive taxation thresholds.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between continuous commercial operations and isolated trade adventures, and differentiates traditional businesses from learned professions.

exclusion: Returns filed without prior proof of tax and interest payment
inclusion: Tax payment prior to submission
Interest and fee calculations
Adjustments for TDS, TCS, and advance tax
descriptor.definition: Before furnishing an updated return, the assessee must pay the due tax, additional income-tax, interest, and fees. Computations account for advance tax, tax deducted or collected at source, and eligible tax credits or reliefs.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regular return filing by the mandatory prepayment of an additional income-tax component alongside applicable interest and fees before submission.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
SPECIAL PROVISION FOR COMPUTING PROFITS AND GAINS OF BUSINESS OR PROFESSION ON PRESUMPTIVE BASIS IN CASE OF CERTAIN RESIDENTS [SECTION 58]

exclusion: Assessees claiming specific deductions under Chapter VIII Part C
inclusion: Resident individuals, HUFs, and partnership firms excluding LLPs
Businesses with turnover up to 2 crores or 3 crores subject to cash transaction limits
descriptor.definition: Eligible resident taxpayers engaged in specified businesses with turnover below statutory limits can compute their business profits using pre-determined presumptive rates. The taxable profit is calculated based on percentages of turnover received via specified digital modes versus cash.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from normal computation provisions by eliminating the need to maintain detailed expense records if statutory profit margins are met.

path.name: INTRODUCTION OF SPECIFIC ANTI AVOIDANCE MEASURES IN RESPECT OF TRANSACTIONS WITH PERSONS LOCATED IN NOTIFIED JURISDICTIONAL AREA [SECTION 94A]
Specific Anti-Avoiadance Measures for Notified Jurisdictional Areas

exclusion: Benefit of permissible statutory price variations
inclusion: Transactions with persons located in notified tax jurisdictions
Mandatory application of transfer pricing provisions to notified area deals
descriptor.definition: Anti-avoidance rules target transactions involving persons located in notified territories that lack effective information exchange mechanisms with India. Transactions with entities in a notified jurisdictional area are deemed international transactions, and the parties are treated as associated enterprises subject to transfer pricing.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard transfer pricing by automatically presuming associated enterprise status based on geographic location rather than equity or management control.

exclusion: Transactions between completely unrelated and independent third parties
inclusion: Intra-group transfer of physical goods
Provision of services between associated enterprises
Transfer of intangible property
descriptor.definition: Transfer pricing refers to the pricing of goods, services, and intangible property transferred between associated enterprises within a multinational group. It is utilized to prevent profit shifting and base erosion across tax jurisdictions through the application of the arm's length principle.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from domestic pricing by the involvement of multiple tax jurisdictions and associated enterprise controls.

exclusion: Data outside official authority possession or information not authorized for upload under relevant tax exchange agreements
inclusion: Information relating to tax deducted or collected at source
Information relating to specified financial transactions and tax payments
Information relating to demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings
descriptor.definition: Tax authorities must upload an annual information statement in Form No. 26AS into an assessee's registered electronic filing portal account within three months of receiving the underlying data. This statement aggregates information on tax deducted or collected at source, specified financial transactions, tax payments, demands, refunds, and pending or completed proceedings.
nearby_distinctions: Constitutes the consolidated statement uploaded to the taxpayer's portal under Section 285BB, whereas Section 285BA governs the underlying reporting obligations submitted by reporting entities

path.name: Particulars to be furnished with the return [section 139(6)]
Particulars to be furnished with the return [section 139(6)]

exclusion: General business audit reports governed under separate sub-sections like section 139(6A)
inclusion: Income exempt from tax
Assets held as beneficial owner or otherwise
Bank account and credit card details
Expenditure exceeding prescribed limits
descriptor.definition: Prescribed return forms require specified categories of taxpayers to disclose comprehensive financial details alongside their income declarations. These mandatory disclosures encompass exempt income, beneficial or other asset holdings, bank accounts, credit cards, and specified high-value outgoings.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from basic income computation schedules by focusing on specific asset ownership, bank linkages, and external financial indicators.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Taxpayers not meeting statutory income or turnover thresholds and not carrying on specified professions
inclusion: Specified professions like legal, medical, and engineering
Businesses exceeding specified income or turnover limits in preceding years
descriptor.definition: Specified professionals and general business taxpayers meeting specific income or turnover thresholds must maintain accounting records and documents to facilitate income computation by the Assessing Officer. These records can be kept in written, electronic, digital, cloud-based, or printed formats.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from tax audit requirements by focusing on day-to-day record keeping rather than formal chartered accountant verification.

path.name: Charging Provision and Scope of Capital Gains

exclusion: Stock-in-trade held for business or profession
Consumable stores
Raw materials held for business
inclusion: Property of any kind held by an assessee
Securities held by specified Foreign Institutional Investors or investment funds
Unit linked insurance policies without specific exemptions
descriptor.definition: Profits and gains arising from the transfer of a capital asset effected in a tax year are chargeable to income-tax under the head Capital Gains and deemed as income of that specific year. The core elements driving this charge are the identification of a valid capital asset and a recognized transfer.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between items held as business stock-in-trade versus items held as personal investments based on the manner of holding rather than the inherent nature of the asset.

path.name: Chapter 20: Tax Audit and Ethical Compliances
Mandatory Tax Audit Provisions and Thresholds

exclusion: Assessees declaring profits in accordance with section 44AD(1) or 44ADA(1)
inclusion: Businesses with total sales exceeding specific statutory limits
Professions with gross receipts exceeding fifty lakh rupees
Assessees claiming lower profits than presumptive rates under designated sections
descriptor.definition: Certain businesses and professions must get their accounts audited by a chartered accountant before the specified date when financial metrics cross prescribed monetary thresholds. Exceptions and specific conditions regarding cash receipts and payments apply to business turnovers within defined limits.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes business turnover thresholds from professional gross receipt thresholds and presumptive income reporting rules.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: employer-paid tax on non-monetary perquisites
tax deducted under section 194N on cash withdrawals
inclusion: all sums deducted under Chapter XVII TDS provisions
eligible foreign income tax deductions allowed as credit
descriptor.definition: All taxes deducted under statutory provisions and eligible foreign tax deductions are treated as income received when computing an assessee's total income. Specific statutory outflows, such as non-monetary perquisite taxes paid by employers and certain cash withdrawal deductions, are excluded from this income-inclusion rule.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from gross cash receipts by legally mandating the addition of withheld tax amounts back into the taxpayer's computed income base.

exclusion: Transactions explicitly shielded from transfer status under statutory exemptions
inclusion: Sale, exchange, or relinquishment of an asset
Conversion of capital assets into business stock-in-trade
Granting possession of immovable property under part-performance contracts
descriptor.definition: Transfer encompasses an inclusive range of transactions regarding capital assets, including sales, exchanges, relinquishments, extinguishment of rights, and compulsory acquisitions. It also covers asset conversions to stock-in-trade, zero coupon bond maturities, and arrangements enabling immovable property enjoyment.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard conveyances from constructive transfers such as part-performance possession, corporate conversions, and bond maturities that lack traditional registered deeds.

path.name: OBLIGATION TO FURNISH STATEMENT OF FINANCIAL TRANSACTION OR REPORTABLE ACCOUNT [SECTION 285BA]
Obligation To Furnish Statement Of Financial Transaction Or Reportable Account [Section 285Ba]

exclusion: Entities outside the designated categories of reporting persons and financial institutions defined under the section
inclusion: Transactions of purchase, sale, or exchange of goods, property, or rights
Transactions for rendering services or under works contracts
Transactions involving investments made, expenditures incurred, or loans taken
descriptor.definition: Specified entities, including reporting financial institutions, registrars, and government offices maintaining books or records, must furnish statements regarding specified financial transactions or reportable accounts to income-tax authorities. These prescribed transactions encompass property purchases, service rendering, works contracts, investments, expenditures, and loan takings.
nearby_distinctions: Imposes broad financial transaction reporting obligations across designated institutional entities, whereas Section 285B is strictly confined to film producers and specified media/event activities

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]
Payment made by an individual or a HUF for contract work or by way of commission or brokerage or fees for professional services [Section 194M]

exclusion: individuals and HUFs required to deduct tax under Sections 194C, 194H, or 194J
inclusion: contract work payments
commission or brokerage
fees for professional services made by non-audit individuals and HUFs
descriptor.definition: Individuals and HUFs not subject to regular business audit requirements who pay substantial sums for contract work, commission, brokerage, or professional services must deduct tax at source. Taxpayers already obligated to deduct tax under specific contractor, commission, or professional sections are excluded.
nearby_distinctions: Serves as a catch-all provision for individual and HUF payees who exceed high financial thresholds but lack business audit obligations.

path.name: MONETARY LIMITS FOR REGULATING FILING OF APPEALS BY INCOME TAX AUTHORITIES [SECTION 268A]
Monetary Limits for Regulating Filing of Appeals by Income Tax Authorities

exclusion: Appeals exceeding the specified monetary cutoffs where merits justify litigation
inclusion: Departmental appeals restricted by prescribed monetary thresholds
Future filings on identical issues for other assessment years or assessees
descriptor.definition: The central board is empowered to set financial thresholds that regulate when tax authorities can file appeals or reference applications before tribunals and courts. Failure to appeal in a specific case due to these monetary limits does not prevent the authority from litigating the same issue in other assessment years or against different assessees.
nearby_distinctions: Regulates administrative discretion to litigate based on financial stakes rather than the legal merit of the underlying dispute.

path.name: RESIDENTIAL STATUS AND SCOPE OF TOTAL INCOME

exclusion: Citizenship as a determinant of tax residency
inclusion: Stay in territorial waters
Stay on ships or boats moored in Indian territorial waters
Both arrival and departure dates counted as days in India
descriptor.definition: An individual's residential status depends on physical stay duration in India during the relevant previous year and preceding years. Citizenship or place of birth does not determine residential status.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes individual residency criteria from corporate residency

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: Non-cash dividend payments to individuals not exceeding the threshold limit
Distributions to qualifying institutional insurers and notified IFSC units
inclusion: Actual dividend distributions
Amounts deemed as dividend under statutory provisions
descriptor.definition: The principal officer of a domestic company must deduct tax when distributing or paying dividends to resident shareholders. Specific small-value non-cash distributions to individuals and payouts to institutional insurers or specialized IFSC aircraft leasing units are exempt.
nearby_distinctions: Restricts tax withholding obligations exclusively to resident shareholders as opposed to foreign recipients.

path.name: Chapter 6: Income of Other Persons included in Assessee’s Total Income
INCOME OF OTHER PERSONS INCLUDIBLE IN TOTAL INCOME OF AN INDIVIDUAL
Remuneration from Concern with Substantial Interest

exclusion: remuneration solely attributable to the technical or professional knowledge and qualifications of the spouse
inclusion: salary, commission, or fees paid to spouse from a concern with individual's substantial interest
descriptor.definition: Spousal remuneration received in cash or kind from a concern in which the individual holds a substantial interest is clubbed with the individual's total income. A substantial interest exists if equity voting power or profit entitlement is at least twenty percent, though an exemption applies if the remuneration is solely due to the spouse's professional or technical qualifications.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from general asset transfers by focusing specifically on employment or service-based compensation derived from entities influenced by the taxpayer.

exclusion: Profits allocation based on unified business integration without market comparison
inclusion: Profits adjustment based on independent market conditions
Separate entity treatment for corporate group members
descriptor.definition: The arm's length principle evaluates transactions between associated enterprises by comparing them to conditions and prices that would be agreed upon between independent, unrelated parties. It treats related entities as separate, independent market participants for profit allocation purposes.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from consolidated group accounting by treating each affiliate as an independent unit.

path.name: LIMITATION OF INTEREST DEDUCTION IN CERTAIN CASES [SECTION 94B]
Limitation of Interest Deduction in Certain Cases

exclusion: Dividend payments on equity financing
inclusion: Interest expenses on debt borrowed from associated enterprises
Ceiling limits on interest deductions under business income
descriptor.definition: This provision restricts the deductibility of interest expenses claimed on borrowings from associated enterprises to curb profit shifting through excessive debt financing. It sets a ceiling limit on interest deductions in alignment with international base erosion countermeasures.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general transfer pricing pricing rules as it applies specifically to debt-to-equity capitalization structures and interest caps.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: rent paid to a business trust being a REIT in respect of directly owned real estate assets
inclusion: payments for land or buildings
rent for plant, machinery, equipment, furniture, or fittings
descriptor.definition: Entities responsible for paying rental income for the use of land, buildings, machinery, plant, equipment, furniture, or fittings to a resident must deduct tax at source. Real estate assets owned directly by a REIT are exempt from this deduction.
nearby_distinctions: Applies distinct tax rates for plant, machinery, and equipment rental compared to land, building, and furniture rental.

exclusion: Traditional face-to-face transactions conducted without computer or telecommunication network ordering methods
inclusion: Online shopping and retail
Online trading of goods and services
Electronic fund transfers and data exchanges
Subscription-based digital service streams
descriptor.definition: Electronic commerce denotes the supply of goods, services, or digital products over a digital or electronic network for economic value. Classification of a commercial transaction as e-commerce is determined strictly by the digital ordering method rather than the underlying product characteristics, participant types, or payment modes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from a standalone business type because e-commerce is merely a method of conducting business transactions containing the same substantive economic content as traditional trades.

path.name: EQUALISATION LEVY - CHAPTER VIII IN THE FINANCE ACT, 2016
Equalisation Levy - Chapter VIII in the Finance Act, 2016

exclusion: Transactions involving non-residents who maintain a taxable permanent establishment in India
Consumer-to-consumer or business-to-consumer transactions
inclusion: Online advertisement consideration exceeding aggregate thresholds
Specified services provided by non-residents without Indian permanent establishments
Business-to-business digital payments
descriptor.definition: Chapter VIII of the Finance Act, 2016 establishes a six percent equalisation levy on gross consideration for specified online advertisement and related services received by non-residents lacking a permanent establishment in India. This levy applies exclusively to business-to-business transactions involving resident payers or non-residents with an Indian permanent establishment, operating outside standard income tax treaty benefit frameworks.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard income tax because it is not characterized as income tax, thereby denying conventional double tax avoidance treaty foreign tax credits.

path.name: TAXATION OF BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING UNITS IN INDIA
Taxation Of Business Process Outsourcing Units In India

exclusion: independent resident service providers operating without business connections
inclusion: outsourced IT-enabled services creating a permanent establishment
profit attribution for separate enterprise operations
descriptor.definition: Foreign entities outsourcing IT-enabled services to resident Indian entities are taxed in India only if the resident unit constitutes a permanent establishment. Profits attributable to such a permanent establishment are determined as if it were a distinct and separate independent enterprise.
nearby_distinctions: distinguishes between independent outsourcing contractors and dependent agents acting as permanent establishments

path.name: Cost of Improvement for Intangible and Other Assets

exclusion: Goodwill of a business or profession
Intangible assets like trademarks or manufacturing rights
inclusion: Capital expenditures on additions to tangible capital assets after 1.4.2001
Capital outlays by previous owners where applicable under Section 73
descriptor.definition: The cost of improvement for goodwill and other specified intangible assets is taken as nil. For other capital assets, it includes capital expenditures incurred on additions or alterations by the previous owner or the assessee depending on the acquisition timeline and mode.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the cost of acquisition, which relates to the initial purchase price or value rather than subsequent capital additions.

path.name: FACILITY FOR ACCEPTING PAYMENT THROUGH PRESCRIBED ELECTRONIC MODES [SECTION 269SU]
Facility For Accepting Payment Through Prescribed Electronic Modes [Section 269Su]

exclusion: Assessees whose gross receipts do not exceed the 50 crore rupee threshold
Specified persons having exclusively B2B transactions with at least 95 percent non-cash receipts
inclusion: Businesses with gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees
RuPay debit card payment facilities
BHIM-UPI and BHIM-UPI QR code payment facilities
descriptor.definition: Businesses with total sales, turnover, or gross receipts exceeding 50 crore rupees in the preceding financial year must provide facilities for accepting payments through prescribed electronic modes. Non-compliance attracts a daily penalty under section 271DB, while system providers are prohibited from imposing charges for using these mandated modes.
nearby_distinctions: Mandates the provision of electronic payment acceptance facilities rather than restricting transaction modes like sections 269SS, 269ST, and 269T

path.name: Particulars to be furnished with return of income in case of an assessee engaged in business or profession [Section 139(6A)]
Particulars to be furnished with return of income in case of an assessee engaged in business or profession [Section 139(6A)]

exclusion: Non-business individual disclosures such as general personal bank accounts or credit cards
inclusion: Tax audit report referred to in section 44AB
Location and style of principal place of business and branches
Names and addresses of partners
Names of members and profit shares in an association of persons or body of individuals
descriptor.definition: Taxpayers engaged in any business or profession must submit specific commercial particulars with their return, including statutory audit reports and principal operational locations. Additionally, they must disclose names, addresses, and profit-sharing ratios of all partners or association members.
nearby_distinctions: Specifically targets commercial entities and professionals requiring structural disclosures like partnership details and audit reports, unlike general asset disclosures under section 139(6).

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
SPECIAL PROVISION FOR COMPUTATION OF COST OF ACQUISITION OF CERTAIN ASSETS [SECTION 40]
Special Provision For Computation Of Cost Of Acquisition Of Certain Assets [Section 40]

exclusion: Assets converted and revalued as capital assets falling under specific conversion rules
inclusion: Assets acquired via amalgamation, gift, will, irrevocable trust, or HUF partition sold as stock-in-trade
Addition of improvement costs and transfer-related expenditures
descriptor.definition: When assets acquired through specific arrangements like amalgamations, gifts, wills, trusts, or partition are sold as stock-in-trade, their acquisition cost equals the previous owner's cost plus improvement expenses. If such capital assets are converted into stock-in-trade after revaluation, alternative statutory conversion provisions apply instead.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct stock-in-trade transfers under amalgamation or gifts from general asset conversions subject to revaluation rules.

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS IN RESPECT OF SLUMP SALE [SECTION 77]
Capital Gains in Respect of Slump Sale

exclusion: Transfer of individual assets or liabilities not constituting an active business undertaking
inclusion: Transfer of an entire undertaking, division, or business activity for a lump sum
Assets held for more than 36 months taxed as long-term and 36 months or less as short-term
descriptor.definition: A slump sale involves transferring one or more undertakings for a lump sum consideration without assigning values to individual assets and liabilities. The net worth of the undertaking is deemed the cost of acquisition and improvement, while the fair market value serves as the full value of consideration.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from itemized asset sales because individual asset valuation is absent, utilizing undertaking net worth instead.

path.name: POWER OF ASSESSING OFFICER TO MAKE A REFERENCE TO THE VALUATION OFFICER [SECTION 142A]
Power Of Assessing Officer To Make A Reference To The Valuation Officer [Section 142A]

exclusion: References made without affording an opportunity of being heard before final assessment integration
inclusion: Reference for estimating fair market value of assets, properties, or investments
Best judgment estimation upon non-cooperation
descriptor.definition: The Assessing Officer can reference a Valuation Officer to estimate the fair market value or value of any asset, property, or investment for assessment purposes. The Valuation Officer must submit the report within six months, and the Assessing Officer utilizes it after granting the assessee a hearing opportunity.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from special audits under section 142(2A) as it focuses strictly on estimating asset, property, or investment values through a specialized Valuation Officer rather than financial account auditing.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Payment of tax and defaults by the assessee [Section 220]
Payment of tax and defaults by the assessee [Section 220]

exclusion: Penalty levy mechanisms
Recovery proceedings through TRO
inclusion: Demand payments within thirty days
Interest on unpaid dues
Reduction or increase of interest resulting from rectification or appellate orders
descriptor.definition: Amounts specified in a notice of demand must be paid within thirty days of service, though the Assessing Officer may extend time, permit installments, or shorten the period if revenue is endangered. Failure to pay within this period triggers simple interest liability for every month or part of a month of default.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from Section 221 penalties as it deals strictly with statutory payment timelines and compounding interest rather than penal impositions for defaults.

exclusion: Original receipts that never received prior expense or loss write-off deductions
inclusion: Subsequent cash receipts compensating for prior allowed losses or expenditures
Benefits derived from previously written-off trading liabilities
descriptor.definition: Recoveries or benefits derived from previously allowed deductions for losses, expenditures, or trading liabilities are treated as taxable income. This deemed income is taxable in the financial year in which the amount is received or the benefit accrues.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary income generation events from secondary recoveries of previously claimed expense deductions.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: income of the nature of capital gains
aggregate income not exceeding the threshold limit in a financial year
inclusion: income distributed on mutual fund units
units from administrators of specified undertakings or specified companies
descriptor.definition: Payers distributing income in respect of mutual fund units or specified undertakings must deduct tax at source. Capital gains distributions and amounts below the financial year threshold are exempt from this deduction.
nearby_distinctions: Excludes capital gains components, focusing strictly on income distributions from specified mutual fund and corporate units.

(ii) M/s RH Steels Ltd. is a company incorporated in India. It sets up two 
units, one in a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and another in non-SEZ 
area for manufacturing of steel bottles. The company transfers the 
product of non-SEZ unit to SEZ unit at a price lower than the fair 
36 
SUGGESTED ANSWER 
DIRECT TAX LAWS & INTERNATIONAL TAXATION 
market value. In respect of such products transferred from non-SEZ 
unit, only insignificant manufacturing activity takes place in the SEZ 
unit. In this way, the company is able to show higher profits in SEZ unit 
than in non-SEZ unit, and consequently claims higher deduction in 
computation of income. The sales from bottles transferred from non-
SEZ unit constitute 15% of the total turnover of SEZ unit. Can 
provisions of GAAR be invoked?  
(4 Marks)

(a) (i) Mr. Ram is engaged in trading of mobiles and is the proprietor of 6 
M/s. Narang Mobiles. His turnover and aggregate receipts for the 
financial year 2024-25 are ` 5,12,00,000. He received ` 22,00,000 from 
sundry debtors in cash and remaining ` 4.90 crores were received 
through online banking channel before 31.03.2025. He also made a 
total business payment of ` 5,50,00,000 against purchase of goods, 
rent; salary and other business expenses during the previous year 
2024-25, out of which total cash payments amounted to ` 28,00,000 
and remaining all kind of payments made through online banking 
channel. No other amount received or paid during the year on business 
account. He has no other business in his name. 
Whether Mr. Ram is required to get books of accounts of Narang 
Mobiles compulsory audited for the A.Y. 2025-26 as per section 44AB of 
the Income-tax Act, 1961? Discuss. 
Assuming Mr. Ram is required to get his accounts audited and in the 
light of the Tax Audit applicability u/s 44AB of the Act, Also discuss 
whether the following issue need to be reported by the Chartered 
Accountant of Mr. Ram in the tax audit report as applicable for  
A.Y. 2025-26 u/s 44AB in relation to Tax audit of M/s. Narang' Mobiles 
in view of section 269ST. You need to give the relevant provisions of law 
in support of your answer. 
Narang Mobiles issued an invoice of ` 3,50,000 to M/s. XYZ and Co. for 
sale of mobiles on 10.02.2025. M/s. XYZ and Co. made payment of  
` 2,50,000 through account payee cheque. The balance of ` 1,00,000 
has been paid on 10 different dates in cash, through payment of  
` 10,000 on each day before 31.03.2025. 
Ignore the Clause numbers given in Form 3CD prescribed for Tax Audit 
Report u/s 44AB for such reporting.   
(6 Marks)

parts.question_text:
(b) ABC Ltd., an Indian company has entered into an agreement for providing 
technical knowhow with PQR Inc., a company registered in Country A. PQR 
Inc. has a sister concern, XYZ LLC., in Country A, which has obtained 
Advance Ruling on an identical technical know-how agreement with 
another Indian company, MNC Ltd.  
The agreement is expected to be of ` 500 crores and expected tax liability 
would be ` 150 crores. ABC Ltd. wants to make use of this advance ruling 
for its assessment proceedings. So, it applied to Board for Advance Rulings 
to issue same ruling for ABC Limited, being identical ruling. To verify the 
transaction between ABC Ltd and PQR Inc., the Board for Advance Rulings 
compel the production of books of accounts. 
Can ABC Ltd make an application for advance ruling with Board for 
Advance Rulings as per the Act. Also Examine whether the Board can ask for 
production of books of accounts when ruling on similar issue has already 
been given. Examine in the context of the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 
1961?  
(4 Marks)

parts.answer_text:
(ii) M/s RH Steels Ltd. has tried to take advantage of tax provisions by 
diverting profits from non-SEZ unit to SEZ unit. This is not the 
intention of the SEZ legislation.  
However, such tax avoidance is specifically dealt with through the 
provisions contained in section 10AA(9), as per which provisions of 
section 80-IA(8) would get attracted in such a case.  
Further, if the aggregate of such transactions entered into in the 
relevant previous year exceed the threshold of ` 20 crore, domestic 
transfer pricing regulations under section 92BA would be attracted.  
38 
SUGGESTED ANSWER 
DIRECT TAX LAWS & INTERNATIONAL TAXATION 
Thus, in this case, due to application of specific anti-avoidance 
provisions, no tax benefit can be derived by M/ RH Steels Ltd. by 
transferring the products from non-SEZ unit to SEZ unit at less than 
fair market value.  
Hence, the Revenue need not invoke GAAR in such a case, though GAAR 
and SAAR can co-exist as per clarification given in the CBDT Circular.

(a) (i) As per section 44AB, every person carrying on business or profession 
is required to get his accounts audited before the “specified date” by 
a Chartered Accountant, if the total sales, turnover or gross receipts 
in business exceeds ` 1 crore in any previous year.  
However, tax audit is not required in case of such person carrying on 
business whose total sales, turnover or gross receipts in business  
≤ ` 10 crore in the relevant previous year (P.Y.), if - 
- 
aggregate cash receipts including amount received for sales, 
turnover, gross receipts in the relevant previous year ≤ 5% of 
such receipts; and  
37 
SUGGESTED ANSWER 
FINAL EXAMINATION: MAY 2025 
- 
aggregate cash payments including amount incurred for 
expenditure in the relevant P.Y. ≤ 5% of such payments  
In this case, the percentage of cash receipts of ` 22 lakhs to 
aggregate receipts of ` 5.12 crore is 4.30% and the percentage of 
cash payments of ` 28 lakhs to aggregate payments of ` 5.50 crore is 
5.09%. 
Since the cash payments made during the year exceed 5% of 
aggregate payments, the M/s Narang Mobiles is required to get its 
accounts audited under section 44AB and furnish audit report before 
the specified date, irrespective of the fact that its turnover does not 
exceed ` 10 crores and its cash receipts do not exceed 5% of total 
receipts. 
Further, particulars of each receipt in an amount exceeding the limit 
speciﬁed in section 269ST i.e., ` 2 lakhs, in aggregate from a person in 
a day or in respect of a single transaction or in respect of transactions 
relating to one event or occasion from a person, during the previous 
year, where such receipt is otherwise than by a cheque or bank draft 
or use of electronic clearing system through a bank account is to be 
reported in Form 3CD.  
In this case, M/s XYZ made payment of ` 2.5 lakhs by account payee 
cheque and the balance of ` 1 lakh in cash in aggregate during the P.Y. 
2024-25 to M/s Narang Mobile. Since the amount received in cash by 
M/s Narang Mobiles is less than ` 2 lakhs and the transaction is not 
covered u/s 269ST, there is no need to report this transaction in the tax 
audit report of M/s Narang Mobiles by his Chartered Accountant.

(b) A resident can make an application for advance ruling in relation to his tax 
liability arising out of one or more transactions valuing ` 100 crore or 
more in total which has been undertaken or is proposed to be 
undertaken. 
Since the value of transactions between M/s ABC Ltd and M/s PQR Inc for 
providing technical knowhow exceeds ` 100 crores, ABC Ltd. can make an 
application for advance ruling with the Board for Advance Rulings. 
As per section 245U, the Board for Advance Rulings shall have all the 
powers of the Civil Court in respect of discovery and inspection, enforcing 
the attendance of any person, including any officer of a banking company 
and examining on oath, issuing commissions and compelling the 
production of books of accounts and other documents. 
Accordingly, the Board can ask for the production of books of accounts 
before passing advance ruling for ABC Ltd.   
39

path.name: BOARDS FOR ADVANCE RULINGS – AN INTRODUCTION
